units.la: Respondeo, Ista Dei opera ad extra, cō munia esse tribus Personis, Patris, Filij & Spiritus sancti. Ideo Christus eodē cap. uersu 27, Sese cui uoluerit Patrem retegere, testatur. Et Ioan.16.13. dicit: Cum autē uenerit ille Spiritus ueritatis, deducet uos in omnem ueritatem. non enim loquetur à semetipso, sed quæcunq; audie-rit, loquetur; & quæ uentura sunt, renun-ciabit ciabit vobis. Alloquitur itaq; nos Deus, sed per Sapientiam coaeternam seu Filium, & quidem afflatu Spiritus sancti, qui est substantialis virtus, amor & laeticia coaeterna Patris & Filij.
units.tr: I answer: these works of God outward are common to the three Persons: Father, Son and Holy Spirit. For this reason Christ in the same chapter, verse 27, testifies that he reveals the Father to whomever he wills. And John 16.13 says: "Howbeit when he, the Spirit of truth, is come, he will guide you into all truth: for he shall not speak of himself; but whatsoever he shall hear, that shall he speak: and he will shew you things to come." Therefore God speaks to us, but through the co-eternal Wisdom, that is, the Son, and indeed by the breath of the Holy Spirit, who is the substantial power, love and co-eternal joy of the Father and the Son.

units.la: Constituta hac thesi, Oraculorum propheticorum & apostolicorum auctor est Deus: res ipsa docet, quàm sint μωρὰ ῥητά[?], quas in Oeconomia sua Biblica mouit Georgius Ederus I.C. An necessaria sit de fide doctrina aliqua? An certa sit Scriptura sancta? An ne scripta sint, quae oportuit, omnia? Ad quam partem Philosophiae sacra scriptura referri debeat, aut possit? Item quae de auctoritate & obscuritate, in scyrpo nodum investigans, illa mouet.
units.tr: This thesis being established, God is the author of the prophetic and apostolic oracles. The matter itself shows how foolish are the questions which Georg Eder, licentiate in law, raised in his Biblical Economy: whether any doctrine is necessary for faith; whether Holy Scripture is certain; whether all things that ought to have been written were indeed written; to which part of philosophy holy Scripture ought or can be referred; and likewise the questions about its authority and obscurity, which he raised while investigating a knot in a bulrush.

units.la: Cum enim Deus sit sapientissimus, veracissimus, optimus, perfectissimus: quis pius dubitet, necessariam scitu doctrinam ab eo nobis praescriptam esse, & eandem certissimam, salubberrimam, perfectissimam censeri debere? Iam vero, num o-ptimus & sentiendi & dicendi artifex ita obscure suam nobis voluntatem tra-didit, ut vix à paucis intel-ligi possit?
units.tr: For since God is most wise, most true, most good and most perfect, what pious person could doubt that he has prescribed to us a doctrine necessary to know, and that this must be judged most certain, most wholesome and most perfect? Indeed, has that best craftsman of both thinking and speaking so obscurely handed down his will to us that it can scarcely be understood by a few?

units.la: Succenturiati prædones oraculorum Dei, & æternæ illius καὶ ὑφιστάμενος[?] Sapi-entiæ cooperarij sunt, utriusq; Testamé-ti fideles ministri.
units.tr: The sly robbers who are added to the oracles of God, and co-workers of that eternal and subsisting Wisdom, are faithful ministers of both Testaments.

units.la: Quæ sunt horum propria? Respondeo: Principem pastorum Christum ἐν προαιρέσεως[?] sequi; optima fide mandato munere fungi: omnibus omnia fieri, ut omnino aliquos lucrifaciant & seruent.
units.tr: What are the proper duties of these men? I answer: to follow Christ, the chief of shepherds, by deliberate choice [ἐν προαιρέσεως]; to discharge the commission entrusted to them with the best faith; to become all things to all men, so that they may by all means win and save some.

units.la: 1. Christum sequi oportet primùm fide, deinde uita. Matt.4.19. Ioan.21.19. Fide, quæ ἐπιγνώσεως[?] τῆς ἀληθείας definitur, Christum sequuntur, qui operum fidei; legi nihil de suo addut, nihil ex ea auferunt. Deut.12.32. Vita, quæ fide per charitatem efficaci constat, Christum sequuntur, qui accipiunt crucem suam, abnegant semetipsos, ac Christi, quem sequuntur, gratia animas suas perdunt, &c. Matt.16.24.25.
units.tr: 1. We ought to follow Christ first by faith and then by life (Matt. 4.19; John 21.19). By faith, which is defined as "knowledge of the truth" [ἐπίγνωσις τῆς ἀληθείας], those follow Christ who add nothing of their own to the works of faith and take nothing away from the law (Deut. 12.32). By life, which consists in faith working through love, those follow Christ who take up their cross, deny themselves, and for the sake of the grace of Christ, whom they follow, lose their souls (Matt. 16.24, 25).

units.la: 2. Ἐκ προαιρέσεως autem Christum nos sequi debere, Paulus suo exemplo ostendit: Nam, dicens, si uolens hoc faciam, mercedem habeo: sin inuitus, dispensa-tio credita est mihi. 1.Cor.9.17.
units.tr: 2. That we ought to follow Christ by free choice [ἐκ προαιρέσεως], Paul shows by his own example: "For if I do this thing willingly, I have a reward: but if against my will, a dispensation of the gospel is committed unto me" (1 Cor. 9.17).

units.la: 3. Optimam autem fidem requiri in dispensatoribus, hæc dicta monent. Qui fi-delis[?] delis est in paucisimis,etiä in multis fidelis est,&c. Luc.16.10. Item: Quod superest aute, illud requiritur in dispensatori-bus,ut fidus quisq; reperiatur. 1.Cor.4.2.
units.tr: 3. That the best faith is required in stewards, these sayings admonish: "He that is faithful in that which is least is faithful also in much" (Luke 16.10). Likewise: "Moreover it is required in stewards that a man be found faithful" (1 Cor. 4.2).

units.la: 4. Omnibus omnia fieri oportere,ut aliquos Christo adducant, docuit Paulus suo exemplo, 1. Cor. 9. 20. Cætera quæ de proprijs & adiunctis Ecclesiæ ministrorum dici poterant,ex ijs locis,in quibus ex professo illa tractantur,petenda sunt,1.Tim.3.&Tit.1.multisq; alijs locis.
units.tr: 4. Paul taught by his own example that all things must be made to all men, so that they may bring some to Christ (1 Cor. 9.20). The other things which could be said about the properties and attributes of the ministers of the Church should be sought from those passages in which these matters are treated expressly: 1 Tim. 3, Titus 1, and many other places.

units.la: Iam, si ἀντιλήψιν[?] paucis instituas[?],grauis-simè peccant, qui nec uita, nec doctrina Christum sequuntur: aut innocentis uitæ & sinceræ doctrinæ diuortium introducunt. Deinde, qui inuiti ministerio funguntur: illud neglecturi, si rei familiari non seruiat. Tertiò,qui mala fide agunt, doctrinam adulterantes. Quartò,qui religionem quæstui seruire uolunt: uentri, gloriæ,auctoritati potius suæ,quàm Christo,seruientes.
units.tr: Now, if you were to set up a contrast among a few, those sin most gravely who follow Christ neither in life nor in doctrine, or who introduce a divorce between innocent life and sincere doctrine. Next, those who take up the ministry unwillingly, who will neglect it if it does not serve their domestic affairs. Third, those who act in bad faith, corrupting doctrine. Fourth, those who want religion to serve their gain, serving their belly, their glory, and their own authority rather than Christ.

units.la: Cum itaq; inculpatos seruos,oraculorum suorum præconio Deus fungi uelit, quanti ipsa quoq; nobis facienda sint,nō est obscurum. Scitè Basilius in Hexam. Euangelij præcones,Christi labra appel-lauit. lauit. Dent igitur ministri uerbi operam, ne Christo indigna proloquantur: sed,ut Pauli uerbis utar,ἀ πρέπει τῇ ὑγιαινούσῃ διδα- σκαλίᾳ[?], quæ decent fanâ doctrinâ. Tit.2.1.
units.tr: Since, therefore, God wishes blameless servants to discharge the proclamation of his oracles, how greatly these men themselves must be made is not obscure. Basil wisely called the preachers of the gospel "the lips of Christ" (Hexaemeron). Let ministers of the Word therefore take care that they do not speak what is unworthy of Christ, but, to use the words of Paul, what befits sound doctrine [ἃ πρέπει τῇ ὑγιαινούσῃ διδασκαλίᾳ] (Titus 2.1).

units.la: DE FORMA.
units.tr: CONCERNING THE FORM.

units.la: Formam Propheta expressit nomine Dabar, quod Paulus noster uocauit τὸ ῥῆμα τῆς ἀκοῆς ὑμῶν[?], Rom.10.16. ῥῆμα θεοῦ, uerbum Dei,v.17.eiusdem cap. ῥῆμα τῆς πίστεως[?], eodem cap.8.uersu. Sermone crucis, qui ijs quidem qui pereūt,stultitia est: nobis autem qui feruamur,potetia Dei. 1.Cor.1.v.18.
units.tr: The Prophet expresses the form by the word Dabar, which Paul our teacher called "the word of your hearing" [τὸ ῥῆμα τῆς ἀκοῆς ὑμῶν], Rom. 10.16; "the word of God" [ῥῆμα θεοῦ], "the word of God," v. 17 of the same chapter; "the word of faith" [ῥῆμα τῆς πίστεως], in the eighth verse of the same chapter; and "the word of the cross," which to those who perish is foolishness, but to us who are being saved is the power of God, 1 Cor. 1.18.

units.la: Vocatur autè primùm ἀκοὴ ὑμῶν[?], quòd ministrorum uox, audientium aureis feriat ἐξωθεῖ[?]. Σύζυγα[?] sint uox ministri,& uox Spiritus sancti. Illa auribus excipitur,hæc corde per fidem purificato. deinde, ῥῆμα θεοῦ, ab efficiente principali, Patre illo luminum & fonte sapientiæ. tertiò, ῥῆμα Χριστοῦ, à correlatiuo pariter & instrumento, quod & uerbo assentiendo respodet, & res inuisibiles uerbo annunciatas apprehendit & applicat: quod fidem uocamus. postremò,ut alia omittamus,uocatur sermo de cruce, quòd non nisi Iesum Christum, eumq; crucifixum,annunciet.
units.tr: It is called first "your hearing" [ἀκοὴ ὑμῶν], because the voice of the ministers strikes the ears of the hearers. The voice of the minister and the voice of the Holy Spirit are yoked together [Σύζυγα]: the former is received by the ears, the latter by the heart purified through faith. Second, it is called "the word of God" [ῥῆμα θεοῦ], from its principal efficient cause, the Father of lights and the fountain of wisdom. Third, it is called "the word of Christ" [ῥῆμα Χριστοῦ], from its correlative and instrument, which both responds to the word by assenting and grasps and applies the invisible things announced in the word; this we call faith. Last, to omit other names, it is called "the word of the cross," because it announces nothing but Jesus Christ, and him crucified.

units.la: Ex his quæ iam συλλογισμοῦ[?] solùm licuit, colligere campo sita. Aturia similis est iis locis, quae circa Arbela sunt, & Lycum fluuiu intermedium habet. Arbela enim ad Babylo niam pertinent, & iuxta eam sunt. Trans Lycum uero Aturię campi, Ninum circumiacent. Moses ab Assure Niniuen conditā docet, Gen.10.11. Assur egressus aedificauit Niniueh, & Rehoboth ciuitatem, &c. Significat Niniue domum Nini, aut simpliciter habitationem: ut alicubi docuit Melanchthon. De magnitudine urbis, uersiculus quem in manibus habemus, monet: Surge, & uade in Niniueh ciuitatem magnam. Quam eadem munita fuerit, inde liquet, quod cum areae urbis ambitus haberet 400 stadia, 1500 turres habuisse dicitur. Moenia fuerunt altitudinis 100 cubitorum. Latitudo tanta erat, ut terris plaustris peruia essent.
units.tr: From these things, which I have been able to gather only by way of inference, the field lies open. Assyria is like the places around Arbela, and has the Lycus river lying between. For Arbela belongs to Babylon and lies near it. Beyond the Lycus, however, are the plains of Assyria, and Nineveh lies around them. Moses teaches that Nineveh was founded by Asshur, Gen. 10.11: "Out of that land went forth Asshur, and built Nineveh, and the city Rehoboth," etc. Nineveh signifies the house of Ninus, or simply a dwelling place, as Melanchthon taught somewhere. Concerning the size of the city, the little verse we have in hand gives warning: "Arise, and go to Nineveh, that great city," Jonah 1.2. How well it was fortified is clear from this: though the circuit of the city's area was 400 stadia, it is said to have had 1,500 towers. The walls were 100 cubits high. Its breadth was so great that chariots could travel on them side by side.

units.la: Discimus autem hoc loco, primùm Deum non sic passum esse praeteritis aetatibus Gentes suis ipsarum viis ambulare, (Act.14.16.) ut non quibusdam voluntatem suam non solùm e libro naturae, id est e Dei opificio, sed etiam sermonum suorum praeconio, innotescere uellet. Secundò, eo facto demonstratum, quòd non solùm Iudæorum, uerumetiam Gentium De-us esset. Tertiò, cum non omnibus Gentibus dederit Dominus doctores & donum poenitentiae, testatum fecit, se & nemini quicquam debere (nisi si cui sponte debitorem pollicedo sese constituit) & sese esse liberrimum agens.
units.tr: Here we learn, first, that God did not so allow the Gentiles in past ages to walk in their own ways (Acts 14.16) that he did not wish to make his will known to some, not only from the book of nature, that is, from God's workmanship, but also through the proclamation of his own words. Second, by this act it was shown that he is the God not only of the Jews but also of the Gentiles. Third, since the Lord has not given teachers and the gift of repentance to all the Gentiles, he has made it witnessed that he owes nothing to anyone (unless he has freely bound himself as a debtor by promise), and that he acts as most free.

units.la: Vt igitur de pluuia terram cœlitùs ri-gante dicitur, Amos 4.7: Sed & ego prohibui à uobis imbrem, cùm adhuc essent tres menses usq; ad messem: & pluere feci super ciuitatem unam, & super alteram non[?] feci pluere: fundus unus complutus fuit, fundus autem super quem non pluit, aruit. ita de uerbi diuini prædicatione sincera dicitur, eam per gratiam aliis quidem concedi, aliis autem denegari.
units.tr: Just as it is said of rain that God causes it to fall upon the earth from heaven, Amos 4.7: "I also withheld the rain from you, when there were yet three months to the harvest; and I caused it to rain upon one city, and caused it not to rain upon another; one field was rained upon, and the field whereupon it rained not withered." So it is said of the sincere preaching of the divine word that by grace it is granted to some but denied to others.

units.la: 3. Quid hunc ad Niniuen legatum agere oportuit? Clamare contra eam. Quid autem hoc fit, docuit Iesaias cap.58.1. Cla-ma gutture, ne prohibeas clamorem: tam quam tuba exalta uocem tuam, & annuncia populo meo prævaricationem suam, & domui Iacob peccatum suum. Clamare igitur contra Niniuen, nihil aliud erat, quàm eam peccatorum ream agere.
units.tr: 3. What was it fitting for this envoy to do to Nineveh? To cry out against her. Isaiah taught what this is, ch. 58.1: "Cry aloud, spare not; lift up thy voice like a trumpet, and show my people their transgression, and the house of Jacob their sins." To cry out against Nineveh, therefore, was nothing other than to bring her to trial as guilty of sins.

units.la: Existimo autem Ioannem Baptistam eo nomine φωνὴν βοῶντος, uocem clamantis est se dictum, Isa. 40.3. Matt. 3.3. quòd ut conuerteret corda filiorum ad parentes, poenitentiam praedicauit. Vt autē fidi speculatores domus Domini, & uigilantes pastores gregis Dominici, hostes & lupos ingruentes uoce sua de periculis impendentibus commonefaciunt: ita econ-trà speculatores caeci nihil norūt: uniuer-si enim ipsi canes muti sunt, qui non ualent latrare, dormitantes, iacentes, diligētes dormitare. Isa. 56.10.
units.tr: I think John the Baptist was called "the voice of one crying" [φωνὴν βοῶντος] for this reason, Isa. 40.3, Matt. 3.3: because he preached repentance in order to turn the hearts of the children to their fathers. And just as faithful watchmen of the Lord's house and vigilant ministers of the Lord's flock warn by their voice of dangers hanging over them, when enemies and wolves attack, so on the contrary blind watchmen know nothing; they are all mute dogs who cannot bark, lying asleep, loving to slumber, Isa. 56.10.

units.la: Ex hac autem φράσει[?], Clamare contra aliquem, liquet, non mirum uideri nobis debere, quòd ueritatis oratio, quae peccata exprobrans, hypocriseos fucum detegit, ingratos mundo Dei seruos efficiat, secundum illud Pauli: Enimuerò si ad-huc hominibus placerem, Christi seruus non essem. Gal. 1.10.
units.tr: From this figure of speech, "to cry out against someone," it is plain that it ought not seem strange to us that the speech of truth, which rebukes sins and exposes the disguise of hypocrisy, makes God's servants unwelcome to the world, according to Paul's saying: "For if I still pleased men, I should not be the servant of Christ," Gal. 1.10.

units.la: 4. Quid eundem Dei nomine testari oporteat? Niniuitarum maliciam ascen-disse in conspectum Iehouae. Syllogismores in hunc modū demonstrabitur: Quo-rum malicia ascendit in conspectum Iehouę, aduersus eos clamandum est seruo Domini. Atqui Niniuitarū malicia ascendit in conspectum Domini. Ergo, &c. Hic observabimus ordine:
units.tr: 4. What it is fitting to bear witness to in the name of God: that the wickedness of the Ninevites has come up before the face of Jehovah. The syllogism may be set out in this way: Whose wickedness comes up before the face of Jehovah, against them the servant of the Lord must cry out. But the wickedness of the Ninevites has come up before the face of the Lord. Therefore, etc. Here we shall observe in order:

units.la: 1. αἰτιολογίαν[?]. Non fit injuria peccatoribus, quando nomine Dei accusantur. Immò Dominus atroce injuria afficitur, cū ad scelera hominum Ecclesiae ministri conniuent: & ut illorum gratiam demereantur, Deum offendi non curant.
units.tr: 1. The reason [αἰτιολογίαν]. No injustice is done to sinners when they are accused in the name of God. Rather, the Lord is grievously wronged when the ministers of the Church connive at men's crimes, and, in order to win the favour of the wicked, take no care to avoid offending God.

units.la: 2. αὔξησιν[?], quę ducitur primùm à specie, videlicet malitia: deinde, à violento motu: neq; enim inter homines humi repere, sed in altū assurgere dicitur, quòd non tantùm in homines & terram, sed etiam in cœlum peccarent Niniuitæ. postremò, à persona Dei, in quem multipliciter deliquerant. Fateor tamen, me non scrupulosè discernere peccatum in cœlum & in Deum: ut etiā D. Beza monet, Luc.15.18.
units.tr: 2. An amplification [αὔξησιν], which is drawn first from the kind of sin, namely wickedness; then from the violent movement, for the Ninevites are said not to creep upon the ground among men, but to rise high, since they sinned not only against men and the earth but also against heaven. Last, from the person of God, against whom they had offended in many ways. I confess, however, that I do not scrupulously distinguish between sin against heaven and sin against God, as Dr. Beza also points out, Luke 15.18.

units.la: 3. Malitiæ vocabulum quid Latinis significet, hęc Ciceronis dicta ostendunt: Malitia est versuta & fallax nocendi ratio. Item: Virtuti contraria est vitiositas. sic enim malo, quàm malitiam appellare, quam Græci κακίαν[?] vocant. nam malitia certi cuiusdam vitij nomen est. Idem: Prudentiam, ait, malitia imitatur. Hoc postremum Ciceronis dictum ideo adscripsi, quia nonnihil facit ad intelligendum Pauli Apostoli dictum, 1.Cor.14.20. Fratres, ne estote pueri intelligentia: sed malitia pueri, intelligentia vero adulti estote. Interdum tamen κακίαν ἀντὶ τῆς κα-κώσεως[?] fumi, ex illo Christi dicto liquet: Sufficit diei sua uexatio, ἡ κακία[?]. Matt.6. 34. Existimo tamen, malitiam in uerbis Ionae uniuersaliter sumtam pro impietate & iniusticia, id est, de horrenda & multiplici transgressione primae & secundae tabulae Decalogi.
units.tr: 3. What the word malice [malitia] signifies in Latin, these sayings of Cicero show: "Malice is a crafty and deceitful plan for harming." Likewise: "Vice is contrary to virtue." For I prefer to call it "vice" [vitiositas] rather than "malice," which the Greeks call κακίαν [kakian]; for malice is the name of a certain particular vice. Again, Cicero: "Malice," he says, "imitates prudence." I have added this last saying of Cicero because it does something to help in understanding the saying of the apostle Paul, 1 Cor. 14.20: "Brethren, be not children in understanding, but in malice be children, yet in understanding be men." Nevertheless, it is clear from that saying of Christ, "Sufficient unto the day is the evil thereof" [ἡ κακία], Matt. 6.34, that sometimes κακίαν is used for affliction [κακώσεως]. I think, however, that malice in the words of Jonah, taken universally, means impiety and injustice, that is, the horrible and manifold transgression of the first and second tables of the Decalogue.

units.la: 4. Malitia cur coram Domino ascendere dicatur. Nubi ascendenti confertur peccatu, Isa.44.22. Deleui ut nubem praeuaricationes tuas, & ueluti nubem peccata tua: redi igitur ad me, quia redemi te. Vt enim densa & caliginosa nubes, Solis fulgorem nobis eripiens, tenebras inducit: ita quoque peccata intermedia obstant, ne serenam Dei faciem aspicere peccatores queant, neue lucis diuinae radijs eorum corda illustrentur.
units.tr: 4. Why malice is said to ascend before the Lord. Sin is compared to a rising cloud, Isa. 44.22: "I have blotted out, as a thick cloud, thy transgressions, and as a cloud, thy sins: return unto me, for I have redeemed thee." For just as a dense and misty cloud, snatching the brightness of the sun from us, brings darkness, so sins that come between hinder sinners from being able to look upon the serene face of God, and keep their hearts from being illumined by the rays of the divine light.

units.la: ¶ Iam uero ut ad θεὸν[?] progrediamur, duae nobis occurrunt: altera de uocatione, altera de poenitentia.
units.tr: ¶ Now, to advance to God [θεὸν], two matters present themselves to us: one concerning vocation, the other concerning repentance.

units.la: I. DEI SOLIVS EST, SVVM cuiq; officij gradum praestituere.
units.tr: I. IT BELONGS TO GOD ALONE TO ASSIGN EACH PERSON HIS OWN RANK OF DUTY.

units.la: Ita rem habere, hæ grauissimæ rationes ostendunt.
units.tr: That this is so, the following most weighty reasons show.

units.la: 1. A' creationis iure. Qui sua solius causa, omnia & condidit & conseruat, donec eiusum est, eius est suam cuiq; stationé assignare, in qua consilio Dei seruiat: ut de Dauide dicitur, Actor. 13. 36. Atqui Deus uniuersa operatus est propter semetipsum: Prouerb. 16. 4. Eius ergo solius est, suam cuiq; functioné praescribere.
units.tr: 1. From the right of creation. He who made and preserves all things solely for his own sake, and for as long as they are his, has the right to assign each thing its own station, in which it serves the counsel of God, as is said of David, Acts 13:36. But God has worked all things for himself, Prov. 16:4. Therefore it belongs to him alone to prescribe to each person his own function.

units.la: 2. A' sapientiæ & bonitatis Dei confide ratione. Quicunq; summe sapiés & summe bonus est, is omnium optime & gradus functionum, & personas & necessaria χαρίσματα [?] dispensare potest. Deus autem talis est. Quare illi relinquenda est plena potestas suam cuiq; prouinciam assignandi.
units.tr: 2. From the confidence we have in the wisdom and goodness of God. Whoever is supremely wise and supremely good is able to distribute the ranks of functions, the persons, and the necessary gifts [χαρίσματα] in the best possible way. God is such a being. Therefore full power to assign each person his own sphere must be left to him.

units.la: 3. A' redemtionis iure. Ordo iusticiæ postulat, ut quod Redemtor ministeriū à se redemtis delegauit, eodem ipsos fungi, & quidé summa fide, æquum sit. Sed Redemtor ille noster Iesus Christus alios dedit Apostolos, alios uero Prophetas, alios autem Euangelistas,alios uerò Doctores & Pastores, &c. Eph.4.11. Idem iudicium est & de caeteris diuinae τῆς ἀν-τάξεως[?] gradibus. Itaq; sua cuiq; uocatio studiose ornanda, & in ea permanendū est. 1.Cor.7.24.
units.tr: 3. From the right of redemption. The order of justice requires that those whom the Redeemer has redeemed should perform, and with the utmost faithfulness, the ministry he has entrusted to them; this is only fair. But that Redeemer of ours, Jesus Christ, gave some to be apostles, others prophets, others evangelists, and others teachers and pastors, etc., Eph. 4:11. The same judgment holds for the other grades of the divine order [τάξεως]. Therefore each person's calling is to be diligently adorned, and in it one must remain, 1 Cor. 7:24.

units.la: Vt sua cuiq; patria probari debet:nam, ut ille ait, ἄλλος μὲν πρὸς ἄλλην πόλιν τετα-γμένος[?]: ita cuiq; placere debet etiam humilis functio, modò fit diuinitus deman data,feruiatq; gloriae Dei.
units.tr: Just as each person's homeland ought to be esteemed, for, as one author says, "one man is set in one city, another in another" [ἄλλος μὲν πρὸς ἄλλην πόλιν τεταγμένος]: so too each person ought to be content even with a humble function, provided it has been assigned by God and serves the glory of God.

units.la: Ex hac doctrina eximiae cofolationis fructus ad nos redit. Etenim cum nemo pius fit, qui ignorantiae & infirmitatis suae sensu non pungatur & afficiatur, statim ubi Deum uocantem & idoneos efficie-tem respicimus, opus nostrum in Domi-no nequaquam inane futurum colligi-mus:& recte precamur,
units.tr: From this doctrine comes back to us the fruit of a most excellent consolation. For since no one is pious who is not pricked and afflicted by a sense of his own ignorance and weakness, as soon as we look to God calling us and making us fit for the task, we conclude that our work in the Lord will by no means be in vain, and we rightly pray:

units.la: Da nescia frangi Pectora, da uires animis tua dona profesis.
units.tr: Grant that my unknowing breast not be broken; grant strength to our minds, you who bestow your gifts.

units.la: Colligimus etiam, quàm grauiter illi peccent, qui non contenti suae uocatio-nis limitibus, πολυπραγμονεῖν & ἀλλοτρ[illegible, ~10 letters] agere malunt. Vult enim Deus nos cotendere, ut quieti fimus,& res no-stras agamus, iuxta canone:Καὶ φιλοτιμεῖ-
units.tr: We also conclude how gravely they sin who, not content with the limits of their own calling, prefer to be busybodies and to meddle in other people's affairs. For God wants us to strive to be quiet, to mind our own business, according to the rule: "And make it your ambition ..."

units.la: Φιλοτιμεῖσθαι[?] ἡσυχάζειν[?], καὶ πράσσειν[?] ἰδία[?]. 1.Thes.4.11.
units.tr: To make it your ambition to be quiet and to do your own business [φιλοτιμεῖσθαι ἡσυχάζειν, καὶ πράσσειν ἰδία], 1 Thess. 4:11.

units.la: DE POENITENTIA, THESIS.
units.tr: CONCERNING REPENTANCE, THESIS.

units.la: Exhortatione ad veram poenitentiam, nunquam non opus est.
units.tr: Exhortation to true repentance is never unnecessary.

units.la: Rationes thesin hanc munientes, εὐλ-[?] λαβῶς[?] ita complecti licebit.
units.tr: The reasons supporting this thesis may conveniently be gathered together as follows.

units.la: 1. Quia Deus omnibus utriusq; Testamenti ministris in mandatis dedit, ut prę dicarent poenitentiam & remissionē peccatorū in nomine Christi. Luc.24.46.47.
units.tr: 1. Because God commanded all ministers of both Testaments to preach repentance and the forgiveness of sins in the name of Christ. Luke 24:46-47.

units.la: 2. Quia ascendit malitia hominum in conspectum Iehouae.Ionae 1.2. Item:Vox sanguinis clamat ad Deum è terra. Gen. 4.10. Item: Clamor Sodomae & Gomorrhae multiplicatus est coram me, & peccatum aggrauatum.Gen.18.20.
units.tr: 2. Because the wickedness of men has come up before the face of Jehovah. Jonah 1:2. Likewise: The voice of blood cries to God from the earth. Gen. 4:10. Likewise: The cry of Sodom and Gomorrah has been multiplied before me, and their sin is very grievous. Gen. 18:20.

units.la: 3. Quia iudicaturus est orbem iustè,ne quis non resipiscentium se excusabilem esse putet,denunciat omnibus ubiq; hominibus ut resipiscant.Actor.17.30.31.
units.tr: 3. Because he is going to judge the world justly, and so that no one who has not repented may think himself excusable, he declares to all men everywhere that they should repent. Acts 17:30-31.

units.la: 4. Quia quid sibi pœnæ & castigatio-nes publicæ & privatæ velint, praeconiū poenitentiæ testari debet.
units.tr: 4. Because the purpose of punishments, both public and private, ought to bear witness to the preaching of repentance.

units.la: Quot modis denunciat Deus hominibus ut resipiscant?
units.tr: In how many ways does God declare to men that they should repent?

units.la: Duobus potisimùm, Verbo nimirum & Facto. Utroq; sanè palàm fit ira Dei è cœlo aduersus omnem impietatē & in-iustitiam hominum. Rom.1.18. Ac uerbo quidem coarguit nos, dum quoties & quàm grauiter deliquerimus, ostendit; factis autem coercet peccadi libidinem, cum pœnas de transgressoribus exigit. Verbo perstringit homines: facto cordiū duriciem, ceu malleo, contundit. Ac uerbum, quo ad mortificationem carnis, & uiuificationem spiritus excitamur, Legis & Euangelij concione continetur: facta autem non solùm quatuor Dei iudicia mala, sed etiam priuatas ærumnas & calamitates complectuntur. De illis dicitur Ezech.14.21. Sic enim dixit Dominus Iehouah: Quanto magis, si quatuor iudicia mea mala, gladium, & famem, & bestiam malam, & pestilentiam, misero aduersus Ierusalem, ut succidam ex ea homines & iumenta.
units.tr: Chiefly in two ways, namely by the Word and by deeds. In both, the wrath of God from heaven against all the ungodliness and unrighteousness of men is plainly made known. Rom. 1:18. By the Word he indeed convicts us, showing how often and how grievously we have sinned; by deeds he restrains the lust of sinning, when he exacts punishment from transgressors. By the Word he pierces men; by deeds he crushes the hardness of hearts, as with a hammer. The Word by which we are stirred to the mortifying of the flesh and the quickening of the spirit is contained in the preaching of Law and Gospel; but deeds comprise not only the God's evil judgments, the four of them, but also private distresses and calamities. Of these it is said in Ezek. 14:21: For thus said the Lord Jehovah: How much more, when I send my four evil judgments upon Jerusalem, the sword, and famine, and evil beast, and pestilence, to cut off from it man and beast.

units.la: Rectè dixit D.Hieronymus in epistola ad Demetriadem: Pœnitentia, secunda tabula naufragis?
units.tr: Did Jerome rightly say in his letter to Demetrias: Repentance is a second plank for the shipwrecked?

units.la: Verba Hieronymi hæc sunt: Verum nos ignoremus pœnitentiā, ne facile peccemus. Illa quasi secunda post naufragium miseris tabula sit: in uirgine integra seruetur nauis, Aliud est quæɾere quod perdideris; aliud est possidere quod nunquam amiseris.
units.tr: Jerome's words are these: "But we should be ignorant of repentance, lest we sin easily. It is like a second plank for the wretched after shipwreck; the ship is kept intact in a virgin. It is one thing to seek what you have lost; it is another to possess what you have never lost."

units.la: Non simpliciter dicit, Ignoremus pœ-nitentiam: sed secundum quid, Ne facilè peccemus. Nam bis peccat, qui facilè peccat: quia pœnitentia facilè elui peccatum opinatur.
units.tr: He does not say simply, "Let us be ignorant of repentance," but qualifies it: "lest we sin easily." For he sins twice who sins easily, because he thinks sin is easily washed away by repentance.

units.la: Addit, pœnitentiam esse quasi secun-dam tabulam post naufragium: quod si ita accipias, ut cum Augustino donū pœ-nitentiæ à Deo dari & compleri statuas: & ut, contrà quàm Novatiani olim statue-bant, lapsis post baptismum resipiscendū testeris, nihil incommodi habebit sententia Hieronymi.
units.tr: He adds that repentance is like a second plank after shipwreck. If you understand this in the sense that, with Augustine, you hold repentance to be a gift of God that is given and brought to completion, and if, contrary to what the Novatians once maintained, you bear witness that the lapsed after baptism must repent, then Jerome's statement will contain nothing amiss.

units.la: Illud tamē in fine apparet, ad speciem, videlicet[?] ad virginitatem, quæ semel a-missa, pœnitentia recuperari nequit, re-spexisse.
units.tr: Yet at the end it is clear that he was looking to the image: namely to virginity, which, once lost, cannot be recovered by repentance.

units.la: VERSVS III,
units.tr: VERSE III,

units.la: Surrexit uero Ionah, ut fugeret in Thar-sis à facie Iehoua, & descendit Iapho: reperit autem nauim euntem in Tharsis, de-ditq; naulum, & descendit in eam, ut iret cum eis in Tharsis, à conspectu Iehoua.
units.tr: But Jonah rose up to flee to Tarshish from the presence of Jehovah, and went down to Joppa; and he found a ship going to Tarshish, and paid its fare, and went down into it to go with them to Tarshish, away from the presence of Jehovah.

units.la: Gravissimam apud Ninivitas poenitentiam praedicandi provinciam ut Prophe-ta noster defugere conatus fit, haec sacrae historiae pars docet. Nos docendi caus-sa primùm historiam, deinde θέσιν[?] perpe-demus. Historiae tria membra sunt: primum, quónam locorum Ionas sese recipere conatus sit: secundum, qnem[?] in locum primò fugiens è conspeƈtu Domini delatus sit: postremum, quo consilio fugam maturauerit. Theses duae sunt: altera de fuga è conspeƈtu Dei, altera de recusatione officij diuinitùs demandati. De his ordine ut agere nobis liceat, faxit Christus unicus noster doƈtor.
units.tr: That this Prophet, as he tried to flee from the very serious task of preaching repentance to the Ninevites, is what this part of the sacred history teaches. For the sake of teaching, we shall first go through the history and then the thesis [θέσιν]. The history has three parts: first, to what region Jonah tried to withdraw; second, to what place he was carried first when fleeing from the face of the Lord; last, with what purpose he hastened his flight. There are two theses: one concerning the flight from the face of God, the other concerning the refusal of the office divinely committed to him. May Christ, our only Teacher, grant that we may treat these in order.

units.la: 1. Testatur historia, Ionam in Tharsis fugam parasse. Hieronymus: Unde, ait, imitatus Cain Ionas: & recedens à facie Domini, fugere voluit in Tharsis: quàm Iosephus interpretatur Tarsum Ciliciae ciuitatem, prima tantùm litera commuta-ta. quantum verò in Paralipomenon libris intelligi datur, quidam locus Indiae sic uocatur. Porrò Hebraei Tharsis mare dici generaliter autumant, secundum illud: In spiritu uehementi confringes naues Tharsis, id est, maris, Et in Esaia: Vlu-late late naues Tharsis. Super quo ante annos plurimos in epistola quadā ad Marcellam, dixisse me memini. Nonigitur Propheta ad certum cupiebat fugere locum: sed mare ingrediēs, quocunq; pergere festinabat. & magis hoc conuenit fugitiuo & timido,nō locum fugæ ociosæ eligere,sed primam arripere occasionem nauigandi.
units.tr: 1. The history testifies that Jonah prepared a flight to Tarshish. Jerome says: "Imitating Cain, Jonah, withdrawing from the face of the Lord, wished to flee to Tarshish, which Josephus interprets as Tarsus, a city of Cilicia, with only the first letter changed. But as far as may be understood from the books of Chronicles, a certain place in India is so called." Moreover, the Hebrews think that Tarshish is generally called the sea, according to that passage: With a vehement spirit you will break the ships of Tarshish, that is, of the sea; and in Isaiah: Howl, ships of Tarshish. On this matter I remember having spoken many years ago in a certain letter to Marcella. Therefore the Prophet was not hurrying toward a definite place, but, entering the sea, he was hastening wherever he might go; and it fits a fugitive and a timid man better not to choose a place for an idle flight but to seize the first opportunity to sail.

units.la: De loco Indiæ uocabulum Tharsis nō esse intelligendum, ex eo colligi potest, quòd occidentem uersus Ionas sibi fugiendum putauit,cum in Asyriam ire recusaret. Nec Iosephi sententia parum est probabilis deTarso Ciliciæ urbe (quam ἐν [?] Ciliciæ urbem Paulus uocat, Act.21.39.) cum Ioppen delatus Ionas in Ciliciam defleētere uoluisse uideri possit, & non ita multis post temporibus Iudæorum multi in ea urbe consederint.
units.tr: That the name Tarshish is not to be understood as a place in India can be gathered from the fact that Jonah thought he had to flee westward, since he refused to go to Assyria. Nor is Josephus's opinion, concerning the city of Tarsus in Cilicia, of little probability: for a city of Cilicia [πόλεως], as Paul calls it, Acts 21:39. Since Jonah, having been carried to Joppa, may seem to have wished to flee into Cilicia, and not long after that many Jews settled in that city.

units.la: Siue autē certū locu,nomine Tharsis designatum,siue diuturnā nauigatione statuas, errore φρονήματος σαρκὸς peccauit Ionas, nō cogitans, ἀμεταμέλητον ἡ πάλι-ναγκαστον esse Dei de sua uocatione decretum,eoq; nec diuturna nauigatione,nec loci mutatione,irritum à se fieri posse.
units.tr: But whether we posit a definite place, designated by the name Tarshish, or a long voyage, Jonah sinned through the error of the mind of the flesh [φρονήματος σαρκὸς], not considering that God's decree concerning his calling is irrevocable [ἀμεταμέλητον] and not to be compelled back [ἡ πάλιναγκαστον], and that therefore it cannot be annulled by him either through a long voyage or through a change of place.

units.la: 2. Ionas fugā meditans Iapho primūm delatus est, in portum, ut apparet, patriæ vicinum. Ioppen Lucas vocat, Act.9.36.
units.tr: 2. Jonah, planning his flight, was first carried to Joppa, a port evidently near his homeland. Luke calls it Joppa, Acts 9:36.

units.la: 43. Ioppen portum esse Iudæae, & in Regnorum & Paralipomenon libris legimus: ad quem Hiram quoq; Rex Tyri ligna de Libano ratibus transferebat, quæ Hierusalem terreno itinere perueheren-tur.[?] Hic locus est, in quo usq; hodie saxa monstratur in littore, in quibus Andromeda religata, Perfei quondam sit libera tā praesidio. Scit eruditus Lector historiam: sed & iuxta regionis naturam de montanis & arduis ad Ioppen & campestria veniens Propheta, rectè dicitur descen-disse & invenisse naue, &c. Hæc Hieronymus αὐτόπτης[?] & incola illius regionis. Meminit eiusdem portus & Strabo lib. 16. Geograph. Turcæ hac ætate portum hunc Palestinæ, Sappho vocare dicuntur.
units.tr: 43. We read in the books of Kings and Chronicles that Joppa is a port of Judea, to which Hiram also King of Tyre transported timber from Lebanon by raft, which was then carried overland to Jerusalem. This is the place where, even today, rocks are shown on the shore to which Andromeda was once bound, and from which she was freed by the protection of Perseus. The learned reader knows the story; but also, according to the nature of the region, the Prophet, coming from the mountains and heights down to Joppa and the flat country, is rightly said to have gone down and found a ship, etc. These are Jerome's words, as an eyewitness [αὐτόπτης] and inhabitant of that region. Strabo also mentions this same port, in book 16 of his Geography. In our own age the Turks are said to call this port of Palestine Sappho.

units.la: 3. Quo consilio & quibus de causis Ionas vocationem sibi defugiendam censuerit, diligenter nobis perpendendum est. Divus Hieronymus has causas adducit.
units.tr: 3. With what purpose and for what reasons Jonah judged that he should flee the calling entrusted to him must be weighed carefully by us. Divus Jerome brings forward these reasons.

units.la: 1. Studium erga gentem[?] suam. Scit, inquit, Propheta, sancto Spiritu suggeren-te, quòd poenitetia gentium, ruina fit Iu-daeorum, dæorum. Idcirco amator patriæ suæ, nō tam saluti inuidet Niniue, quàm nō uult perire suum populum.
units.tr: 1. Zeal for his own people. The Prophet knows, says Jerome, the Holy Spirit suggesting it, that the repentance of the Gentiles means the ruin of the Jews. Therefore, as a lover of his fatherland, he does not so much begrudge Nineveh its salvation as he is unwilling that his own people should perish.

units.la: 2. Exemplum cæterorum Prophetarum. Pręterea uidens Ionas comprophetas suos mitti ad oues perditas domus Israel, ut ad pœnitentiam populum prouocarent: Balaam quoq; diuinum de salute Israelitici populi prophetasse: dolet se solum electum, qui mitteretur ad Assyrios inimicos Israel, & ad ciuitatem hostiū maximam: ubi idololatria, ubi ignoratio Dei, &c. Nos alias duas addemus.
units.tr: 2. The example of the other Prophets. Moreover, seeing that his fellow prophets were sent to the lost sheep of the house of Israel, to stir the people to repentance, and that Balaam also prophesied of the salvation of the Israelite people, Jonah grieves that he alone is chosen to be sent to the Assyrians, the enemies of Israel, and to the greatest city of the enemies: where there is idolatry, where there is ignorance of God, and so on. We shall add two others.

units.la: 3. Fuga uanitatis. Seruus Dei non solum à uanitate, sed etiam ab eius suspicione alienus & esse & haberi uult. Iam uero consideratio clementiæ & bonitatis Dei persuasit Ionæ, ut uerereretur, ne si post à se denunciatam Niniuitis πανωλέθρῳ[?] Dominus resipiscentibus parceret, ipse uanus uideretur uates, & comminationes propheticæ mendacij insimularentur. Atqui istud perpendere Ionam par erat, & comminationem illam habere annexam conditionem de resipiscentia, & Dei seruo officium esse faciendū, quicquid tandem eueniat.
units.tr: 3. Avoidance of vanity. The servant of God wishes not only to be free from vanity but also from any suspicion of it, and to be and to be thought so. Indeed, consideration of the clemency and goodness of God persuaded Jonah that he should fear that, if after his proclamation to the Ninevites of utter destruction [πανωλέθρῳ] the Lord should spare them when they repented, he himself would appear to be a vain prophet, and the prophetic threats would be charged with falsehood. Yet Jonah ought to have weighed this: that the threat carried with it the condition of repentance, and that it is the duty of God's servant to do what he has been given, whatever may come of it.

units.la: 4. Metus periculorum. Perinde enim erat Ionam ad Niniuitas ad resipiscentiā prædicandam ablegare, ac si hac ætate mittatur Euangelij præco Constantinopolin ad impios Mahometistas, & eorū Principem Amurathem Selymi secundi filium, qui nunc rerum potitur.
units.tr: 4. Fear of dangers. For it would have been just as if someone in our own age were sent as a herald of the Gospel to Constantinople, to the impious Mahometans, and to their Prince Murad, son of Selim the Second, who now holds power.

units.la: THESIS PRIMA, DE FVGA è conspectu Domini.
units.tr: THESIS FIRST, ON FLIGHT FROM THE SIGHT OF THE LORD.

units.la: 1. Fuga è conspectu Dei, non simpliciter respectu essentiæ diuinæ, sed κατὰ τί respectu gratiæ aut officij, accipi debet.
units.tr: 1. Flight from the sight of God must be understood not simply with respect to the divine essence, but in what respect [κατὰ τί], that is, with respect to grace or to office.

units.la: Declaratio. Nam Dei essentia immensa est, & omnia implet. Ier. 23. 23. 24. Numquid Deus de propinquo ego sum, dixit Iehouah, & non Deus de longinquo? Num occultabit se quisquam in occultis, & ego non uidebo eum, dixit Iehouah? An non cœlum & terram ego impleo, dixit Iehouah? Hac proprietate essentiali, quemadmodum & æternitate ἀνάρχῳ & aliis, differt Creator à creaturis.
units.tr: Explanation. For the essence of God is immense and fills all things. Jer. 23:23-24: "Am I a God at hand, says the LORD, and not a God afar off? Can any hide himself in secret places so that I shall not see him? says the LORD. Do not I fill heaven and earth? says the LORD." By this essential property, as by his eternity without beginning [ἀνάρχῳ] and other attributes, the Creator differs from creatures.

units.la: 2. Respectu gratiæ, non nisi reprobi è conspectu Dei fugiunt. Vt de Caino dicitur: Egressus est Cain à facie Iehouæ. Gen. 4. 16.
units.tr: 2. With respect to grace, only the reprobate flee from the sight of God. So it is said of Cain: "Cain went out from the presence of the LORD." Gen. 4:16.

units.la: 3. Iidem deserentes communionem καὶ ἐπισυναγωγὴ[?] Sanctorum, apostatas se esse, nec unquam uiua Ecclesiae membra fuisse, ipsis factis testantur, iuxta dictum: E' nobis egressi sunt, sed non erant ex nobis: nam si fuissent ex nobis, permansif-sentutiq; nobiscum. Sed hoc factum est, ut patefieret, quod nō sint omnes ex nobis. 1. Ioan. 2.19.
units.tr: 3. Those who abandon the fellowship and assembly [ἐπισυναγωγὴ] of the saints show by their very deeds that they are apostates, and that they were never living members of the Church, according to the saying: "They went out from us, but they were not of us; for if they had been of us, they would have continued with us. But this happened so that it might be made plain that not all are of us." 1 John 2:19.

units.la: 4. Ac tum deleri è libro uiuentium dicuntur, cum testatum fit, nunquam adoptionis participes fuisse. Psal. 69.29.
units.tr: 4. Moreover, they are said to be blotted out of the book of the living when it is made plain that they never shared in adoption. Ps. 69:29.

units.la: 5. Fideles etsi saepe grauiter labuntur, è gratia tamen finaliter non excidunt. Ratio: 1. Quia fidei πληροφορίᾳ[?] cum perseuerantiae dono coniungitur. 2. Quia illorum errata, Dei propositum non possunt irritum facere. 3. Quia nemo, inquit Christus, oues meas de manu mea rapiet. Ioan. 10.
units.tr: 5. Believers, although they often fall grievously, do not finally fall away from grace. The reasons are: (1) faith is joined with the gift of perseverance; (2) their errors cannot render the purpose of God void; (3) as Christ says, no one shall snatch my sheep out of my hand. John 10.

units.la: 6. Fugere autem è conspectu Iehouae etiam tum dicuntur, cum sanctam uocationem detrectat & defugiunt, ut hoc loco de Iona dicitur, quòd arduam functionem denunciandi apud Niniuitas poenitentiam declinans, fugerit è conspectu Iehouae.
units.tr: 6. Moreover, they are said to flee from the sight of the LORD also when they reject and shun a holy calling, as is said here of Jonah, who, shrinking from the arduous task of preaching repentance to the Ninevites, fled from the sight of the LORD.

units.la: 7. Item, cùm se à populi Dei consortio, & sacris congressibus, in quibus Deus pu-re colitur, subducunt, neue uel iacturam fortunarum suarum faciant, uel quæstus faciendi arisam[?] negligant.
units.tr: 7. Likewise, when they withdraw themselves from the fellowship of the people of God and from the holy gatherings in which God is purely worshipped, in order that they may either lose nothing of their fortunes or neglect the gain to be made.

units.la: Quod autem ebrijs interdum euenire uidemus, ut eorum obliuiscatur, quæ nemini sano ignota sunt: id etiam Sanctis, si quandō τὸ τῆς σαρκὸς φρόνημα[?] secuti, suis desiderijs indulgent, & ubi non erat metuendum metuunt, accidit, ut ea non veniant in mentem, quæ ipsos alioquin non fugiunt. Vt Ionæ fugienti è conspectu Iehouæ, in illo paroxysmo non venit in mentem illud Dauidis: Quò ibo à Spiritu tuo, & quò fugiam à facie tua? Si ascendero in cœlum, ibi es: & si stratum fecero in inferno, ecce tu ades. Psal. 139. 6. 7. 8. 9.
units.tr: But as we sometimes see happen to drunken men, that they forget things unknown to no sober person, so it also happens to the saints: when they follow the mind of the flesh [τὸ τῆς σαρκὸς φρόνημα] and indulge their desires, and fear where there was no cause to fear, those things do not come to mind which otherwise they do not overlook. So Jonah, fleeing from the sight of the LORD, in that frenzy did not recall that saying of David: "Whither shall I go from your Spirit, or whither shall I flee from your face? If I ascend into heaven, you are there; if I make my bed in hell, behold, you are there." Ps. 139:6-9.

units.la: THESIS SECVNDA, DE RECV-satione officij diuinitùs demandati.
units.tr: THESIS SECOND, ON REFUSING AN OFFICE DIVINELY COMMITTED.

units.la: 1. Pessimè agunt, qui sanctam uocatio-nem serio detrectant. Aduersantur enim consilio & uoluntati diuinæ, de qua dicitur 1. Cor. 7. 17. Vt unicuiq; (donum) partitus est Deus, ut unumquemque uocauit Dominus, ita incedat: & ita in Ecclesijs omnibus constituo.
units.tr: 1. They act very wickedly who seriously refuse a holy calling. For they oppose the counsel and will of God, of whom it is said: "As God has distributed to each, as the Lord has called each, so let him walk; and so I ordain in all the churches." 1 Cor. 7:17.

units.la: 2. Horū tamen duo sunt genera. Vnum eorum, qui officium diuinitùs delegatū suscipere recusant: alterum eorum, qui officium suscèptum deponunt.
units.tr: 2. There are, however, two kinds of these people: one kind of those who refuse to take up an office divinely entrusted to them; the other of those who lay down an office they have taken up.

units.la: Sunt enim, qui errore simplici ducti, uocationem defugiant: posterioribus autem curis admoniti, Deo libenter pareant.
units.tr: For some, led by simple error, shun their calling; but these, when admonished by later troubles, gladly obey God.

units.la: Sunt qui τὰ ἴδια quaerentes, per omnem uitam Deo uocanti parere recusent. Sunt denique, qui fide temporaria nonnihil excitati, tandem cum fide uocationem abijciant.
units.tr: Some, seeking their own things [τὰ ἴδια], refuse all their life to obey the God who calls them. Finally, there are those who, roused for a time by a passing faith, at last cast off their calling along with their faith.

units.la: 3. Eorum qui initiò officium recusant, alij Deo uocanti cedunt, illius quàm suiipsorum maiorem habentes rationem: alij sua potius quàm quae sunt Dei quaerentes, nunquam Dei uocanti obtemperat.
units.tr: 3. Of those who at the outset refuse an office, some yield to the God who calls, having a greater regard for his will than for their own; others, seeking their own rather than the things of God, never obey the call of God.

units.la: Ad priorem classem referri debet magna Ecclesiae lumina, Isaias, Ieremias, Ionas, & multi alij. Fuit autem προσκαταρτι[?] recusati muneris causa, quòd in seipsos descendentes, indignos se tantis muneribus, nec praesidijs ad ea rectè administranda instructos, agnoscerét & ingenuè faterentur. Isaias dicebat: Væ mihi, quia tacui: nam uir pollutus labijs ego sum, & in medio populi pollutis labijs habito. cap.6.5. Tria deplorat, peccatum, infantiam & consortium cum pollutis? quæ omnia segregationi ad sanctum munus è diametro aduersari iudicabat. Ieremias autè respodebat Domino ipsum uocanti ad munus propheticum: Ah ah, Domine Iehouah, en nescio loqui, quia puer sum. cap.1.6. Ionas, ueritus ne si denunciationes non implerentur, uanus ψευδοπροφήτης[?] uideretur, initiò defugit munus prædicandi apud Niniuitas pœ-nitentiam. Verùm hi & alij eorum simi-les tandem Deo morem gesserunt, freti ipsius præsentia & ope.
units.tr: To the first class belong the great lights of the Church: Isaiah, Jeremiah, Jonah, and many others. Now the cause of their refusal was that, descending into themselves, they recognised and freely confessed that they were unworthy of such great gifts and not equipped with the resources to discharge them rightly. Isaiah said: "Woe is me, for I have held my peace; for I am a man of unclean lips, and I dwell among a people of unclean lips." Isa. 6:5. He lamented three things: sin, infancy, and fellowship with the unclean; he judged all of these to be wholly opposed to separation for a holy office. Jeremiah, indeed, answered the Lord who called him to the prophetic office: "Ah, ah, Lord GOD! Behold, I cannot speak, for I am a child." Jer. 1:6. Jonah, fearing that if his predictions were not fulfilled he would seem a vain false prophet, at first shunned the task of preaching repentance to the Ninevites. Yet these and others like them at last obeyed God, relying on his presence and help.

units.la: 4. Minus autem mali in eo est, si quis conscientia suæ infirmitatis ductus, officium delegatum initiò recuset, quàm si quis suijpsius suorumq; maiorem habe-at rationem, quàm Dei & sanctę ipsius uo-luntatis. iuxta dictum: Sequere me, & si-ne ut mortui sepeliant suos mortuos. Matt.8.22. Item: Qui amat patrem aut matrem supra me, non est me dignus. Matt.10.37.
units.tr: 4. Less harm, however, is done if someone, led by a consciousness of his own weakness, at the outset refuses an office entrusted to him, than if someone has greater regard for himself and his own than for the will of God and of holiness. According to the saying: "Follow me, and let the dead bury their dead." Matt. 8:22. Likewise: "He who loves father or mother more than me is not worthy of me." Matt. 10:37.

units.la: 5. Sed illud plenum impietatis est, opes & gratia mundi, Dei cōsilio anteponere.
units.tr: 5. But it is full of impiety to set the riches and favour of the world before the counsel of God.

units.la: 6. Eorum uerò qui uocationem susce-ptam abijciunt, duo itidem ordines sunt. De his dicitur: Nemo qui manu sua admota aratro, respexerit ad ea quę a tergo sunt, aptus est regno Dei. Luc. 9. 62.
units.tr: 6. Of those who cast off a calling they have accepted, there are likewise two orders. Of them it is said: "No one who puts his hand to the plough and looks back to the things behind is fit for the kingdom of God." Luke 9:62.

units.la: 7. Primus eorum est, qui loca tenetes, animo, non externo opere, officium deserūt, quod aut inuiti & perfunctorie, aut gloriae & quaestus causa administrant. De talibus extant haec dicta.
units.tr: 7. The first of these are those who, while holding their place, desert the office in spirit, not in outward work, performing it either unwillingly and perfunctorily, or for glory and gain. Of such people these sayings exist.

units.la: Matt.7.21. Non omnis qui dicit mihi, Domine Domine, introibit in regnū coelorum: sed qui fecerit voluntatem Patris mei, qui in coelis est.
units.tr: Matt. 7:21: "Not everyone who says to me, Lord, Lord, shall enter the kingdom of heaven, but he who does the will of my Father who is in heaven."

units.la: Phil. 2. 21. Nam omnes quae sua ipsorum sunt quaerunt, non quae sunt Christi Iesu.
units.tr: Phil. 2:21: "For all seek their own, not the things of Jesus Christ."

units.la: 8. Secundus autem illorum est, qui opere discedunt a vocatione, vel aliud agentes, vel nihil agentes, vel vocationem sibi probatis conditionibus astringentes.
units.tr: 8. The second of these are those who depart from their calling in deed, either by doing something else, or by doing nothing, or by binding their calling to conditions of their own choosing.

units.la: 1. Aliud agunt, qui fingunt quidem se opus Domini agere, sed revera aliud, alio modo & fine, quam oportebat, agunt. Tales erant contumaces illi ματαιόλογοι[?], & mentium seductores ex circumcisione, Tit.1.10. Ad horum ordinem omnes ἑτεροδιδάσκαλοι[?], ut maximè loca Sanctorū teneant, referendi nobis sunt.
units.tr: 1. They do something else who pretend that they are doing the work of the Lord, but in truth are doing another work, in another manner and for another end than they ought. Such were those stubborn empty talkers [ματαιόλογοι] and deceivers of minds from the circumcision. Titus 1:10. To this order all teachers of other doctrine [ἑτεροδιδάσκαλοι] are to be referred, especially those who hold the chief places among the saints.

units.la: 2. Nihil agût[?], qui officio abiecto, susq; deq; faciunt, quicquid tandem de eo fiat. De his dicitur Pro.27.8: Vtauis discedens é nido suo, sic uir deserens locum suum. Talis erat Demas, de quo Paulus: Dereliquit, ait, me, amplexus praesens se-culum: & Thessalonicam profectus est. 2.Tim.4.10.
units.tr: 2. They do nothing who, having cast off the office, care nothing for whatever may become of it. Of such it is said: "As a bird that wanders from her nest, so is a man who forsakes his place." Prov. 27:8. Such was Demas, of whom Paul says: "He has forsaken me, having loved this present world, and has gone to Thessalonica." 2 Tim. 4:10.

units.la: Est hominum quoddam genus, cui si de culina & vetre laute prospicias, ne hu-ius quidem facturi sint veritatem & eius ingenuam professionem: ius, fas, honestum non maioris faciant, quàm suas de-litias.
units.tr: There is a certain kind of men who, if you provide for them from the kitchen and the belly with fine fare, will not even make a true and honest profession of what they should do: they do not esteem right, duty, or honour any more than their own pleasures.

units.la: 3. Vocatione aut sibi probatis conditio-nibus adstringunt, qui ab ea Christi cru-cem separant. Parati sunt hi officio fun-gi, dum hominum gratia, opes, uitae com-moda ita ferre uidentur. Si horum iactu-ram facturi uideantur, stultitiam esse pu-tant, mentis maiorem habere rationem quàm uentris. Itaque & exemplo & exhor-tatione sua nocent, dum mundum Christo anteponendum statuunt.
units.tr: 3. They bind their calling to conditions of their own choosing, and so separate the cross of Christ from it. These men are ready to discharge the office as long as it seems to bring them the favour of men, riches, and comforts of life. But if they seem likely to suffer loss from it, they think it folly to have greater regard for the mind than for the belly. And so they harm both by their example and by their exhortation, while they establish that the world is to be preferred to Christ.

units.la: Certissimum autem est, [illegible, ~10 letters] istis imminere: nobis verò, siquidem in sancta vocatione permanserimus, spe-randum randum esse, laborem nostrum non fore inanem in Domino.
units.tr: It is most certain that [...] hang over those men; but for us, provided we persevere in the holy calling, we ought to hope that our labour will not be in vain in the Lord.

units.la: [illegible, ~10 letters] de Theologici studij de-sertoribus.
units.tr: On the deserters of theological study.

units.la: Initiò observanda nobis sunt Theologiae studiosorum honestissima nomina.Vocantur enim Filij Prophetarum, 2.Reg.4. 1.& 39. quia decet eos, Christo Iesu testimonium perhibentes, Prophetis subscribere ut patribus.Act.10.43. Item, κατ' ἐξοχὴν, πιστοὶ ἄνθρωποι, fideles homines. Etsi enim omnes Ecclesiae cives fidelitatem Domino suo probare decet: tamen eos qui aliquando acturi sunt promos & codos oraculorum Dei,& depositarios τῆς καλῆς παρακαταθήκης, fide prae caeteris excellere decet. iuxta haec dicta: Quod superest, hoc requiritur in dispensatoribus, quòd fidus quisque reperiatur. 1.Cor.4.2. Item: Praeclarum depositum servua, per Spiritū sanctū, qui habitat in nobis. 2.Tim.1.14.
units.tr: At the outset we must note the most honourable names of those who study theology. They are called sons of the prophets (2 Kings 4:1 and 39), because it befits them, bearing witness to Christ Jesus, to stand alongside the prophets as their heirs, as sons do their fathers (Acts 10:43). They are also called faithful men par excellence [κατ' ἐξοχὴν, πιστοὶ ἄνθρωποι]. For although all citizens of the Church ought to prove their faithfulness to their Lord, those who will one day be the stewards and guardians of God's oracles, and the keepers of the good deposit [τῆς καλῆς παρακαταθήκης], ought to excel in faithfulness above the rest. To this accords the saying: "Moreover it is required of stewards that a man be found faithful" (1 Cor. 4:2). Also: "Keep the good deposit through the Holy Spirit who dwells in us" (2 Tim. 1:14).

units.la: Plurimum autem refert, vocationis ad hoc studium [illegible, ~6 letters] observare, & ab ἀποστασίας, quibus nonnulli decipiuntur, discernere. Τιμῆς sanctae ad Theologiam discendam vocationis sunt:
units.tr: It matters greatly to observe the calling to this study and to distinguish it from apostasies [ἀποστασίας], by which some are deceived. The marks of a holy calling to the study of theology are [...] honours [Τιμῆς]:

units.la: 1. Singulare & constans studium τῆς θεογνωσίας,
units.tr: 1. A singular and constant zeal for the knowledge of God [τῆς θεογνωσίας],

units.la: { } The printed Greek of the heading and of the tail of the last line is set in a larger or smaller font than the Latin, and some Greek words are read only in part. θεογνωσίας, id est, agnitionis Dei.
units.tr: { } The printed Greek of the heading and of the tail of the last line is set in a larger or smaller font than the Latin, and some Greek words are read only in part. The knowledge of God [θεογνωσίας], that is, the knowledge of God.

units.la: 2. Desiderium iuge profitendi & propagandi doctrinam cœlestē, propter Dei gloriam.
units.tr: 2. A continual desire to profess and spread the heavenly doctrine, for the glory of God.

units.la: 3. Ἐπιχαρ[?]αγαθία[?] cum Verbi & Sacramentum administratione ædificatur Ecclesia.
units.tr: 3. The Church is built up by the administration of the Word and the Sacraments.

units.la: 4. Nemesis & ingens dolor, cum Ecclesiæ desunt fidi pastores, & præsunt hypocrytæ aut mercenarij, cauponantes verbum Dei: aut cum idololatræ loca tenet, & idololatriam exercent.
units.tr: 4. Righteous indignation and deep grief when faithful ministers are lacking in the Church, and hypocrites or hirelings hold office, peddling the Word of God; or when idolaters hold the places and practise idolatry.

units.la: 5. Sensus præsentiæ Spiritus sancti, & usus donorum quibus opus est ad plantandum & rigandum Ecclesiæ aruum.
units.tr: 5. A sense of the presence of the Holy Spirit and the use of the gifts needed for planting and watering the field of the Church.

units.la: Εἰκότα autem sunt;
units.tr: The likely reasons [Εἰκότα] are these:

units.la: 1. Occasiones ꝑficiendi in studio Theologico propter doctorum, librorum, condiscipulorum, ocij, sumtuum, copiam.
units.tr: 1. Opportunities for progress in theological study, through the abundance of teachers, books, fellow students, leisure and means.

units.la: 2. Parentum & liberorum voluntas cō-sentiens, sed quæ sæpe spe honoris, quæstus, successionis in officio, magis commouent, quàm studio sanctificandi nomen Dei.
units.tr: 2. The agreeing will of parents and children, though this is often moved more by hope of honour, gain, or succession to an office than by zeal to sanctify the name of God.

units.la: Danda est autem opera, ut mente pura & spontanea, ac in Dei solius gloriam & Ecclesiæ ædificationem respiciente, sacrum istud professionis Theologicæ genus & aggrediamur, & constanter prosequamur.
units.tr: We must take care to undertake and steadily pursue this sacred kind of theological profession with a pure and willing mind, looking only to the glory of God and the building up of the Church.

units.la: Adiuncta sacri istius studij petere licebit ex Pauli Apostoli uerbis: Et quæ audistì a me inter multos testes, hæc committe fidelibus hominibus, qui erunt idonei ad alios quoq; docendos. 2.Tim.2.
units.tr: The things that go with this sacred study may be sought from the words of the Apostle Paul: "And what you have heard from me among many witnesses, commit this to faithful men, who will be able to teach others also" (2 Tim. 2:2).

units.la: Tria sunt studiosorum Theologiæ προ κεφάλαια[?], Primum, audiendo uerbum Domini, ceu pretiosum semen, puro corde excipere. Secundum, custodiendo depositum illud præclarum asseruare. Nam idem de illis, quod de Iudæis, dici potest, uidelicet illis commissa esse Dei oracula. Rom.3.2. Tertiū, docendo propagare uerbū Domini. Omnia autem ista, summa fide, per Spiritum sanctum, præstáda sunt.
units.tr: There are three chief heads [προκεφάλαια] for students of theology. First, to receive the word of the Lord with a pure heart, as precious seed, by hearing it. Second, to keep and guard that excellent deposit. For what is said of the Jews may be said of these men too, namely that the oracles of God were committed to them (Rom. 3:2). Third, to spread the word of the Lord by teaching. All these things must be performed with the utmost faithfulness, through the Holy Spirit.

units.la: Postremò, Scādala quæ à studio Theologico abstêrrent, & eorundem ἀντιφα-μαχα, expendenda sunt. Hæc autem præcipua sunt:
units.tr: Finally, the stumbling-blocks that turn people away from theological study, and their antidotes [ἀντιφάρμακα], must be weighed. The chief of these are:

units.la: 1. Paupertas, cum omnibus incommodis, quæ illam comitari solet. Notæ sunt historiæ, de uidua & filijs Prophetę, quos creditor in seruitutem redigere uolebat. Item, de hospitijs & uictu filiorum Prophetarum. 2.Reg.4. Remedium huius mali, quod est αὐτάρκεια[?] & frugalitas, suo exemplo in medio adducto Paulus indicauit, cum diceret: Ego didici, in quibus sum, ijs contentus esse. Noui autem deprimi, noui & abundare: ubiq; & in omnibus initiatus sum, & ad saturitatem, & ad esuritionē: id est, tum ad abundantiam, tum ad inopiam. Omnia ualeo per Christum, qui me corroborat. Phil. 4. 11. 12. 13.
units.tr: 1. Poverty, with all the troubles that usually accompany it. We have the stories of the widow and the sons of the prophet, whom the creditor wanted to reduce to slavery, and of the lodging and food of the sons of the prophets (2 Kings 4). The remedy for this evil is self-sufficiency [αὐτάρκεια] and frugality, which Paul showed by his own example when he said: "I have learned to be content in whatever circumstances I am. I know how to be abased, and I know how to abound; in any and every circumstance I have learned the secret of facing plenty and hunger, abundance and need. I can do all things through Christ who strengthens me" (Phil. 4:11–13).

units.la: 2. Contemtus & odium mundi, iuxta dictum: Si mundus uos odit, scitis quòd me prius quàm uos odio habuerit. Si de mundo fuissetis, mundus quod suum est diligeret: quia uerò de mundo non estis, sed ego elegi uos ex mundo, propterea odit uos mundus. Ioan. 15. 18. 19.
units.tr: 2. Contempt and hatred from the world, according to the saying: "If the world hates you, know that it hated me before it hated you. If you were of the world, the world would love what is its own; but because you are not of the world, but I chose you out of the world, therefore the world hates you" (John 15:18–19).

units.la: Antipharmaca huius mali petęda sunt ex hisce & similibus dictis: Enimuerò si adhuc hominibus placerem, Christi seruus non essem. Gal. 1. 10. Item: At[?] me uerò abest gloriari, nisi in cruce Domini nostri Iesu Christi: per quem mundus mihi crucifixus est, & ego mundo. Gal. 6. 14.
units.tr: The antidotes to this evil are to be sought in these and similar sayings: "For if I still pleased men, I would not be a servant of Christ" (Gal. 1:10). Also: "But far be it from me to glory, except in the cross of our Lord Jesus Christ, through whom the world has been crucified to me, and I to the world" (Gal. 6:14).

units.la: 3. Ingratitudo & uanitas magnæ partis hominum, qui in Ecclesia, sed non ex ea sunt. Sed huic tentationi illud opponendum, Quòd Deus est merces magna seruorum suorum. Gen.12.
units.tr: 3. The ingratitude and vanity of a large part of mankind, who are in the Church but not of it. Against this temptation the following must be set: that God is the great reward of his servants (Gen. 15:1).

units.la: 4. Falsorum fratrum apertę uellicationes, clandestinæ obtrectationes, & technæ, quas [illegible, ~9 letters] Satanæ suggerit. Sed meminerimus, consolationes Christi superabundare in fidelibus seruis, &c.
units.tr: 4. The open attacks of false brethren, secret slanders, and the schemes that [...] Satan suggests. But let us remember that the consolations of Christ abound in faithful servants, etc.

units.la: Iam si quis, primùm ea quæ nos monent, ut in sancta uocatione perseueremus: deinde contraria, ea uidelicet quæ ab illa nos absterret, perpendat: animad-uertet, neminem eorum, qui de sua uocatione ad hoc genus studiorum certò persuasi sunt, sine scelere eam abijcere posse. Cætera, quæ addi poterant, pijs uestris meditationibus relinquo.
units.tr: Now if someone first weighs those things that urge us to persevere in the holy calling, and then the contrary things, namely those that turn us away from it, he will see that none of those who are certainly persuaded of their calling to this kind of study can cast it off without sin. I leave the rest, which might be added, to your pious meditations.

units.la: VERSVS IIII.
units.tr: VERSE 4.

units.la: At Iehouah excitauit uentum magnū in mare, fuitq; turbo magnus in mari, & nauis putauit conteri.
units.tr: But Jehovah stirred up a great wind upon the sea, and there was a great tempest in the sea, and the ship was thought to be broken.

units.la: Huius uersus [παραφραστικῶς?] expositionē è Psalmo 107. initiò adducam: ac deinde Logicè eundē interpretari conabor. Dauidis hæc uerba sunt: Descendentes in mare nauibus, qui q; faciut opus in aquis multis, ipsi uident opera Iehouæ, & mirabilia eius in profundo. Dicit namque, & flare facit spiritum turbinis, & exaltat fluctus eius. Ascendunt usque ad cœlum, descendūt usque ad uoragines: ita ut anima eorum in malo liquefiat. Iactantur & nutant uelut ebrius, ita ut omnis sapientia eorum absorbeatur.
units.tr: I will first set out an paraphrase of this verse, taken from Psalm 107, and then try to interpret it logically. These are David's words: "Those who go down to the sea in ships, who do business in great waters, they see the works of Jehovah and his wonders in the deep. For he speaks and raises the stormy wind, and lifts up its waves. They mount up to heaven, they go down to the depths; their soul melts away in misery. They reel and stagger like a drunken man, so that all their wisdom is swallowed up."

units.la: In hac, quanquā breui, horrendæ tempestatis in mari descriptione, tria occurrunt: Efficientes eius causæ, forma, & proximus finis.
units.tr: In this description of a dreadful storm at sea, brief though it is, three things present themselves: the efficient causes, the form, and the proximate end.

units.la: 1. Αἴτιον ζωΐον[?], erat Deus, qui solus ut conditor est totius uniuersitatis rerum, sic etiam liberrimus & omnipotens gubernator est. Ille tempestates ciere, &, cum uisum est, sedare potest. Psal. 29. Itaq; præclarum Deitatis Iesu Christi argumentum erat, cum mare & uenti ei auscultarent: Matth. 8. 27. Ac uel hinc colligere est, quid eorum opinioni deferedum sit, qui Diabolum & Lamias, pro sua libidine, grandines, tonitrua, pruinam, & alias tempestates excitare posse, putant.
units.tr: 1. The efficient cause [αἴτιον] was God, who alone, as the creator of the whole universe, is also its free and almighty governor. He can stir up storms and, when it seems good to him, calm them. Psalm 29. Hence it was a remarkable proof of the divinity of Jesus Christ that the sea and the winds obeyed him: Matthew 8:27. From this one may also gather how much weight should be given to the opinion of those who think that the devil and witches can, at their own pleasure, raise hailstorms, thunder, frost, and other tempests.

units.la: 2. Famulans causa fuit, Ventus ingens, Psal. 135, 7. Qui ascendere facit nubes ab extremo terræ: fulgura cum pluuia ipsa facit, qui educit uentum è thesauris suis.
units.tr: 2. The servant cause was a mighty wind, Psalm 135:7: "He causes the clouds to rise from the ends of the earth; he makes lightnings with the rain, and brings the wind out of his storehouses."

units.la: Peripatetici,ut hoc addam propter iuniores, docent, Ventum esse exhalatione calidam & siccam, quae difficulter inflammabilis, eleuatur usque ad mediam aeris regionem, à cuius frigore deorsum repulsa, & sursum nitens, partim leuitate sua, partim propter alias exhalationes inferne occurrentes, lateraliter mouetur supra terram, in infima regione aeris, quem agitat & uentilat, ne quasi putrescat perpetua desidia.
units.tr: Let me add, for the sake of younger readers, that the Peripatetics teach that wind is a warm and dry exhalation, which is hard to set on fire. It is lifted up to the middle region of the air, and being driven back down by the cold there, and striving upward again, it moves sideways over the earth, partly by its own lightness and partly because of other exhalations meeting it from below, in the lowest region of the air. It stirs and ventilates the air so that it does not go bad through constant stillness.

units.la: 3. Forma tempestatis marinae, Graecis λαῖλαψ μέγας ἐν τῇ θαλάσσῃ[?] uocatur. Ac uix uerior descriptio iactationis istius adferri potest, ea quam è Psal. 107. iam adduxi: cui addi potest alia, quae extat Matt.8, 24: Motus magnus factus est in mari, adeo ut nauis operiretur à fluctibus.
units.tr: 3. The form of a storm at sea is called in Greek a great squall [λαῖλαψ μέγας ἐν τῇ θαλάσσῃ]. Hardly a truer description of this tossing can be given than the one I have already quoted from Psalm 107. To it may be added another, found in Matthew 8:24: "A great motion arose in the sea, so that the ship was covered by the waves."

units.la: 4. Finis proximus, Vt nauis uideretur conterenda. Sic ab undis & uentis conquassata est nauis, ut nauigantes parum in eius firmitate spei sibi superesse statuerent. Ita solet Deus praesidia ad quae confugimus, conterere, ut liberatio miranda soli Deo accepta feratur.
units.tr: 4. The proximate end was that the ship should seem to be about to break up. The ship was so shaken by the waves and winds that those sailing judged that little hope of its firmness remained to them. So God is accustomed to break the very aids to which we flee, so that the deliverance, which is wonderful, may be recognised as coming from God alone.

units.la: THESIS, DE VINDICTA DIVINA, ob negligentiam officij.
units.tr: THESIS, ON DIVINE VENGEANCE, FOR NEGLECT OF DUTY.

units.la: Ad uindicandam officij diuinitus delegati negligentiõne, ærumnas & mala publica & priuata, seruiente eidem rerum uniuersitate, Deus Zelotes adhibet. In hac thesi hæc omnia notanda sunt:
units.tr: To avenge the negligence of a duty divinely assigned, God, the jealous God, brings upon us public and private troubles and evils, the whole created order serving him for this purpose. In this thesis the following points are to be noted:

units.la: 1. Deum Zelotem uisitare iniquitatem etiam in seruis suis, ut eos emendet. Psal. 119: Bonum est mihi Domine, quòd me humiliasti, ut discere iustificationes tuas.
units.tr: 1. God, the jealous God, visits iniquity even upon his servants, in order to correct them. Psalm 119: "It is good for me, O Lord, that you have humbled me, so that I may learn your righteous decrees."

units.la: 2. Specialem offensam, sæpius esse publici mali causam προκατάληψιν, ut Dauidis populum numerantis delictum, Ionæ fuga, & similia.
units.tr: 2. A particular offence is often the cause of a public evil, a prolepsis [προκατάληψιν], as with the sin of David in numbering the people, with Jonah's flight, and with similar cases.

units.la: 3. Ex eo tamen, quòd ob unius noxam multi laborant, non rectè colligi, hosce ἁμαρτωλούς esse, & iniuria affici. Nemo enim est, qui sese iustum esse, uere profiteri possit. Satis est, si quem manu Dei, quæ neminem iniuria afficit, percussum constet: cum Dei, non nostro, aut aliorum hominum, iudicio nobis standum sit.
units.tr: 3. Yet from the fact that many suffer because of one person's offence, it cannot rightly be concluded that these sufferers are sinners and are being wronged. For there is no one who can truly profess himself to be righteous. It is enough if it is clear that a person has been struck by the hand of God, which wrongs no one; for we must abide by God's judgment, not our own or that of other men.

units.la: 4. Cum uerò & rerum naturalium uires, & artificialium fragilitas, executioni iudicij & uindictæ Dei seruiat, quis dubitet illud uerum esse, quod de rerum uniuersiuersitatis obsequio thesis nostra habet?
units.tr: 4. Since both the powers of natural things and the frailty of artificial things serve the execution of God's judgment and vengeance, who would doubt that the thesis we have here, concerning the obedience of the whole created order, is true?

units.la: 5. Vt intelligetiam & fiduciam carnis, stulticiae coarguat Dominus, cùm uentis & fluctibus nauium robur nauigantes oppenant, abillis hoc nonfolùm (cum interest gloriae ipsius)affligi,sed etiam cõteri curare: ut compellat homines ad primae & omnipotentis caussae praesidium implorandum.
units.tr: 5. The Lord rebukes the understanding and confidence of the flesh as foolish, when sailors place the strength of their ships against winds and waves. He wills that they be afflicted by these not only, since it concerns his own glory, but also that they be cared for in other ways, so that he may drive people to implore the protection of the first and almighty cause.

units.la: 6. Nec terra, nec mari, quenquam Dei uindicis manum euitare posse.
units.tr: 6. Neither on land nor at sea can anyone escape the hand of God the avenger.

units.la: 7. In omnibus istis Dei operibus nihil fortuitum esse. Itaq; cùm commoda tempestas obtinet, Dei per gratiam benedicentis beneplacitum: cùm horrida tempestas sæuit, eiusdem maledicentis iudicium adorandum est.
units.tr: 7. Nothing happens by chance in all these works of God. Therefore, when a favourable wind prevails, it is the good pleasure of God, who blesses through grace, that is to be acknowledged; when a dreadful storm rages, the judgment of the same God, who curses, is to be adored.

units.la: 8. Ac proinde memores nos esse debere praeclari illius epiphonematis, Psal. 107.42.43. Videnthæc recti,&lætantur: & omnis iniquitas claudit os suum. Quis sapiens,& obseruabit hęc,&aduertet[illegible, ~6 letters] ad misericordias Iehouae? [illegible, ~3 letters] nomine uoluptatibus ebrios accusat, cap.5.v.12. quòd opus Iehouae non respiciant,nec manuum eius opera uideant.
units.tr: 8. And accordingly we ought to remember that memorable exclamation of Psalm 107:42-43: "The upright see these things and rejoice, and all iniquity shuts its mouth. Who is wise, and will observe these things, and understand the mercies of Jehovah?" [illegible] accuses those who are drunk with pleasures, ch. 5, v. 12, because they do not regard the work of Jehovah, nor see the operation of his hands.

units.la: VERSUS V.
units.tr: VERSE 5.

units.la: Timuerunt igitur nauta, & clamave-runt quisq; ad Deum suum, proiecerunt q;[?] instrumenta qua erant in navi, in mare, ut alleviarent eam ab his. Ionah autem descenderat ad unum e lateribus navis, dormiebatq; & sopore oppressus erat.
units.tr: So the sailors were afraid, and each cried out to his own god. They threw into the sea the cargo that was in the ship, to lighten it of these things. But Jonah had gone down to one of the sides of the ship, and he lay there sleeping, overcome by deep sleep.

units.la: Continet hic versus amplissimam doctrinam de hominum repentino aliquo malo circumventorum perturbationibus, consiliis, actionibus: quae quo quisq; animo sit, egregiè ostendunt. Aristoteles [illegible, ~22 letters] recte affirmat. Nos, cum haec πρακτικά[?] sint, & usitatissima in communi vita, ad institutionē & admonitionem nostram, ea omnia [illegible, ~8 letters] completi studebimus.
units.tr: This verse contains a very full teaching on the agitations, plans and actions of people caught up in some sudden evil, and it clearly shows how each person behaves according to his state of mind. Aristotle [illegible] rightly affirms this. Since these matters are practical and very common in ordinary life, we will strive to take in all of them for our instruction and admonition.

units.la: 1. Quod index est auro, id sunt hominum genere δαιμόνιοι φόβοι, profecti a repetitinis mutationibus. & a summis periculis.
