All these things warn that it often happens that men, led astray by their feelings, act against God while they strive to please and help other men. Two common topics arise in this verse: concerning good intention, and concerning the unhappy fate of those who try either to delay or even to hinder the course and execution of God's judgments.

units.la: DE BONA INTENTIONE.
units.tr: CONCERNING GOOD INTENTION.

units.la: 1. τὰ [illegible, ~8 letters] (his annumero etiam omittenda) referri debent ad certum finem. Sic autem voco actiones interiores & exteriores, quae ad ultimum finem per subordinatos referri debent. Rationes autem eius rei duae in praesentia satisfacere poterunt. Altera est,quòd bonitas actus attenditur in ordine ad finem: ut Scholastici dicere soliti sunt. Altera,quòd homini nihil temere & sine consilio agendum est,aut etiam omittendum.
units.tr: 1. Things (among which I also count those to be left undone) ought to be referred to a certain end [τὰ]. By this I mean both inward and outward actions, which must be referred to the ultimate end through subordinate ends. Two reasons may suffice for the present. The first is that the goodness of an act is judged in relation to its end, as the Schoolmen were accustomed to say. The second is that a man must do nothing rashly and without deliberation, nor leave anything undone in that way.

units.la: 2. Finis autem ille respondere debet consilio & voluntati divinæ in creatione hominis. Ratio: Quia homo Dei caussa conditus est, ut in eo gloria Dei & eiusdem opera,manifesta fierent.
units.tr: 2. This end ought to correspond to the counsel and will of God in the creation of man. The reason: man was created for God's sake, so that in him the glory of God and his works might be made manifest.

units.la: 3. Dei autem consilium & voluntas ex opere Legis & luce fidei petenda est,iuxta hæc dicta: Deut.12.32. Quicquid ego præcipio vobis, custodietis ut faciatis: non addes ei,nec diminues ex eo. Rom. 14.23: Quicquid ex fide non est, peccatum est.
units.tr: 3. The counsel and will of God, however, must be sought from the work of the Law and the light of faith, according to these words: "Whatever I command you, you shall observe to do; you shall not add to it nor take away from it" (Deut. 12.32). "Whatever is not of faith is sin" (Rom. 14.23).

units.la: 4. Quòd si illis duobus, Legi inquam fidei & operum, respodeat intentio, tum demum bona censeri debet.
units.tr: 4. If the intention corresponds to both of these, namely the Law and faith, and works, then at last it ought to be judged good.

units.la: Ratio manifesta est: Quia mens luce Dei fulgens, & voluntas à Spiritu sancto ducta, utitur ministerio inferiorum viriũ ad Dei obsequium, qui ultimus est bonæ intentionis finis.
units.tr: The reason is plain: because a mind shining with the light of God, and a will led by the Holy Spirit, uses the service of the lower powers for the obedience of God, which is the last end of a good intention.

units.la: 5. Neq; verò ab horum ordine, heroici & ardentis Spiritus opera seiungi debet: etsi nostrum non est, sine speciali mandato ea imitari. Notum est illud de Phineës, Psal. 106. 30. Sed adfuit Phinees, & vin dicauit (scelus,) & cohibita est plaga.
units.tr: 5. Nor indeed should the works of a heroic and fervent spirit be separated from this order, although it is not for us to imitate them without a special command. That deed of Phinehas is well known: "But Phinehas stood up and executed judgment (on the wickedness), and the plague was stayed" (Ps. 106.30).

units.la: 31. Et imputatū est ei ad iusticiam, in gene[?] ratione & generatione usq; in seculum.
units.tr: 31. "And it was counted to him for righteousness, throughout all generations, for ever" (Ps. 106.31).

units.la: 6. Cætera non nisi ἰμωνύμως loquendo, bona intētione fieri aut omitti dicimus, cum factorum species diuersæ sunt ab ijs quæ præcepit Dominus: ut ἰϑελοϑρησκείαι [?] Baalitarum & monachorum: vel cum alij modi & fines sunt actionum & omissionum, quàm Deus velit & præceperit.
units.tr: 6. In other cases we speak of things being done or omitted with good intention only equivocally [ὁμωνύμως], when the kind of deed is different from what the Lord commanded, as with the self-chosen worship [ἐθελοθρησκεία] of the Baalites and of the monks; or when the manner and ends of the actions or omissions are other than God wills and has commanded.

units.la: Prioris ordinis olim erant victimæ hū mānæ, Molech aut Saturno oblatæ, [illegible, ~6 letters]- φιλίᾳ [?] quadam Abrahæ ductis idololatris, ut Deo exsecrabilem cultum præstarent. Ad posteriorem ordinem Pfeudoiud-orum sacrificia etiam & Sacrameta, quibus operis operati fiduciam affictam apparet, recte retuleris. Item Missam, ieiu-nia, & multa alia.
units.tr: Of the former kind were once the human sacrifices offered to Moloch or Saturn, led by a certain misguided zeal [φιλίᾳ] like Abraham's, by idolaters, who thought they rendered to God a worship he abhorred. To the latter kind one may rightly refer the sacrifices of the Pseudo-Jews, and also their sacraments, in which it is plain that a false trust in the work done (ex opere operato) is placed. Likewise the Mass, fasts, and many other things.

units.la: 7. Fatendum autem est, etiam Dei filios, ante & post uocationem, intentione (κατά τι)[?] bona peccare, cum uel ignorantia, uel nimia modestia delinquunt.
units.tr: 7. It must be admitted, however, that even the sons of God, both before and after their calling, sin in some respect [κατά τι] with a good intention, when they err through ignorance or through excessive modesty.

units.la: Paulus de seipso adhuc Iudæo testatur, blasphemum, persequutorem & iniuriosum se fuisse, sed ignorantem id fecif-fe, quòd esset fidei expers. 1.Tim.1.13.
units.tr: Paul testifies of himself, while still a Jew, that he had been a blasphemer, a persecutor, and an insolent man, but that he had done it in ignorance, because he lacked faith (1 Tim. 1.13).

units.la: Baptista bona intetione ductus (si sensum infirmitatis suæ & gloriæ Christi spe stes) obnixè prohibebat Christū, dicens: Ego necesse habeo à te baptizari, & tu uenis ad me? Matt.3.14.
units.tr: John the Baptist, moved by good intention (if one understands it as coming from a sense of his own weakness and the hope of Christ's glory), strongly tried to prevent Christ, saying: "I have need to be baptized by you, and do you come to me?" (Matt. 3.14).

units.la: Peccauit uterq;, sed non eodem modo, necijsdem de causis. κατά τι[?] bona fuit intentio Pauli, qui nolebat Iudaicam religionem (quam sibi persuaserat adeò esse ueram & absolutam, nihil ut in ea iure desiderari posset) antiquari: mala autem fuit, quia cum ignorantia coniuncta erat, quæ in blasphemiam & persecutionem erupit. Non erat dignus Ioannes Baptista, qui portare calceos Domino Iesu: sed tamē eius indignitatem non oportuit impedimento esse impletioni omnis iusticiæ, quā defungendum erat Christo.
units.tr: Both sinned, but not in the same way nor for the same reasons. Paul's intention was good in some respect [κατά τι], since he did not want the Jewish religion (which he had persuaded himself was so true and complete that nothing in it could rightly be found wanting) to be abolished; but it was evil, because it was joined with ignorance, which broke out into blasphemy and persecution. John the Baptist was not worthy to carry the shoes of the Lord Jesus; yet his unworthiness ought not to have been an obstacle to the fulfilling of all righteousness, which Christ had to accomplish.

units.la: 8. Vt autem malum sæpe boni quadam specie blanditur: ita nō raro fit, ut τῇ ἀλόγῳ[?] aut errore, fascinati homines, scelera atrocia, bona ut ipsi putant intentione, admittant. Exemplo sunt ij, qui eum pios trucidant, putant se cultum præstare Deo: Ioan.16.2. Item ij qui deuouerant se neque esuros, neque bibituros, usquequo trucidassent Paulum: Act.23.12.
units.tr: 8. Since evil often flatters under the appearance of good, it frequently happens that men, bewitched by irrationality [τῇ ἀλόγῳ] or by error, commit atrocious crimes with what they think is a good intention. Examples are those who kill the godly, thinking they render worship to God (John 16.2). Likewise those who bound themselves neither to eat nor to drink until they had slain Paul (Acts 23.12).

units.la: 9. Minus grauiter peccant, qui humano aliquo affectu, uerbi gratia, nimia indulgentia aut clemetia ducti, delinquunt. Vt qui cum Iona propheta nauigabant, commiseratione quadam erga eum ducti, initio noluerunt eum in mare præcipitare: totisq; uiribus adnisi sunt, ut necessitatem illam declinarent. Etsi autem in eo non deliquerunt, quod eius uices commiserati, uitæ eius rationem habendam iudicauerunt: grauiter tamen peccasse refragando iudicij diuini executio-ni, nihil dubium est.
units.tr: 9. Those sin less gravely who offend out of some human feeling, for instance led by excessive indulgence or mercy. Such were those who sailed with the prophet Jonah: moved by some pity for him, at first they were unwilling to cast him into the sea, and they strained with all their strength to avoid that necessity. Yet although they did not sin in this, that out of pity for him they judged his life should be considered, it is beyond doubt that they sinned gravely by resisting the execution of the divine judgment.

units.la: 10. Cum itaq; operum quoque species intentio non mutet, sic ut ex malis bona faciat: optimum fuerit canonem Apostolicu sequi: ἕκαστος ἐν τῷ ἰδίῳ νοῒ πληροφορέσθω: Vnusquisque in animo suo plene certus esto. Rom.14.5.
units.tr: 10. Since intention does not change the kind of works so as to make bad things good, it would be best to follow the apostolic rule: "Let each one be fully convinced in his own mind" (Rom. 14.5) [ἕκαστος ἐν τῷ ἰδίῳ νοῒ πληροφορέσθω]: let each one be fully certain in his own mind.

units.la: DE INFELICI EORVM LV-sta, qui cursum & executionem iudiciorum Dei seu impedire, seu remorari conantur.
units.tr: On the unhappy lot of those who try either to hinder or to delay the course and execution of God's judgments.

units.la: Vniuersalis experientia Ethnicos docuit, inelu-ctabile fatum esse. Itaque praeclare Persa ille, apud Herodotum in Calliope, dixit: Ξάνι,ὦ,τι ἀεὶ γινέσθαι ἐν τῇ θεῷ, ἀμήχανον ἀποτρέψαι ἀνθρώπῳ. [?]ἀλλ᾽ ἡ πρᾶγμα λέγεται ἰδίλα [?]τε[?]. ταῦτα δὲ πεπρωμένα ἐπιγάμφοι ἐπόμεθα ἀναγκαίῃ ἐν δεδειλέμενοι. ἐχθί-στη δὲ ὁδὸς ἐπὶ τῶν ἐν ἀνθρώποισι αὕτη, πολλὰ φρονέοντα, μηδὲν [?]ὑπ᾽ ἀρετῆς [?].
units.tr: Universal experience has taught the heathen that fate cannot be escaped. So the Persian in Herodotus, Book 7 (Calliope), spoke well: "Indeed, it is impossible for a man to turn aside what God has determined to happen" [Ξάνι, ὦ, τι ἀεὶ γινέσθαι ἐν τῇ θεῷ, ἀμήχανον ἀποτρέψαι ἀνθρώπῳ. [?]ἀλλ᾽ ἡ πρᾶγμα λέγεται ἰδίλα [?]τε[?]. ταῦτα δὲ πεπρωμένα ἐπιγάμφοι ἐπόμεθα ἀναγκαίῃ ἐν δεδειλέμενοι. ἐχθί-στη δὲ ὁδὸς ἐπὶ τῶν ἐν ἀνθρώποισι αὕτη, πολλὰ φρονέοντα, μηδὲν [?]ὑπ᾽ ἀρετῆς [?].]

units.la: Sed in eo grauiter errauerunt Ethnici, quòd fatum, seu uolūtatem diuinam, finxerunt esse causam proximam tum peccatorum, tum poenarum quae comitari solent atrocia delicta: & quòd eius praetextu sunt usi ad hominū scelera excusanda. Falsissima igitur erat Priami deliran-tis ad Helena oratio illa apud Homerū: Οὔτοι
units.tr: But the heathen erred gravely in this: they imagined that fate, or the divine will, was the immediate cause both of sins and of the punishments that usually accompany atrocious crimes, and they used this as a pretext to excuse men's wickedness. Therefore that speech of Priam, raving to Helen in Homer, was utterly false: Οὔτοι [Not you]

units.la: Οὕτοί μοι αἰτίη ἐστὶ, θεοί νυ μοι αἴτιοί εἰσι: Nil tibi ego imputo, uerum ipsis magis imputo diuis.
units.tr: "Not you are the cause for me; the gods are the causes for me" [Οὕτοί μοι αἰτίη ἐστὶ, θεοί νυ μοι αἴτιοί εἰσι]. "I impute nothing to you, but rather I impute it to the gods themselves."

units.la: Rectius Creon apud Sophoclem, fato, quod uolentem ducit, nolentem trahit, non repugnandum monês, ait: ἀνάγκῃ δ᾽ ἐχὶ ἀντιμαχητέον[?].
units.tr: Creon in Sophocles spoke more rightly when, warning that one should not struggle against fate, which drags the unwilling and leads the willing, he said: "one must not fight against necessity" [ἀνάγκῃ δ᾽ ἐχὶ ἀντιμαχητέον].

units.la: Sed ut de specie, id est, de fontium poenis paucis dicam: ordo diuinę iusticiae postulat, ut dent poenas ij qui peccauerunt. Hunc ordinem Deus tolli non uult, ne licentia peccandi concessa, hominum maxima pars ruat in genus omne scelerum.
units.tr: But, to speak briefly of the kind of punishment, that is, of the sources of punishments: the order of divine justice requires that those who have sinned should pay the penalty. God does not wish this order to be abolished, lest, if licence to sin were granted, the greater part of mankind should rush headlong into every kind of wickedness.

units.la: Ae si spectes castigatione filiorum, praeclare Hieronymus: Prouidentia Dei, ait, gubernantur omnia: & quae putatur poena, medicina est. Sed non minus praeclare Cyprianus: Quia, inquit, impunitum non debet esse peccatum, puniatur à te, ne tu pro illo puniaris: peccatum tuum te iudicem habeat, non patronum. De utilitate poenitentiae.
units.tr: And if you look at the chastisement of children, Jerome speaks admirably: "All things are governed by the providence of God, and what is thought to be punishment is medicine." But Cyprian is no less admirable: "Because sin ought not to go unpunished, let it be punished by you, lest you be punished for it; let your sin have you as its judge, not as its advocate." On the Usefulness of Repentance.

units.la: Aliter autè punitur ciuis, aliter hostis: ut Gregorius alicubi dicit, ac certum est, nocentes sic poenas sequi, ut eas euitare non possint. Manum Dei extentam, infirmi homines reducere nunquam possunt: sunt: nec eius de pœnis inferendis decre-tum irritum reddere.
units.tr: A citizen is punished differently from an enemy, as Gregory says somewhere, and it is certain that the guilty are pursued by punishments in such a way that they cannot escape them. Weak men can never draw back the outstretched hand of God, nor render void his decree concerning the infliction of punishments.

units.la: Etsi autem quorunda pœnæ diu differ-runtur, ut Caini, Doegi, Semei, Ahitophe-lis & similium: tamen hæc mora horribi-les malæ conscientiæ cruciatus habet, & tandem sua pœna nocetem consequitur. Et ne quidem ferreus murus (ut ille ait) præpedire potest id quod Deus facere constituit.
units.tr: Although the punishments of some are long deferred, as those of Cain, Doeg, Shimei, Ahithophel and others like them, yet this delay brings the horrible torments of a guilty conscience, and at last the punishment overtakes the wrongdoer. Not even an iron wall (as the saying goes) can hinder what God has determined to do.

units.la: VERSUS XIIII.
units.tr: VERSE 14.

units.la: Clamauerunt itaque ad Iehovam, & dixerunt: Quæsumus Iehovah, ne obsecro pereamus propter animam viri istius, neque ponas super nos sanguinem innocentem: tu enim Iehovah, sicut voluisti, fecisti.
units.tr: Therefore they cried to the LORD and said: We beseech thee, O LORD, let us not perish for this man's life, nor lay upon us innocent blood; for thou, O LORD, hast done as it pleased thee. (Jonah 1:14)

units.la: Cum sententiam Ionæ audivissent, ne Domini Prophetam temere supplicio afficerent, Deum ardentissimis precibus orant, ne se aliud quàm quod ipse decrevisset, exequi permitteret.
units.tr: When they had heard Jonah's sentence, lest they rashly put the prophet of the Lord to death, they beseech God with the most fervent prayers not to permit them to carry out anything other than what he himself had decreed.

units.la: THESIS.
units.tr: THESIS.

units.la: Nemesis in fontium pœnis, non hominum crudelitati & aliis cæcis affectibus, sed Dei voluntati & decreto servire debet. Rationes Thefeos hæ sunt.
units.tr: The vengeance exacted in punishments should serve not the cruelty of men or other blind passions, but the will and decree of God. The reasons for this thesis are these.

units.la: I.
units.tr: I.

units.la: 1. Quia auctoritate diuina, non auté hu mana, nititur dispesatio ut præmiorum, ita etiam pœnarum. Rom.13.4. Dei minister est (magistratus) tuo bono. Quòd si feceris quod malū est, metue: nō enim temerè gladium gestat.nam Dei minister est, ultor ad iram ei, qui quod malum est, fecerit.
units.tr: 1. Because the dispensation of punishments, as of rewards, rests on divine authority, not human. Rom. 13:4: "He is the minister of God to thee for good (the magistrate). But if you do what is evil, fear; for he does not bear the sword in vain; for he is the minister of God, an avenger to execute wrath on him who does evil."

units.la: 2. Quia Deus ideo Legum cancellis potestate ordinis politici circūscripsit, ut ca-nones de voluntate Dei non deessent.
units.tr: 2. Because God, for this reason, has bounded the power of the political order by the limits of laws, so that canons concerning the will of God would not be lacking.

units.la: 3. Quia etiam cūm aliorum, quàm politicorum gubernatorum, ministerio uti-tur, mentes manusq; eorum regit, ut ne extra decreti diuini septum euagentur: ut in hac de Iona propheta historia uidere licet.
units.tr: 3. Because even when he uses the ministry of others than political rulers, he governs their minds and hands, so that they do not wander beyond the fence of the divine decree, as can be seen in this history of the prophet Jonah.

units.la: 4. Quia tranquillitas generis humani turbaretur, si immani bestiæ, id est, perturbationū intēperiei, locus esset in pœnis.
units.tr: 4. Because the tranquillity of the human race would be disturbed if there were room in punishments for a savage beast, that is, the intemperance of the passions.

units.la: 5. Quia certò certius est, perituros eos esse omnes, qui sanguine innocente fundūt: etiāsi nulla humana iudicia metuāt.
units.tr: 5. Because it is more certain than certain that all those will perish who pour out innocent blood, even if they fear no human judgments.

units.la: 6. Quia etiam illud nō dubium est, pœ-nas daturum magistratum, qui nimium indulgens hominibus scelerosis, parci cum non erat parcendum.
units.tr: 6. Because it is also beyond doubt that the magistrate who, indulging wicked men too much, spares where there was no need to spare, will himself give punishment.

units.la: Cùm hoc loco dicatur Deus fecisse sicut voluit: visum mihi est, ad ædificatio-nem & institutionē nostram aliquid ἀλλὰ βραχέων[?] de omnipotentia Dei dicere.
units.tr: Since in this place it is said that God did as he willed, it has seemed to me useful, for our building up and instruction, to say a little concerning the omnipotence of God.

units.la: ESTNE DEI POTENTIA actiua solùm,non etiam passiua?
units.tr: IS THE POWER OF GOD active only, and not also passive?

units.la: Dei potentia actiua tantùm est. Nam Deus est actus infinitus & æternus, essentia simplicissima, ἀσυνθετότατη[?], incommutabilis ἡ ἀπαθὴς.
units.tr: The power of God is active only. For God is infinite and eternal act, of the simplest essence, most uncompounded, unchangeable and impassible.

units.la: QVOMODO DISTINGVI-tur Dei omnipotentia?
units.tr: HOW IS THE OMNIPOTENCE OF GOD distinguished?

units.la: Cum Dei omnipotentia nihil aliud sit, quàm ipsius essentia, quæ simplicissima est & unica: omnipotentia quoq; simplicissima & una est. Distinguitur tamē, propter diuersos respectus, in actualem, qua omnia quæcunq; vult, efficit: & in absolutam, qua infinita alia, quæ nō vult, operari potest.
units.tr: Since the omnipotence of God is nothing other than his essence, which is most simple and one, his omnipotence too is most simple and one. Nevertheless it is distinguished, on account of different respects, into actual, by which he effects all things whatsoever that he wills, and into absolute, by which he can do countless other things that he does not will.

units.la: CONVERTITVR'NE ACTVA-lis omnipotentia cum voluntate Dei?
units.tr: Is actual omnipotence identical with the will of God?

units.la: Maximè. Hoc enim sibi volunt præ-clara hæc testimonia.
units.tr: Most certainly. For these notable testimonies mean exactly this.

units.la: Psal.115.3. Atqui Deus noster est in cœ-lo, & omnia quæ voluit, fecit.
units.tr: Ps. 115.3: But our God is in heaven; whatever he willed, he has done.

units.la: Psal.135.6. Omnia quæcunque uult Ie-houah facit,in cœlis & in terra,in mari & in omnibus abyssis.
units.tr: Ps. 135.6: Whatever Jehovah wills, he does, in heaven and on earth, in the seas and in all the deeps.

units.la: Ionæ 1.14, Tu enim Iehouah, sicut uo-luisti,fecisti,
units.tr: Jonah 1.14: For you, Jehovah, have done as you willed.

units.la: DE CHRISTI OMNIPO-tentia quid credendum est?
units.tr: What must be believed concerning the omnipotence of Christ?

units.la: Rectè dixeris:Christus est omnipotes; Homo Christus est omnipotes:Filius hominis est omnipotens, Quia λόγος & omnipotens est, & ipsa omnipotentia. Assumsit autem λόγος carnem in unionem personæ. De toto itaq; Christo piè illa dicuntur. Aç concretæ uoces sunt Christus, Homo Christus,Filius hominis. Vt ergo hominem rectè dixeris intelligentem,& mortalem: cum tamen respectu quidem mentis, intelligens: respectu autem corporis, mortalis dicatur: ita Christus omnipotens & omnipræsens dicitur, respectu Deitatis,cuius hæc essentialia & quae to modo propria sunt.
units.tr: You may rightly say: Christ is omnipotent; the man Christ is omnipotent; the Son of man is omnipotent. For the Word [λόγος] is omnipotent, and is omnipotence itself, and the Word took on flesh into the unity of person. Those pious statements are therefore made of the whole Christ. Christ, the man Christ, and the Son of man are concrete terms. Just as we rightly call a man understanding and mortal, understanding with respect to his mind and mortal with respect to his body, so Christ is called omnipotent and omnipresent with respect to his Deity, of which these are essential and, in a manner, proper attributes.

units.la: RECTE'NE HUMANITAS CHRI-sti omnipotens dicitur?
units.tr: Is the humanity of Christ rightly called omnipotent?

units.la: Nequaquam. Quia omnipotens rectè proprieq; dicitur is qui natura Deus est, æternus, immensus, conditor uniuerso-rum, rum. Humanitas autem creatura est, initio & spacio circumscripta. Quare recte D.Lutherus eos accusat, qui Christi humanitatem omnipotentem esse fingunt, magis etiam absurde loquentes, quàm si quis corpus humanum fingat esse λογικόμ.
units.tr: By no means. For he is rightly and properly called omnipotent who is by nature God, eternal, immeasurable, and the creator of all things. But the humanity is a creature, bounded by beginning and by space. Hence Luther rightly accuses those who feign that the humanity of Christ is omnipotent, speaking even more absurdly than if someone were to feign that the human body is rational [λογικόν].

units.la: ATQVI CHRISTVS AIT, SIBI datam omnem potestatem in cœlo & in terra, Matt. 28. 18. Est ergo eius humanitas omnipotens.
units.tr: But Christ says that all power in heaven and on earth has been given to him (Matt. 28.18). Therefore his humanity is omnipotent.

units.la: Obsecro te, ut argumenti tui (si hoc nomine dignum est) uitia, semoto praeiudicio, expendas. Sic enim fiet, ut tot fere paralogismis scatere uideas, quot ulcera in Magis Ægyptijs (qui etiam eo nomine coram Mose subsistere non poterant) fuisse dicuntur, Exodi 9. 11. Ita enim illud habet:
units.tr: I beg you, setting prejudice aside, to weigh the faults of your argument (if it deserves the name). For you will see it teeming with almost as many paralogisms as there were sores on the Egyptian magicians, who for that reason could not even stand before Moses (Exod. 9.11). For it runs thus:

units.la: Quaecunq; Christo in tempore data leguntur, ea soli eius humanitati data sunt.
units.tr: Whatever is read as given to Christ in time was given to his humanity alone.

units.la: Ratio Maioris.
units.tr: The major premise.

units.la: Etenim sola humanitas aliquid accipere potuit: Deitas autem non item, cum sit perfectissima, & ἀὐτάρκης πρὸς τὴν ἀνθλαμovlαν,
units.tr: For only the humanity could receive anything; the Deity could not, since it is most perfect and self-sufficient [αὐτάρκης] in respect of [πρὸς τὴν ἀνθλαμovlαν].

units.la: Sed omnis in cœlo & terra potestas Christi Christo in tempore data est:ut ipsemet testatur Matt.28.18.
units.tr: But all power in heaven and on earth was given to Christ in time, as he himself testifies (Matt. 28.18).

units.la: Quare humanitatem Christi esse om-nipotentem, existimandum est.
units.tr: Therefore the humanity of Christ must be thought omnipotent.

units.la: Responsio.
units.tr: Reply.

units.la: 1. Ad Maiorem. Est petitio principii, Christo Iesu nihil datum est, nisi quate-nus Christus est, Mediatoris personam sustinens. Christus autem & Mediator ille est, utriusque naturae respectu: neutra enim natura sola mediatrix est. Quare quaecunq; ei data sunt, toti personae Mediatoris data sunt: cum obid data sint, ut Mediatoris munere posset fungi, non altera è duabus naturis, sed tota persona Immanuelis θεανθρώπου[?].
units.tr: 1. To the major premise: this is a petitio principii. Nothing was given to Jesus Christ except insofar as Christ bears the person of the Mediator. Christ, however, is the Mediator in respect of both natures, for neither nature alone is mediator. Therefore whatever has been given to him has been given to the whole person of the Mediator, since it was given so that he might be able to discharge the office of Mediator, not by one of the two natures but by the whole person of Immanuel, the God-man [θεανθρώπου].

units.la: 2. Ratio Maioris laborat paralogismo à dicto secundum quid ad simpliciter di-stum. Nam ut maxime ἁπλῶς loquendo, λόγος, si eius τὴν ἰδιότητα respicias, nihil accipere possit: cum in eius οὐσίᾳ[?] non cadat παραλλαγὴ[?], ἢ τροπῆς ἀποσκιάσματος, Iac.1.17. ta-men κατὰ τι, ut à Patre exire, in hunc mū-dum venire, in carne patefieri, à Patre mit-ti potuit: sic etiam aliquid accipere, aliquid suum non esse, sed Patris (Matt.20, 23.) profiteri, Patrem mittentem se missa maiorem esse (Ioan.14.28.) agnoscere, facere prout ei mandauit Pater (Ioan.14. 13.) reuera potuit. Ac nequaquam est, cur sycophantice ad Arianismi [illegible, ~12 letters] quisquam nos decurrere fingat, cum aeterni Patris coaeternum filium, essentiae respectu ἀναλλοίωτον[?] profitemur: & haec praedicata non nisi quatenus idem Mediatoris munere fungitur, ei tribuamus. Si quis fallaciam accidetis dicere malit, cum quod de persona officio Mediatoris defungente, orthodoxe dicitur, id sophistice detorquetur ad diuinam naturā, non pugnabimus.
units.tr: 2. The major premise suffers from the fallacy of passing from a statement made in a qualified sense (secundum quid) to one made absolutely (simpliciter). For although, speaking most strictly (ἁπλῶς), the Word could receive nothing with respect to its own property, since no change [παραλλαγή] or shadow of turning [τροπῆς ἀποσκιάσματος] (James 1.17) can fall into its essence [οὐσίᾳ], nevertheless in some respect, as going forth from the Father, coming into this world, being made manifest in the flesh, and being sent by the Father, it truly could receive something. Likewise it could confess that something is not its own but the Father's (Matt. 20.23), acknowledge that the Father who sends is greater than the one sent (John 14.28), and do what the Father commanded (John 14.13). Nor is there any reason why anyone should slyly drive us into Arianism, since we profess the Son to be coeternal with the eternal Father and unchangeable [ἀναλλοίωτον] in essence, and we ascribe these predicates to him only insofar as he discharges the office of Mediator. If someone prefers to call it a fallacy of accident, on the ground that what is said orthodoxly of the person discharging the office of Mediator is sophistically twisted to the divine nature, we will not quarrel.

units.la: 3. Minor ὕπαλος[?] est, propter uomicā aequiuocationis, quae latet in abusu uocabuli Potestas. Cum enim interfit inter ἀνθρώπου[?] & ἐξουσίας, sophistice agunt qui hanc cum illa confundunt. Potestas seu auctoritas, Graece ἐξουσία, officij est propria, & nituriure eo, quod superior in subiectos obtinet. Potentia uero, δύναμις, naturę seu essentiae diuinae propriam in quarto modo, efficiendi uim haec significat. Ac περὶ ἐξουσίας, quam Christus à Patre accepit, ipsemet dicit Ioann.17.2: καθὼς ἔδωκας αὐτῷ ἐξουσίαν πάσης σαρκὸς: Sicut dedisti ei auctoritatem in omnem carnem, ut quot quot dedisti ei, det eis vitam æternam. Matt.28.18: Data est mihi omnis auctoritas in cœlo & in terra. Hanc auctoritatem seu potestatem electis dandi æternam vitam, etsi cum Deus in carne patefactus esset, maximè declarauisse videri potest: tamen inde usque ab initio obtinuisse, ex hisce dictis colligi potest: Iesus Christus heri & hodie idem est & in secula: Hebr.13.8. Item: Agnus ille mactatus jam inde à iactis mundi fundamentis: Apoc.13.8. Nisi omnibus mundi temporibus hac potestate usus esset Mediator ille Dei & hominum, olim incarnandus, nunc vero incarnatus, tum vero nulla fuisset Ecclesia, nec quisquam saluus fieri potuisset.
units.tr: 3. The minor premise is faulty, because of the hidden equivocation in the misuse of the word "power". For there is a difference between human and authority [ἐξουσίας], and those who confuse the one with the other argue sophistically. Authority, or power of office, in Greek ἐξουσία, belongs properly to office and rests on the right which a superior holds over subjects. Power, however, δύναμις, which belongs properly to the nature or essence of God, signifies the force of effecting, in the fourth sense. Concerning the authority which Christ received from the Father, he himself says (John 17.2): "καθὼς ἔδωκας αὐτῷ ἐξουσίαν πάσης σαρκὸς" ("as you gave him authority over all flesh, that he should give eternal life to all whom you have given him"). And Matt. 28.18: "All authority has been given to me in heaven and on earth." Although this authority or power of giving eternal life to the elect may seem to have been most clearly displayed when God was revealed in the flesh, it can nevertheless be gathered from these words that he had possessed it from the beginning: "Jesus Christ is the same yesterday, today, and forever" (Heb. 13.8); and again: "the Lamb slain from the foundation of the world" (Rev. 13.8). Unless that Mediator of God and men, who was to be incarnate in time past and was now incarnate, had used this power in all ages of the world, there would have been no Church then, and no one could have been saved.

units.la: 4. Conclusionem falsam esse, ex præcedentibus quidem liquet: sed nos tamen addemus demonstrationem, ne locus ullus superfit dubitationi.
units.tr: 4. From what has been said above it is clear that the conclusion is false. Yet we will add a demonstration, so that no room is left for doubt.

units.la: Cuicunq; tribuitur omnipotetia Dei ꝑpria in quarto modo, eidē & essentia tri-buitur. Humanę aut in Christo naturę nō tribuitur essentia Dei: quia est & manet creatura, nobis ὁμοούσιος: sicut æternus ὁ λό-γος est [?]yos est Creator, Patri & Spiritui sancto ὁ-μοούσιος. Quare ei non tribuitur, seu de ea non praedicatur omnipotentia. Ne uerò quisquam sinistra accipiat id quod dextera offerimus, repetimus duas saltem enunciationes, quarum prior est orthodoxa: Homo Christus est omnipotens. posterior haeretica est: Humanitas est omnipotens. Hominis enim uocabulum Personam denotat: humanitatis uerò naturam assumtam, quae est semen Abrahae & Dauidis. Valde autem & hortor & o-ro studiosos ueritatis, ne sibi fucum fieri patiantur confusione uocabulorum con-cretorum & abstractorum, sub qua non-nullos uelut sub Aiacis clypeo delitesce-re uidemus. Dominum oro, ne patiatur lucem ueritatis in cordibus nostris accensam exstingui, & ut errantes in viam re-uocare dignetur.
units.tr: Whoever is properly attributed the omnipotence of God in the fourth sense is attributed the essence of God as well. But the essence of God is not attributed to the human nature of Christ, since it is and remains a creature, homoousios with us [ὁμοούσιος]; whereas the eternal Word, who is Creator, is homoousios with the Father and the Holy Spirit. Therefore omnipotence is not attributed to it, nor is it predicated of it. Lest anyone take amiss what we offer with the right hand, let us repeat at least two statements, of which the first is orthodox: "The man Christ is omnipotent." The second is heretical: "The humanity is omnipotent." For the word man denotes the Person, but the word humanity denotes the assumed nature, which is the seed of Abraham and David. I earnestly urge and beg those who love the truth not to allow themselves to be deceived by the confusion of concrete and abstract terms, under which some hide as under the shield of Ajax. I pray the Lord not to suffer the light of truth kindled in our hearts to be extinguished, and to deign to call back the erring into the way.

units.la: VERSVS XV.
units.tr: VERSVS XV.

units.la: Tulerunt ergo Ionam, & proiecerunt eum in mare: constititq; mare ab ira sua.
units.tr: So they took Jonah and threw him into the sea, and the sea ceased from its raging.

units.la: THESIS I.
units.tr: THESIS I.

units.la: Etsi sontium afflictiones non λύτρα[?], sed τιμωρίαι sunt: tamen cum seruiunt gloriae Dei, etiam publica mala mitigantur aut toltolluntur.iuxta hæc dicta:
units.tr: Although the afflictions of the guilty are not ransoms [λύτρα], but punishments [τιμωρίαι], yet when they serve the glory of God, even public evils are softened or removed. According to these words:

units.la: 1.Petr.4.15. Ne quis vestrûm affliga-tur ut homicida, aut fur, aut maleficus, aut alienarum rerum inspector. Hoc di-ctum proprie loquitur de maleficorum, qui delicta atrocia, turbantia tranquillita-tem generis humani, admiserunt, poenis, quas τιμωρίας [?] vocant.
units.tr: 1 Pet. 4.15. Let none of you suffer as a murderer, or a thief, or an evildoer, or as a meddler in other men's affairs. This saying properly speaks of the punishments of evildoers who committed atrocious crimes that disturb the peace of the human race, which the Greeks call punishments [τιμωρίας].

units.la: Deut.21.8.Et expiabitur ab eis sanguis.
units.tr: Deut. 21.8. And blood shall be expiated by them.

units.la: Num.35.33. Et ita non polluetis terrâ in qua fueritis, quia sanguis iste polluet terrâ: neq; terra expiabitur propter sanguinem qui effusus est in ea, nisi per sanguinem illius qui effudit eum.
units.tr: Num. 35.33. So you shall not pollute the land in which you are, for blood pollutes the land; and the land cannot be expiated of the blood shed in it, except by the blood of the one who shed it.

units.la: Obiectio.
units.tr: Objection.

units.la: Expiatio &λύτρον uni & eidem tribu-untur: ut vel ex Christi Jesu Domini nostri exemplo liquet.
units.tr: Expiation and ransom [λύτρον] are ascribed to one and the same thing, as is clear even from the example of Christ Jesus our Lord.

units.la: Sed in illo testimonio Num.35.33. sanguini homicidæ legitimè fuso tribuitur expiatio.
units.tr: But in that testimony, Num. 35.33, expiation is ascribed to the blood of a murderer lawfully shed.

units.la: Quare eidem tribui debet, quòd sit λύτρον: & per cōsequens, falsa est altera pars theseos superioris.
units.tr: Therefore it must be ascribed to the same thing, namely that it is a ransom; and consequently the other part of the thesis above is false.

units.la: Respondeo esse paralogismū ὁμωνυμίας [?] in vocabulo Expiationis: quod in Maio-re [?] significat spirituale donum, videlicet ablutioablutionem à peccatis, per aspersionem sanguinis Christi in Minore significat ciuile opus, quo satisfit legi de poenis homicidarum. Vult enim Deus e medio tolli homicidas uoluntarios, latrones, & alios turbantes societatem generis humani atrocibus sceleribus.
units.tr: I answer that there is a paralogism of equivocation [ὁμωνυμία] in the word expiation. In the major premise it signifies a spiritual gift, namely the washing away of sins through the sprinkling of Christ's blood; in the minor premise it signifies a civil act by which satisfaction is made to the law concerning the penalties of murderers. For God wills that voluntary murderers, robbers, and others who disturb the society of mankind by atrocious crimes be removed from the midst.

units.la: THESIS II.
units.tr: THESIS II.

units.la: In sanctorum lapsus sic animaduertit Deus, ut afflictio diuerso respectu & τιμω-ρία sit, & ἀνομία. Τιμωρία est, quia peccata sic ulciscitur Dominus: ἀνομία, quia emēdat [?], & in uiam suos hoc pacto idem reuocat. Exemplo est Ionas, quem ut maxime demus grauissimè deliquisse: faci-norosis tamen nequaquam annumerabi-mus. Eius itaq; afflictio poena erat inobedientiæ, & castigatio qua reuocadus erat ad obedientiam, in legatione apud Nini uitas obeunda Deo probandam.
units.tr: In the lapses of the saints God so takes note that the affliction is, in different respects, both a punishment [τιμωρία] and an amendment [ἀνόρθωσις]. It is a punishment, because the Lord thus avenges sins; it is an amendment, because by this means he corrects and brings his people back to the way. Jonah is an example. Although we grant that he sinned most grievously, we will by no means count him among criminals. His affliction, therefore, was the punishment of his disobedience and a chastisement by which he was to be recalled to obedience, so that he might prove himself in carrying out his commission from God at Nineveh.

units.la: Et nostra πάθηματα σύμμιξα [?] esse ne dubitemus, cum & peccatorum poenas luamus, & paterna Dei ferula ad officium faciedum adigamur. Ac nisi Dominus pro sua erga nos bonitate, castigando efficeret, ut πάθηματα nobis μαθήματα sint, nunquam nō nobis ipsis blandiremur etiam in multiplicibus erratis & peccatis. Sed be-ne habet, quòd nos quoq; castigat dili-gens, & flagellat recipiens. Heb.12.6.
units.tr: Nor should we doubt that our own sufferings [πάθηματα] are of this kind, since we both pay the penalties of our sins and are driven by the fatherly rod of God to do our duty. And unless the Lord, out of his goodness toward us, by chastising brings it about that our sufferings [πάθηματα] become lessons [μαθήματα] for us, we would never cease to flatter ourselves, even in our manifold errors and sins. But it is well that the Lord, who is diligent, also chastises us, and scourges every son whom he receives. Heb. 12.6.

units.la: Exempla animaduersionis diuinæ in sanctorum [?]
units.tr: Examples of divine punishment in the saints.

units.la: Mosi dixit Iehouah: Morere in monte, &c. Eo quòd præuaricati estis in me, in medio filiorum Israelis ad Aquas iurgij Cades deserti Sin, eo quòd non sanctifi-castis me in medio filiorum Israelis. E're gione quidem uidebis terram: sed illuc nō ingredieris ad terram illam, quam do filijs Israel. Deut.32.51.52.53.
units.tr: Jehovah said to Moses: Die on the mountain, etc. Because you trespassed against me among the children of Israel at the waters of strife at Kadesh in the wilderness of Zin, because you did not sanctify me among the children of Israel. Over against you you shall see the land, but you shall not enter there, into the land which I give to the children of Israel. Deut. 32.51–53.

units.la: Adulterium & homicidiū Dauidis, seditione Israelitarum, cædefiliorum, pollutione quarundam coniugum Regis, ultus est Deus.
units.tr: God avenged David's adultery and murder, the sedition of the Israelites, the slaughter of his sons, and the defilement of certain wives of the king.

units.la: Ezechiæ, quòd opes suas oftentasset Legatis Babylonici Regis, denuciata est captiuitas Babylonica, excidium Hierosolymæ, & triste fatum Regiæ familiæ.
units.tr: Because Hezekiah displayed his riches to the envoys of the Babylonian king, the Babylonian captivity, the destruction of Jerusalem, and the sad fate of the royal house were foretold.

units.la: THESIS III.
units.tr: THESIS III.

units.la: Deus etiam in medijs ærumnis & afflictionibus, ipsaq; adeò morte, seruos suos glorificat. Cum prædictioni Ionæ de maris tempestate sedanda, ipso iam in mare proiecto, responderet euentus, animaduer-
units.tr: God glorifies his servants even in the midst of troubles and afflictions, even in death itself. When the outcome answered Jonah's prediction that the storm at sea would be calmed, though he had already been cast into the sea, it was observed

units.la: sum fuit non esse ψευδοπροφήτην[?]: sed Iehouæ afflatu de re tanta edoctum, illam religiosè uereq; prænunciauisse. Ac quòd eundem maiorem alienæ, quàm suæ incolumitatis rationem habuisse uiderent, non potuerunt non admirari uirtutem & humanitatem tanti uiri.
units.tr: that he was not a false prophet, but had been taught about such a great matter by the inspiration of Jehovah, and had foretold it religiously and truly. And because they saw that he had regarded the safety of others more than his own, they could not but admire the virtue and humanity of so great a man.

units.la: Vtinam uerò ipsi quoq; admirãda Dei opera intuentes, discamus ὅτι ἰδίᾳ [?] ... αὐτῷ τινὸς ἀγγελίας [?], ac moderatè & eleganter aduersos casus feramus, nunquàm non repetentes illud propheticum: Iram Iehoue portabo, quia peccaui illi. Mich. 7.9.
units.tr: Would that we too, looking upon the wonderful works of God, might learn [ὅτι ἰδίᾳ ... αὐτῷ τινὸς ἀγγελίας], and bear adverse events calmly and gracefully, always repeating that prophetic word: I will bear the wrath of Jehovah, because I have sinned against him. Mic. 7.9.

units.la: THESIS IIII.
units.tr: THESIS IIII.

units.la: Ionas Christi typus fuit, ut ex hac collatione liquet.
units.tr: Jonah was a type of Christ, as this comparison makes clear.

units.la: 1. Ionas propheta ab Ethnicis hominibus iudicatus, & in mare præcipitatus fuit. Iesus Christus traditus est in manus Gentium, passus sub Pontio Pilato.
units.tr: 1. Jonah the prophet was condemned by heathen men and thrown headlong into the sea. Jesus Christ was delivered into the hands of the Gentiles and suffered under Pontius Pilate.

units.la: 2. Iona in mare proiecto, sedata est tempestas, & seruati sunt qui in naui erant, & in optatum portu deducti. Iesu Christo pro nobis crucifixo & resuscitato, sedata est æterni Patris ira: idq; perfectum, ut Ecclesia enauigato huius uitæ Oceano, certò fit appulsura in cœlestis nostræ patriæ optatissimo portu.
units.tr: 2. When Jonah was cast into the sea, the storm was calmed, and those who were in the ship were saved and brought into the desired harbour. When Jesus Christ was crucified and raised again for us, the anger of the eternal Father was appeased; and this was accomplished so that the Church, having sailed across the ocean of this life, will surely be brought to the most desired harbour of our heavenly fatherland.

units.la: In eo tamen magna dissimilitudo est. 1. Ionas enim offensæ fuę[?] poenas dedit: Christus Iesus innocens pro nobis, qui rei eramus, passus est. iuxta dictum: Deus Pater fecit, ut is qui non nouit peccatum, pro nobis peccatum esset, ut nos efficeremur iustitia Dei in eo. 2. Cor. 5. 21.
units.tr: There is, however, a great dissimilarity here. 1. Jonah paid the penalty for his own offence; Christ Jesus, innocent, suffered for us who were guilty, according to the saying: God the Father made him who knew no sin to be sin for us, so that in him we might become the righteousness of God. 2 Cor. 5.21.

units.la: 2. Ionæ afflictio erat τιμωρία[?] inobedientiæ, Christi perpessio λύτρων[?] & expiatio peccatorum nostrorum.
units.tr: 2. Jonah's affliction was the punishment [τιμωρία] of disobedience; Christ's suffering was a ransom [λύτρων] and the expiation of our sins.

units.la: DE SANCTORVM AF-flictionibus.
units.tr: On the Afflictions of the Saints.

units.la: Cum nemo nostrum in rebus aduersis sibi non aliqua saltem ratione blandiatur, dum præter meritum durius secum agi putat & queritur, ut maximè reatum communem agnoscat & fateatur: operæprecium fuerit, fucum quo nobis ipsis imponimus, detergere. Atq; id à nobis præstari poterit, si hæc omnia perpenderimus. Primùm, afflictiones istas, quæ nos exercèt, à Deo proficisci. Deinde, earum non unam esse speciem, nec diuersas afflictionum species nobis esse confundedas. Postremò, non minore exaduersis, quàm è rebus secundis, utilitate ad nos redire.
units.tr: Since none of us, in adverse circumstances, fails to flatter himself in some way, when he thinks he is treated more harshly than he deserves and complains, it will be worth our while to strip away the pretence by which we deceive ourselves, and above all to acknowledge and confess our common guilt. This we can accomplish if we weigh the following points. First, that the afflictions which exercise us proceed from God. Second, that they are not all of one kind, and that we must not confuse the different kinds of affliction. Last, that adversity brings us no less profit than prosperity.

units.la: 1. Initiò occurrendum nobis est errori Epicureo, qui fingit Deo connivente adversa nobis evenire ac[?] firmiter statuendum est, adversa esse ἀπόπεμπτα[?]. Ubi hoc nobis persuasum fuerit, primùm non pecabimus fremitu adversus Dei iudicium: multum sanè ijs dissimiles, qui canes (lapides quibus læsi sunt mordentes) imitantur, & proximas calamitatum suarum causas, homines videlicet sibi infensos, hostiliter oderunt & infestantur: deinde, non dubitabimus præcipuo nostro bono nos affligi, cū Dei cōfilio affligamur. Nō ta sunt pijs omnib. præclara hæc oracula.
units.tr: 1. First we must meet the error of Epicurus, who imagines that adversities befall us with God looking on indifferently; and we must hold firmly that adversities are sent by God. Once this has been persuaded upon us, first, we shall not sin by raging against the judgment of God. We shall be very unlike those who imitate dogs, biting the stones by which they were struck, and who bitterly hate and attack the nearest causes of their calamities, namely men who are hostile to them. Second, we shall not doubt that we are afflicted for our chief good, since we are afflicted by the counsel of God. These splendid oracles are not equally sweet to all the godly.

units.la: Iob.2.10. Bonum suscipiemus à Deo, & malum non suscipiemus?
units.tr: Job 2.10. Shall we receive good at the hand of God, and shall we not receive evil?

units.la: Eccl.7.15. In die bono, esto in bono: & in die mala, uide: etiam hanc è regione illius fecit Deus.
units.tr: Eccl. 7.15. In the day of prosperity be in good case, but in the day of adversity consider: God also has made the one over against the other.

units.la: Thren.3.37. Quis igitur est qui dixit, & fuit, & Dominus non præcepit? 38. Aut si ex ore altissimi non egredientur bona & mala?
units.tr: Lam. 3.37. Who is he who has spoken and it has come to pass, when the Lord has not commanded it? 38. Do not good and evil proceed from the mouth of the Most High?

units.la: Matth.10.30. Vestri verò etiam capilli capitis omnes numerati sunt. 31. Ne igi-tur timueritis: multis passerculis præsta-tis vos.
units.tr: Matt. 10.30. But the very hairs of your head are all numbered. 31. Fear not therefore: you are of more value than many sparrows.

units.la: 2. Sunt etiam nobis afflictionum formae distinguendae, ne earum confusione nobis ipsis imponamus, & malis nostris mala addamus.
units.tr: 2. The forms of affliction must also be distinguished, lest by confusing them we deceive ourselves and add evils to our evils.

units.la: Τιμωρία est, cum ob peccata in nos animadvertit Deus, morbis, egestate, contumeliis, quòd ualetudinem, facultates opum, nomen laudatum, nobis ipsis potius, quàm sibi, tribuere uideat. Facit huc illud oraculum: Et ipsa nesciebat, quòd ego ei dedissem frumentum, uinum & oleum: imò argentum quod ego multiplicaueram ei, & aurum fecerūt in Baal. Idcirco conuertar, & sumam frumentū meum tempore suo, & uinum meum tempore suo: auferamq; lanam meam, &c. Hos.2.8.9.
units.tr: Punishment (τιμωρία) is when God, on account of sins, takes vengeance upon us with sickness, want, and reproaches, because he sees us attributing health, wealth of goods, and praised reputation to ourselves rather than to him. To this belongs that oracle: "And she did not know that I had given her grain, wine and oil; indeed the silver which I had multiplied for her, and the gold, they made into Baal. Therefore I will turn back and take away my grain in its time, and my wine in its time, and I will take away my wool," etc. Hos. 2.8, 9.

units.la: Δοκιμασία[?] est, cum non tam ob reatum aliquem nos punit, quàm ut ad gloriam suam & aliorum aedificationem, periculum faciat nostrae fidei, constantiae, patientiae, nos aduersis castigat Dominus. Nouit enim, nos in rebus aduersis obedientiam fidei, & multas alias egregias uirtutes, multò magis declarare, quàm in secundis, quae fere reddunt securos, & minus promtos ad preces, ad gratiarū actio nes, & alia uerae pietatis exercitia. iuxta dictu: Priusquam humiliarer, ego errabam; nunc autem praecepta tua custodio. Item: Bonum est mihi Domine, quòd humiliasti me, ut discere iustificationes tuas: Psal.119. Meminerimus autem etiam in hoc afflictionum genere, cum cor nostrum non accusat nos, συκοφαντοῦντας[?] uidelicet de iustificatione nostri, tamen agnoscendas esse peccatorum carnis nostrae sordes. Summ-mittamus itaque nos ipsos potenti manui Dei, ut nos in tempore attollat. 1.Pet.5.6.
units.tr: Trial (δοκιμασία) is when the Lord chastises us with adversities not so much because of some guilt, but in order to test our faith, constancy and patience, for his own glory and the edification of others. For he knows that in adversity he can display the obedience of faith and many other excellent virtues far more than in prosperity, which mostly makes men secure and less ready for prayers, thanksgivings, and other exercises of true piety; according to the saying: "Before I was humbled I went astray, but now I keep your precepts." Likewise: "It is good for me, O Lord, that you have humbled me, that I may learn your statutes." Ps. 119. We must remember also in this kind of affliction that, although our heart does not accuse us (namely of slandering our justification), we must nevertheless acknowledge the filth of the sins of our flesh. Let us therefore humble ourselves under the mighty hand of God, that he may lift us up in due time. 1 Pet. 5.6.

units.la: Μαρτύριον est, cum nos uult ob ueritatis testimonium nō modò obnoxios esse ca-lumniis ἐν τῇ θυμομαχίᾳ[?] falsorum fratrum, sed etiam facultates terrenas, cognatos & domesticos deserere, sanguinem denique & uitam profundere. Huc facit illud Petri Apostoli dictum: Sed si ut Chri-stianus affligitur, ne pudefiat: imô glorificet Deum in hac parte. Nam tempus est, quo incipiat iudicium a domo Dei. quod si primum incipit a nobis, quis erit finis eorum qui non parét Dei Euangelio? Et, si iustus vix seruatur, impius & peccator ubi comparebit? Itaque qui affligitur ex voluntate Dei, tanquam fideli conditori commencommendent animas suas benefaciendo. 1.Pet.4.16.17.18.19.
units.tr: Martyrdom (μαρτύριον) is when he wills that we be exposed not only to the calumnies of the false brethren, raging in their anger, for the testimony of the truth, but also that we forsake our earthly goods, kin and household, and at last pour out our blood and life. To this belongs the saying of the apostle Peter: "But if anyone suffers as a Christian, let him not be ashamed, but let him glorify God in this respect. For the time has come for judgment to begin at the house of God; and if it begins first with us, what will be the end of those who do not obey the gospel of God? And if the righteous is scarcely saved, where will the ungodly and the sinner appear?" Therefore let those who suffer according to the will of God commend their souls to a faithful Creator, in well-doing. 1 Pet. 4.16–19.

units.la: Quis dubitet affirmare, incruētum & diuturnum esse hac aetate eorum martyrium, quibus cum tot haereseon monstris nunquam non est depugnandum? Stant quidem illi in prima aduersus Antichristum acie, & multis annis fortiter pugnando bene meriti sunt de tota Ecclesia. Et tamé à Cadmaeis fratribus ueneratae linguae spiculis & dentata charta hostiliter confodiuntur.
units.tr: Who would doubt to affirm that in our age the martyrdom of those is bloodless and long-lasting, who must always fight with so many monsters of heresies? Indeed they stand in the front line against Antichrist, and by fighting bravely for many years they have deserved well of the whole Church. And yet they are hostilely pierced by the darts of the tongue and by the toothed paper of the Cadmean brethren.

units.la: 3. Porrò, cum non raro maiorem ex aduersis, quàm ex secundis, utilitatem percipiamus, in aduersis gloriari nos conueniebat, cum sciamus quòd oppressio patientiam efficiat, patientia uero experientiam, experientia autem spem non pudefacientem, eo quòd charitas Dei effusa sit in cordibus nostris per Spiritum sanctum. Rom.5.3.4.5.
units.tr: 3. Moreover, since we not seldom receive greater profit from adversities than from prosperities, we ought to glory in adversities, since we know that tribulation works patience, patience experience, and experience hope, which does not disappoint, because the love of God is poured out in our hearts through the Holy Spirit. Rom. 5.3, 4, 5.

units.la: VERSVS XVI.
units.tr: VERSE 16.

units.la: Timuerunt aute uiri illi timore ingenti Iehouam, & immolauerunt hostiam Iehoa- uaë uouerunt̄q; uota.
units.tr: Those men feared Jehovah with a great fear, and offered a sacrifice to Jehovah, and made vows.

units.la: Pœnas publicas & priuatas, earumq; mitigationem, conuersio ad Deum verū, solennis gratiarū actio, & alij fructus Spiritus, sequi debent. Loquor iam de ijs, quibus resipiscetiae donum largitur Deus: non de τοῖς ἀμετανοήτοις[?], qui malis deteriores fiunt. Iuxta illud Pauli dictū: Ecce enim istuc ipsum, quòd secūdum Deum tristicia affecti fuistis, quantum in vobis effecit studium? imò defensione, imò indignationem, imò timore, imò vehemes desiderium, imò zelum, imò vindicationem? per omnia testatum fecistis, vos esse puros in hoc negocio. 2.Cor.7.11.
units.tr: Public and private punishments, and their mitigation, conversion to the true God, a solemn thanksgiving, and the other fruits of the Spirit ought to follow. I am now speaking of those to whom God grants the gift of repentance, not of those who are unrepentant [ἀμετανοήτοις] and grow worse through their evils. In accordance with Paul's saying: "For behold, this very thing, that you were grieved according to God, what earnestness it worked in you, what defence, what indignation, what fear, what vehement desire, what zeal, what vindication! In every way you have shown yourselves to be pure in this matter." 2 Cor. 7:11.

units.la: Celebrantur autem hoc loco hæc tria. Primò, ingens Iehovæ timor: secundò, sa cra λατρεία: postremò, religiosa vita.
units.tr: Three things are celebrated in this place. First, a great fear of Jehovah; second, sacred worship [λατρεία]; last, a religious life.

units.la: DE TIMORE IEHOVAE.
units.tr: On the Fear of Jehovah.

units.la: Cum timor Iehovæ[?] caput sapientiæ sit, Psal.111.10. equidem mihi persuadeo, istos homines vocatos ad agnitione veri Dei, quæ à reverentia erga eundem non potest seiungi. Non enim idola, sed Iehovam summè timuisse seu reveritos esse, dicitur. Movit autem eos iusticiæ iudicij divini declaratio erga tantum virū, ut Iohouam iudicium à domo sua incoantem sibi reuerendum iudicarent. Idem sanè elogium tribuitur Cornelio centurioni,cum dicitur: εὐσεβὴς[?] καὶ φοβούμενος τὸν θεόν[?]. Act.10.2.
units.tr: Since the fear of Jehovah is the beginning of wisdom (Ps. 111:10), I am fully persuaded that these men, called to the knowledge of the true God, which cannot be separated from reverence towards him, feared and reverenced Jehovah, not idols. For it is said that they greatly feared Jehovah. Indeed, the declaration of the justice of the divine judgment against so great a man moved them to judge that Jehovah, who was bringing judgment upon his house, was to be revered. The same commendation is given to the centurion Cornelius, where it is said: "devout and fearing God" [εὐσεβὴς καὶ φοβούμενος τὸν θεόν] (Acts 10:2).

units.la: Expendant autem studiosi iuuenes hoc de timore Dei dictum. De Mesia benedicto dicitur Isa.11.2. Et requiescet super eum Spiritus Iehouae, Spiritus sapie-tiae & intelligentiae, Spiritus fortitudinis & consilij, Spiritus scientiae & timoris Iehouae. Ex hoc dicto colligimus: 1. Spiritui sancto accepta fereda esse χαρίσματα[?]. 1.Cor. 12.8. 2. E plenitudine Christi nos omnes accipere gratia pro gratia. Ioan.1.17. 3. Saepius in eodem homine varia Spiritus sancti χαρίσματα[?] iungi. 4. Cum timore Iehouae coniungi eiusdem scientiam, quemadmodum antea quoque exemplo adducto ostendi.
units.tr: Let studious young people consider what is said here about the fear of God. Of the blessed Messiah it is said (Isa. 11:2): "And the Spirit of Jehovah shall rest upon him, the Spirit of wisdom and understanding, the Spirit of counsel and might, the Spirit of knowledge and of the fear of Jehovah." From this saying we gather: (1) that gifts [χαρίσματα] are rightly attributed to the Holy Spirit (1 Cor. 12:8); (2) that we all receive grace for grace from the fullness of Christ (John 1:17); (3) that various gifts [χαρίσματα] of the Holy Spirit are often joined together in the same person; (4) that knowledge of the same Spirit is joined with the fear of Jehovah, as I showed before by the example adduced.

units.la: Obiectio.
units.tr: Objection.

units.la: Rom.11.20. dicitur:Ne effertor animo, sed time. Ergo non modò τῶν[?] ἐφ' ἡμῖν[?] est timere Deum: sed etiam dubitationi de salute locus aliquis est.
units.tr: It is said in Romans 11:20: "Do not be proud, but fear." Therefore it is not only in our power to fear God, but there is also some room for doubt about salvation.

units.la: Respondeo: primùm, è praecepto non rectè colligi facultatem praestandi: cum illud,quid à nobis requirat Deus, nō quid uiribus humanis post lapsum præstari possit, testetur. Alloquitur autem Deus tales, quales ipse olim creauit. Ac si con sideres statum in quo nunc sunt homines, meditari oportet illud D. Augustini: Det Deus quod iubet, & iubeat quod uult.
units.tr: I answer: first, it is not rightly inferred from a command that there is ability to perform it, since the command shows what God requires of us, not what can be performed by human strength after the fall. God, however, addresses such people as he originally created them. If you consider the state in which men now are, one should meditate on the saying of Augustine: "Let God give what he commands, and let him command what he wills."

units.la: Porrò, cum nos timere uult Apostolus, carnalem securitatem improbat, nō fidei πληροφορίαν[?] de nostra salute, tollit.
units.tr: Moreover, when the Apostle wills that we fear, he rejects carnal security; he does not take away the full assurance [πληροφορία] of faith concerning our salvation.

units.la: DE SACRA VORVM λειτουργία[?]
units.tr: On the Sacred Service [λειτουργία] of the Sacrifices.

units.la: Σωτήρια[?] obtulerunt Iehouae, à quo solo se seruatos esse uidebant. Erant autem σωτήρια[?] sacrificia εὐχαριστικά[?], quae Seruatori Deo gratitudinis ergò ab ijs qui se diui nitùs seruatos esse uidebát, offerebantur.
units.tr: They offered salvation offerings [σωτήρια] to Jehovah, by whom alone they saw themselves to have been saved. Now the salvation offerings were thank offerings, which were offered to God the Saviour, for gratitude, by those who saw themselves divinely saved.

units.la: Noah ex arca egressus, σωτήρια[?] Iehouae obtulit. Gen.8.20[?] Ædificauit Noah altare ipsi Iehouae, tulitq; ex omni animali mundo, & ex omni volatili mundo, obtulitq; in altari illo holocausta. 21. Odoratusq; est Iehouah odore quietis, dixitq; Iehouah in corde suo: Non addam ut maledicam terrae propter hominem, &c.
units.tr: Noah, coming out of the ark, offered salvation offerings to Jehovah (Gen. 8:20). "Noah built an altar to Jehovah himself, and took of every clean animal and of every clean bird, and offered burnt offerings on that altar. And Jehovah smelled the sweet savour, and Jehovah said in his heart: I will not again curse the ground for man's sake, etc." (Gen. 8:21).

units.la: Iacob Patriarcha redux è Mesopotamia σωτηρία[?] obtulit Iehouæ. Genes.35.7. Ædificauit ibi altare, uocauitq; locum El Beth-el: quia ibi apparuerat ei Deus, cū fugeret à facie fratris sui Esau.
units.tr: Jacob the patriarch, returning from Mesopotamia, offered a salvation offering [σωτηρία] to Jehovah (Gen. 35:7). He built there an altar and called the place El-Beth-el, because God had appeared to him there when he was fleeing from the face of his brother Esau.

units.la: Quæ sunt Christianorum sacrificia Eucharistica?
units.tr: What are the Eucharistic sacrifices of Christians?

units.la: 1. Δοξολογία[?] & gratiarum actio pro beneficijs diuinis. Hebr.13.15. Per ipsum igitur assiduè offeramus Deo sacrificiū laudis, id est, fructum labiorum confitentium nomini eius.Redemtionis enim nostræ, per Christū partæ & peractæ, beneficiū semper nobis grata memoria recolendum, ut nunquā nō agamus Deo gratias,
units.tr: 1. Doxology [δοξολογία] and thanksgiving for divine benefits (Heb. 13:15). Therefore through him let us continually offer to God the sacrifice of praise, that is, the fruit of lips confessing his name. For the benefit of our redemption, obtained and accomplished through Christ, must always be recalled with grateful memory, so that we never cease to give thanks to God.

units.la: 2. Beneficentia erga pios egenos & oppressos. Eodem cap.uers.16. Beneficen-tiæ uerò & communicationis ne obliuiscimini: talibus enim uictimis delecta-tur Dominus. Prouerb.21.3. Facere iu-sticiā & iudiciū, magis placet Deo quàm sacrificium.
units.tr: 2. Beneficence towards godly needy and oppressed people. In the same chapter, verse 16: "But do not forget to do good and to share, for with such sacrifices the Lord is pleased." Prov. 21:3: "To do justice and judgment is more acceptable to God than sacrifice."

units.la: 3. Sese totum Deo consecrare, ac sum-mo studio obediedi Deo flagrare. Rom. 12.1. Precor igitur uos, fratres, per miserationes Dei, ut sistatis corpora uestra hostiam uiuam, sanctam, acceptam Deo, rationalem illum cultum uestrum,
units.tr: 3. To consecrate oneself wholly to God, and to burn with the highest zeal to obey God. Rom. 12:1: "I beseech you therefore, brethren, by the mercies of God, that you present your bodies a living sacrifice, holy, acceptable to God, which is your reasonable service."

units.la: Quia non satis est homini fideli, cum recens est sensus divinæ liberationis & accepti beneficij, gratitudinem Deo seruatori probasse: non dubitat religioso, de perpetua gratitudine & obedientia, voto sese obstringere. Adhibuit autem vetustas non raro sacrificia anniversaria, ad recolendam memoriam divinorum beneficiorum, ut ex hisce dictis colligere licet. Psal.50.23. Qui sacrificat Iehouæ laudem, is demum glorificat me: qui viam disponit, ostendam ei salutem Dei. Eodem Psalmo, verf.14. Sacrifica Deo laudes, & redde Excelso vota tua. 15. Et invoca me in die tribulationis, & eruam te, & glorificabis me. Psal.66.13. Veniam domum tuam cum holocaustis: persoluam tibi vota mea: 14. Quæ protulerunt labia mea, & os meum locutum est in afflictione mea: 15. Holocausta pinguium offeram tibi cum suffitu arietum: iuuencos & hircos tibi sacrificare instituí.
units.tr: Because it is not enough for a faithful man, when the sense of divine deliverance and of a received benefit is fresh, to have shown gratitude to God the Saviour, he does not hesitate to bind himself by a vow to perpetual gratitude and obedience in religious devotion. Antiquity often used annual sacrifices to recall the memory of divine benefits, as may be gathered from these sayings. Ps. 50:23: "Whoever offers praise sacrifices to Jehovah, he glorifies me; and to him who orders his way aright I will show the salvation of God." In the same psalm, verse 14: "Offer to God praises, and pay your vows to the Most High. 15. And call upon me in the day of trouble, and I will deliver you, and you shall glorify me." Ps. 66:13: "I will come into your house with burnt offerings; I will pay you my vows, 14. which my lips uttered and my mouth spoke in my affliction; 15. I will offer to you burnt offerings of fatlings with the incense of rams; I will make ready oxen and goats for sacrifice to you."

units.la: VERSVS XVII.
units.tr: VERSE 17.

units.la: Præparauerat autem Iehouah piscem grandem, ut deglutiret Ionam: & fuit Ionah in uetre piscis tres dies & tres noctes.
units.tr: Now Jehovah had prepared a great fish to swallow Jonah, and Jonah was in the belly of the fish three days and three nights.

units.la: Historiam & mysterium huius loci nemo rectius exposuit, quàm Dominus Iesus Christus, cuius hæc uerba sunt: Sicut fuit Ionas in uentre ceti tres dies & tres noctes, ita erit Filius hominis in corde terræ tres dies & tres noctes.Matt.xii.40.
units.tr: No one has explained the history and the mystery of this passage more correctly than the Lord Jesus Christ, whose words these are: "As Jonah was in the belly of the whale three days and three nights, so the Son of man will be in the heart of the earth three days and three nights." Matt. 12.40.

units.la: Nos primùm de signo, deinde de re signata, uidelicet de sepultura Christi, agemus.
units.tr: First we shall speak of the sign, and then of the thing signified, namely the burial of Christ.

units.la: HISTORIA DE SIGNO IONÆ Prophetæ.
units.tr: THE HISTORY OF THE SIGN OF JONAH THE PROPHET.

units.la: Factum istud, quod cum Iona Dominus peregit, modis omnibus ftupedum, & ob id celebre, Christus Dominus noster uocauit τὸ σημεῖον Ιωνᾶ τῆ προφήτου, Matthæi 16.4. Quid enim magis admiradum esse potest, quàm hominem è naui in medias maris undas præcipitatum, ab ingenti ceto deglutiri, & tres dies noctesq; incolumem in eo uersari, ac tádem euomi incolumem in litore? Totius autem signi pulcerrima descriptio exstat in cap.2. uerf.4.5.6.7. Ideo de circumstantijs nûc non agemus.
units.tr: This event, which the Lord brought about with Jonah, is wonderful in every way and therefore famous. Christ our Lord called it "the sign of Jonah the prophet" (τὸ σημεῖον Ἰωνᾶ τοῦ προφήτου) [Matt. 16.4]. For what can be more astonishing than a man thrown from a ship into the midst of the waves of the sea, swallowed by a huge whale, and living unharmed in it for three days and three nights, and at last cast up unharmed on the shore? The most beautiful description of the whole sign is found in chapter 2, verses 4, 5, 6 and 7. Therefore we shall not now deal with its details.

units.la: Meminerimus autem, imagines miradas de conseruatione fanctorû & totius EccleEcclesiæ, nobis ad consolatione nostram obseruandas, ut in ipsis malorũ quę nos circũdant gurgitibus, & mortis faucibus, spe ponamus in Deo uiuo & omnipotente.
units.tr: Let us remember, however, that these wonderful images of the preservation of the saints and of the whole Church are set before us for our consolation, so that, amid the whirlpools of evils that surround us and the jaws of death, we may place our hope in the living and almighty God.

units.la: Psalm.66.10. Probasti nos Deus: examinasti nos, sicut conflatur atgentum[?]: 11. Deduxisti nos in laqueũ: posuisti co-arctationem in lumbis nostris. 2. Equi-tare fecisti unumquenq; super capita nostra: transuenimus in ignem & aquam: sed duxisti nos in locum irriguum. Psal.91.11. Quoniam angelis suis mandauit de te, ut custodiat te in omnibus uijs tuis. 12. Super manus portabũt te, ne offendas ad lapidem pedem tuum. 13. Super leones & aspides ambulabis: conculcabis leuncu-los & dracones.
units.tr: Psalm 66.10. Thou hast proved us, O God; thou hast tried us as silver is tried. 11. Thou broughtest us into the net; thou laidst affliction upon our loins. 12. Thou hast caused men to ride over our heads; we went through fire and water, but thou broughtest us out into a place of abundance. Psalm 91.11. For he shall give his angels charge over thee, to keep thee in all thy ways. 12. They shall bear thee up in their hands, lest thou dash thy foot against a stone. 13. Thou shalt walk upon the lion and the adder; the young lion and the dragon shalt thou trample under foot.

units.la: Dauidem in spelunca latitantem seruauit Deus, 1.Sam.24. Danielis socij in fornace ardete seruati sunt, Dan.3. Daniel in lacu leonũ diuinitus conseruatus fuit, Dan.6. Ionas in uentre ceti incolumis delituit, & tandem eductus est. Paulus Apostolus: In prima mea defensione, inquit, nemo mihi adfuit, sed omnes me deseruerunt (ne illis imputetur.) Sed Dominus mihi adfuit, & corroboravit me: ut per me fieret fides præconij, quod audirent omnes gētes: & ereptus fui ex o-re leonis. Eteripiet me Dominus ab omni opere malo, &c. 2.Tim.4.16.17.18.
units.tr: God preserved David hiding in a cave (1 Sam. 24). The companions of Daniel were preserved unharmed in the burning furnace (Dan. 3). Daniel was kept safe by God in the den of lions (Dan. 6). Jonah lay unharmed in the belly of the whale, and at last was brought out. The Apostle Paul says: "In my first defence, no one stood by me, but all forsook me (may it not be charged against them). But the Lord stood by me and strengthened me, so that through me the preaching might be fully proclaimed and all the Gentiles might hear; and I was rescued from the mouth of the lion. And the Lord will deliver me from every evil work," etc. 2 Tim. 4.16, 17, 18.

units.la: Quotus aute quisq; nostrum est, qui an teastae[?] suae uitae fata secum recolligens, nō deprehēdat, multis modis & uicibus sese diuinitus seruatum, à contentione populi liberatum, è manibus & tricis ho-stium ereptum esse?
units.tr: Yet how few of us there are who, recalling the fortunes of their own lives, do not find that in many ways and on many occasions they have been preserved by God, delivered from the strife of the people, and snatched from the hands and snares of their enemies?

units.la: Nos ipsos itaq; aspicientes, præsentiæ & beneficentiæ diuinæ argumenta collegamus, ut in nobis accendatur spes & gratitudo erga Deum. iuxta dictum: Vident hæc recti, & lætantur: & omnis iniquitas (iniquus) claudit os suum. Quis sapiens, & obseruabit hæc, & aduertet animum ad misericordias Iehouæ? Psal.107.42.43.
units.tr: Looking therefore at ourselves, let us gather the evidences of the divine presence and kindness, so that hope and gratitude toward God may be kindled in us, according to the saying: "The upright see these things and rejoice, and every iniquity shuts its mouth. Who is wise, that he may observe these things and consider the mercies of Jehovah?" Psalm 107.42, 43.

units.la: DE SEPULTURA CHRISTI, ET eius fructu ad nos redeunte.
units.tr: ON THE BURIAL OF CHRIST, AND THE FRUIT OF IT RETURNING TO US.

units.la: 1. Quis sepultus est?
units.tr: 1. Who was buried?

units.la: Filius hominis, Iesus Christus Dominus noster. Etsi autem Filius hominis, Homo Christus, & similes appellationes in cōcreto totâ persona Mediatoris Christi denotant: Matt.17.22. 1.Tim.2.5. tamē, qui in carne solùm passus est, idem in car ne quoq; sepultus est. uni enim & eidem naturae in Christi persona hæc conueniunt. Christus autem pro nobis passus est in carne : 1.Pet.4..1. In carne igitur, cui soli passio & sepultura illa competit, sepultus quoq; est.
units.tr: The Son of man, Jesus Christ our Lord. Although "the Son of man," "Man Christ," and similar names in the concrete denote the whole person of the Mediator Christ (Matt. 17.22; 1 Tim. 2.5), nevertheless he who alone suffered in the flesh was also buried in the flesh. For these things belong to one and the same nature in the person of Christ. But Christ suffered for us in the flesh (1 Pet. 4.1). Therefore it was in the flesh, to which alone that passion and burial belong, that he was also buried.

units.la: Obseruent hoc loco studiosi aureum Augustini dictum : Et idcirco Dei Filium secundum substantiam diuinitatis suæ invisibilem, incorporeum & immortalem & incircumscriptum, nos credere & confiteri oportet: iuxta humanitatem vero visibilem, corporeum, localem, atq; omnia membra humana veraciter habetem, credere oportet & confiteri. De essentia divinitatis.
units.tr: Let the diligent observe here the golden saying of Augustine: "Therefore we must believe and confess that the Son of God, according to the substance of his divinity, is invisible, incorporeal, immortal and uncircumscribed; but according to his humanity, he is visible, corporeal, local, and truly has all human members, and we must believe and confess this." On the Essence of the Divinity.

units.la: 2. Ubi sepultus est?
units.tr: 2. Where was he buried?

units.la: In corde terræ, id est, in sepulcro, de quo Matth.27.60. Joseph Arimathiensis posuit (corpus Domini Jesu) in monumento suo nouo, quod excíderat in petra : & aduoluto saxo magno ad ostium monumenti, abijt.Luc.23.53. Joa.19.41.42.
units.tr: "In the heart of the earth," that is, in the sepulchre, of which Matthew 27.60 says: Joseph of Arimathea laid (the body of the Lord Jesus) in his new tomb, which he had hewn out in the rock; and having rolled a great stone to the door of the tomb, he went away. Luke 23.53; John 19.41, 42.

units.la: Si quia in Christo personaliter unitæ sunt duæ naturæ, divina & humana, hæc ubiq; fuisset, nec crucifigi, nec sepeliri in certo loco potuisset eius caro.
units.tr: If, because the two natures, divine and human, are personally united in Christ, his flesh were everywhere, it could neither have been crucified nor buried in a certain place.

units.la: 3. Quare sepeliri voluit?
units.tr: 3. Why did he choose to be buried?

units.la: Ut neq; de morte, neq; de resurrectione eius ambigi posset, qui traditus erat in mortem propter offensas nostras, & excitatus propter iustificationem nostri. Roman.4.25.
units.tr: So that there could be no doubt either about his death or about his resurrection, he who was delivered up to death for our offences and raised again for our justification. Rom. 4.25.

units.la: 4. Quā autem lege sepultus fuit?
units.tr: 4. Under what law was he buried?

units.la: Ea, ut nec anima illius relinqueretur apud inferos, neq; caro eius sentiret corruptionem. Act.2.31. Psal.16.10.
units.tr: So that his soul would not be left among the dead, nor his flesh see corruption. Acts 2.31. Ps. 16.10.

units.la: 5. Quamdiu autem in sepulcro conditum fuit sanctum Christi corpus?
units.tr: 5. How long was the holy body of Christ shut up in the sepulchre?

units.la: Trinoctium: de cuius supputatione Evangelistae consulendi sunt. Atq; haec omnia historice a nobis accipienda sunt, nec in allegorias transformanda.
units.tr: Three nights. The reckoning of this should be taken from the Evangelists. All these things are to be received historically by us, and not turned into allegories.

units.la: 6. Qui fructus ad nos redeunt ex Christi sepultura?
units.tr: 6. What fruits come back to us from Christ's burial?

units.la: 1. Mortificatio carnis nostrae, quae eo facit, ut peccato non amplius viuamus. Rom.6.4. Sepulti igitur sumus una cum eo per Baptismum in mortem. Col.2. ii.[?] In quo etiam circumcisi estis circumcisione quae fit sine manibus, dum corpus carnis peccato obnoxiae exuistis per circumcisionem Christi:12. cosepulti cu eo per Baptismum. Haec duo testimonia often dunt dunt: primò, sanctificationis nostræ par-tem prima, esse ueteris hominis seu pecca-ti morte: secundò, pedere autē eam à mor-tis & sepulturæ Christi merito: tertiò, Sa-cramētis Circucisionis & Baptismi eandē esse tum repræsentatā, tum obsignatam.
units.tr: (1) The mortification of our flesh, which brings it about that we no longer live to sin. Rom. 6.4: "We are buried therefore with him by baptism into death." Col. 2.11–12: "In him you were also circumcised with a circumcision not made by hands, when you put off the body of the flesh, subject to sin, through the circumcision of Christ; buried with him in baptism." These two testimonies teach three things: first, that the death of the old man, or of sin, is the first part of our sanctification; second, that this comes from the merit of Christ's death and burial; third, that both circumcision and baptism are sacraments which represent and seal this same thing.

units.la: 2. Sanctificatio nostrorum Bethaim, & sepulcrorum, quæ rectè domus uiuentiū ab Hebræis uocatur. Etsi enim feminan-tur corpora nostra animalia, corruptioni obnoxia, ignominiosa, infirma: resurgent tamen, Christi uirtute excitata, spiritua-lia, incorruptibilia, gloriosa, firma. 1. Cor. 15. 42. 43.
units.tr: (2) The sanctification of our graves, the sepulchres which the Hebrews rightly call "the house of the living." For although our bodies are sown animal, subject to corruption, dishonourable and weak, they will rise, raised by the power of Christ, spiritual, incorruptible, glorious and strong. 1 Cor. 15.42–43.

units.la: CAPITIS SECVN-di Enarratio.
units.tr: Commentary on the Second Chapter.

units.la: TReis sunt Capitis secūdi, quod Ionę precum in uentre ceti ad Iehouam habitarum descriptionem complec-titur, parteis. Prima de precum illius cir-cumstantijs: secūda, de earum capitibus: tertia, de euentu. Res enim ipsa docuit, à Deo exauditas fuisse preces illas.
units.tr: The second chapter of Jonah, which contains the description of Jonah's prayers to Jehovah from the belly of the whale, falls into three parts. The first concerns the circumstances of that prayer; the second, its heads (contents); the third, its outcome. For the event itself taught that those prayers were heard by God.

units.la: THESES.
units.tr: THESES.

units.la: 1. Fides Dei seruos etiam in imis aduer-sorum forum gurgitibus versantes ad precandū hortatur. verf.1.
units.tr: 1. Faith urges God's servants, even when they are tossed in the deepest whirlpools of their adversaries, to pray. Verse 1.

units.la: 2. Ut autem non nisi ad Iehovam clamat, sic de exauditione plenè persuasa est. verf.2.
units.tr: 2. And just as he cries out only to Jehovah, so he is fully persuaded of being heard. Verse 2.

units.la: 3. Agnoscit autem illa, adversa quibus exercentur fideles, esse θεόπνευστα[?]: nec hominibus, aut alijs propinquis afflictionū caussis, irascendum esse. verf.3.
units.tr: 3. He acknowledges, moreover, that the adversities with which the faithful are exercised are θεόπνευστα [theopneusta, inspired by God], and that one must not be angry with men or with other nearby causes of affliction. Verse 3.

units.la: 4. Ut autem cum desperationis tenta-tione vehementer luctatur fides: sic eam tandem fortiter insurgens superat. verf.4.
units.tr: 4. As faith struggles vehemently with the temptation of despair, so, rising up bravely, it at last overcomes it. Verse 4.

units.la: 5. Nec sane ita leuiter afficitur afflictionum magnitudine, multitudine, & earū acerbissimo sensu, quin infirma caro querulas hominis voces extorqueat. verf.5.
units.tr: 5. Yet the heart is not so lightly moved by the greatness and multitude of afflictions, nor by their most bitter feeling, that the weak flesh does not wring from a man querulous cries. Verse 5.

units.la: 6. A' desperationis tamen praecipitio mœstum hominis animū fides serena, Sol lis instar exoriens & emergens, & consolationis radijs caliginem discutiens, revocat, & praeclarè de liberatione divina sperare iubet. verf.6.
