units.tr: 6. Nevertheless, faith, like a calm sun rising and emerging, and dispelling the darkness with the rays of consolation, calls back the sorrowing mind of man from the precipice of despair and bids it hope splendidly for deliverance from God. Verse 6.

units.la: 7. Iubet etiam fides, ut non tam in no-stra mala, quorum sensus acerbissimus est, quam in Iohovam omnipotentem & beneficum respiciamus, plenè de precū exauditione persuasi. verf.7.
units.tr: 7. Faith also bids us look not so much to our own evils, whose feeling is most bitter, as to Jehovah, omnipotent and beneficent, being fully persuaded that prayers are heard. Verse 7.

units.la: 8. Qui in creaturis potius quàm in creatore confidunt, sibijpsis & aliis, maximo utrorumq; malo, imponunt. vers.8.
units.tr: 8. Those who trust in creatures rather than in the Creator impose upon themselves and others, to the great harm of both. Verse 8.

units.la: 9. Per fidem & voto gratitudinis nos obstringimus, & idem illud exsoluimus. vers.9.
units.tr: 9. By faith and by a vow of gratitude we bind ourselves, and we fulfil that same vow. Verse 9.

units.la: 10. Fidelis est Deus, ut ait Apostolus, qui nō sinet uos tentari supra id quod potestis, sed præstabit unà cum tentatione etiam euasione, ut possitis sufferre. 1.Cor. 10.13. Joan.1.10.
units.tr: 10. God is faithful, as the Apostle says, who will not suffer you to be tempted beyond what you are able, but will provide with the temptation also the way of escape, that you may be able to bear it. 1 Cor. 10.13. John 1.10.

units.la: 11. Sicut Jonas post trinoctium in ven-tre ceti exactum, in lucem mirando mo-do prodijt, euomente eum ceto: ita Filius hominis Jesus Christus è corde terræ re-divivus prodijt, parta nobis non solum spirituali, sed etiam carnis nostræ resur-rectione.
units.tr: 11. As Jonah, after three nights spent in the belly of the whale, came forth into the light in a wonderful manner, the whale vomiting him out, so the Son of man, Jesus Christ, came forth restored to life from the heart of the earth, having obtained for us not only spiritual resurrection but also the resurrection of our flesh.

units.la: CAPITIS SECVNDI versus I.
units.tr: CHAPTER 2, VERSE 1.

units.la: Et orauit Jonah ad Jehouam Deum su-um de ventre piscis.
units.tr: And Jonah prayed to Jehovah his God out of the belly of the fish.

units.la: In hoc loco occurrit exemplū illustre distorum [?] Prophetarum: Invoca me in die tribulationis, & eruam te, & glorifica bis me [?]: Pfal.50.15. Item: Jehouah in angustia visitauerunt te, effuderunt orationem, cum correctio tua fuit ipsis. Sicut prægnans, cum appropinquat partui, dolet, clamat in doloribus suis: sic fuimus a facie tua Iehouah. Isa.26.16.17. Prius autem quam ad thesin accedamus, circumstantias expendemus.
units.tr: Here we have an illustrious example of the prophets in distress: "Call upon me in the day of trouble, and I will deliver you, and you shall glorify me": Ps. 50:15. Likewise: "In their distress they sought you out; they poured out a prayer when your correction was upon them. As a pregnant woman, when she draws near her delivery, writhes and cries out in her pains, so have we been before your face, O Jehovah": Isa. 26:16, 17. But before we come to the thesis, we will weigh the circumstances.

units.la: 1. Quis preces istas ardentissimas effudit?
units.tr: 1. Who poured out these most ardent prayers?

units.la: Ionas propheta, & quidem eo tempore, quo recusatę uocationis pœnas danti, omnia præsentem mortem intentabant. Discimus, ne quidem iræ iudicijq; diuini sensum precandi ardorem in nobis extinguere debere, ut maximè cor nostrum non mediocriter nos accuset ob specialem offensam.
units.tr: Jonah the prophet, and indeed at a time when those who had refused their calling were being punished and threatened with present death. We learn that not even the sense of God's wrath and judgment ought to extinguish in us the ardour of prayer, and that our heart, above all, should not moderately accuse us on account of a special offence.

units.la: 2. Quem autem invocauit?
units.tr: 2. Whom, then, did he call upon?

units.la: Iehouam, Stat enim illud: Dominum Deum tuum adorabis, & ei soli seruies. Deut.6.13,& 10.20. Matt.4.10. Ac diuinitus ita comparata est hominum natura, ut cum in summas angustias, & ad incitas sibi adducta uidetur, ad omnipotens Numen sibi confugiendum statuat. Hæc [?] tamen agitur de eo, qui non tam naturæ, quam fidei lumine præluncente [?], preces concepit.
units.tr: Jehovah. For this stands: "You shall worship the Lord your God, and serve him alone": Deut. 6:13; 10:20; Matt. 4:10. And human nature has been so divinely constituted that when it is brought to the greatest straits and seems driven to extremity, it resolves to flee to the almighty Deity. Yet this concerns one who conceived his prayers not so much by the light of nature as by the light of faith shining before him.

units.la: 3. Quo
units.tr: 3. How

units.la: 1. Quo animo precatus est Ioans?
units.tr: 1. In what disposition did Jonah pray?

units.la: [illegible, ~6 letters]: sic ut statueret, Iehouam illum quem inuocabat, esse Deum suum, id est, sibi quaquam peccatori esse propitium. Hebr.11.6. Atqui fieri non potest, ut sine fide quisquam placeat Deo. nam qui accedit ad Deum, huc credere oportet esse (Deum, id est, propitium patrem ei qui in uocat) & praemia largiri iis qui ipsum requirunt.
units.tr: [illegible]: so as to hold that Jehovah, whom he invoked, was his God, that is, that he would be propitious to him, although a sinner. Heb. 11:6. Yet it is impossible for anyone to please God without faith; for he who comes to God must believe that he is (God, that is, a propitious Father to the one who calls upon him) and that he bestows rewards on those who seek him.

units.la: 4. Vnde?
units.tr: 4. Whence?

units.la: E' uentre ceti. Monet haec res, Deo acceptissimas esse preces eorum, qui in media uoragine miseriarum, è carceribus, è rogo, è grabatulis suis, ad eum clamitant, Psal.51.17. Sacrificia Deo grata sunt spiritus contritus: cor contritum & afflictum Deus non despicies. Psal.147.3. Iehouah sanat contritos corde, & alligat dolores eorum.
units.tr: From the belly of the whale. This matter teaches that the prayers of those are most acceptable to God who, in the midst of the whirlpool of miseries, from prisons, from the pyre, from their sickbeds, cry out to him: Ps. 51:17. "The sacrifices pleasing to God are a contrite spirit; a contrite and afflicted heart God will not despise." Ps. 147:3: "Jehovah heals the brokenhearted and binds up their sorrows."

units.la: THESIS DE ORATIO-ne fidei.
units.tr: THESIS ON THE PRAYER OF FAITH.

units.la: Fides, Dei seruos etiam in medijs aduersorum gurgitibus positos, ad inuocationem ueri Dei hortatur.
units.tr: Faith urges God's servants, even those placed in the midst of the whirlpools of adversity, to call upon the true God.

units.la: Iacobi 5.v.15. celebratur ἡ εὐχὴ τῆς πίστεως[?], oratio fidei. Eius rationem, theseos[?] de monstranmonstrandae & declarandae gratia, secundum Scripturarum diuinarum pręscriptū syllogisticè tradere, propositum est.
units.tr: James 5:15 speaks of ἡ εὐχὴ τῆς πίστεως [hē euchē tēs pisteōs], the prayer of faith. It is our purpose to set out its reasoning syllogistically, according to the pattern of the divine Scriptures, in order to show and declare the thesis.

units.la: 1. A finitione fidei. Certum est, nulla re alia ad inuocationem nos magis incitari & permoueri, quàm ea quæ est ὑπόστασις rerum sperádarum, & ἔλεγχος eorum quæ non uidentur. Nam in precibus τὰ μὴ βλε-πόμενα καὶ τὰ ἐλπιζόμενα petimus nobis dari. Sed, finitore Apostolo Paulo, Fides est ὑπόστασις rerum sperádarum, &c. Heb.ii.i. Fides igitur ad preces nos hortatur.
units.tr: 1. From the definition of faith. It is certain that nothing moves and stirs us to invocation more than that which is hypostasis [ὑπόστασις] of things hoped for and elenchos [ἔλεγχος] of things not seen. For in prayers we ask that ta mē blepomena kai ta elpizomena [τὰ μὴ βλεπόμενα καὶ τὰ ἐλπιζόμενα] be given to us. But the Apostle Paul, defining it, says faith is ὑπόστασις [hypostasis] of things hoped for, and so on: Heb. 11:1. Faith therefore urges us to prayer.

units.la: 2. A proprio. Cuius proprium est suauissimè acquiescere in Deo Conditore & Redemtore, illud certè ad eius opem in aduersis implorandâ maximè nos permouet. Atqui fides, quatenus τῇ πληροφορίᾳ definitur, acquiescit in Iehouah Deo suo: & agnoscit eum esse non solùm conditorem, sed etiam saluatorem. Quare fides ad preces ad Deum fundendas impellit.
units.tr: 2. From its proper nature. It is the property of faith to rest most sweetly in God the Creator and Redeemer, and this certainly moves us most strongly to implore his help in adversity. Yet faith, as it is defined by full assurance [τῇ πληροφορίᾳ], rests in Jehovah its God and acknowledges him to be not only Creator but also Saviour. Therefore faith impels us to pour out prayers to God.

units.la: 3. Ab adiuncto. Id demum ad inuocationem maximè excitat, quod omnia eius impedimenta amolitur & superat. Fides autem omnia scandala & impedimenta precum, ipsumq; adeò mudum uincit. iuxta dictum: Haec est victoria quae vicit mūdum, nempe fides nostra: 1.Ioan.5.4. Cum Ionas in ventre ceti delitesceret, carnis periculosam imaginationem de exitio, & de implacabili Dei ira, nō nisi fide, statuente gratiam exuberare supra delictum, superare & repellere potuit. Sed tamen & illud nobis fatendum est, nō tam aduersa quae desperabundos, quàm secunda quae securos & turgidos reddere solent, invocationis Dei impedimenta esse: quae sanè non nisi fide à nobis vinci possint.
units.tr: 3. From its concomitant. That which most of all stirs up invocation is that it removes and overcomes all the hindrances to it. Faith overcomes all the stumbling-blocks and hindrances of prayer, and the world itself, according to the saying: "This is the victory that overcomes the world, namely our faith": 1 John 5:4. When Jonah lay hidden in the belly of the whale, he could repel and overcome the perilous imagination of the flesh about destruction and God's implacable wrath only by faith, which held that grace abounds above sin. Yet we must also confess that it is not so much adversities, which tend to make men despairing, as prosperities, which tend to make them secure and proud, that are the hindrances to invoking God; and these can be overcome by us only by faith.

units.la: Caeterum ut haec doctrina de fidei praecibus illustretur, causas praecipuas adducemus.
units.tr: Moreover, that this doctrine of the prayer of faith may be illustrated, we will adduce its principal causes.

units.la: 1. ἀντίλυτρον[?] istarum precum est Spiritus sanctus, qui ideo dicitur gratiae & precum Spiritus, quòd testis est gratiae Dei erga nos, & hortator ad preces. Dicitur idē[?] subleuare infirmitates nostras. quid enim precemur ut oportet, nō nouimus: sed ipse Spiritus interpellat pro nobis suspiriis[?] inenarrabilibus: Rom.8.26. Ut igitur ad cōcipiedas[?] preces nos impellit, sic qua ratione nobis concipiendae & fundendae sint, fideliter ostendit: quia q[?] Dei sunt, nemo nouit nisi Spiritus Dei. 1.Cor.2.11.
units.tr: 1. The chief cause of these prayers is the Holy Spirit, who is therefore called the Spirit of grace and of prayer, because he bears witness to God's grace toward us and exhorts us to pray. He is also said to relieve our infirmities. For we do not know what we ought to pray for, but the Spirit himself intercedes for us with unspeakable groanings: Rom. 8:26. So as he impels us to conceive prayers, he faithfully shows us how they are to be conceived and poured out; for no one knows the things of God except the Spirit of God: 1 Cor. 2:11.

units.la: 2. Συναίτιον[?] precum fidei recte dixerimus esse, mandatum Dei de inuocatione & eius forma. Vt enim Lex caussa impulsiua est, quia (ut optimus ille Melanchthō dicere solebat) est cogitatio agentis, qua impellitur ad agendum: ita mandatū, Dominum Deum tuum adorabis: impel-lit inuocantem ad ferias preces, ac simul docet quis inuocandus sit, & quomodo.
units.tr: 2. We may rightly say that the co-cause [συναίτιον] of the prayers of faith is God's command concerning invocation and its form. For as the Law is the impelling cause, because (as that excellent Melanchthon used to say) it is the thought of the agent by which he is driven to act, so the command, "You shall worship the Lord your God," impels the one invoking to frequent prayer, and at the same time teaches whom he is to invoke, and how.

units.la: 3. Σύνπιστις[?] fides excitata à Spiritu sancto, & in mandatum pariter & promissionem de exauditione respiciens. Ideo ἐὐχὴ[?] τῆς πίστεως[?] dicitur, Iac.5.15.
units.tr: 3. Faith stirred up by the Holy Spirit, looking both to the command and to the promise of being heard. Therefore it is called the prayer of faith [ἡ εὐχὴ τῆς πίστεως], Jas. 5:15.

units.la: 4. Forma eius scite descripsit idem Apostolus, Epistolae suae cap.1.v.6, Αἰτείτω ἐν πίστει, μηδὲν διακρινόμενος, ὁ γὰρ διακρινόμενος ἔοικε κλύδωνι θαλάσσης ἀνεμιζομένῳ καὶ ῥιπιζομένῳ. Sed postulet cum fide nihil disceptas; nam qui disceptat, similis est fluctui maris, qui ventis agitatur & iactatur.
units.tr: 4. The same Apostle described its form well in the first chapter of his Epistle, verse 6: "Let him ask in faith, wavering in nothing; for he who wavers is like a wave of the sea, driven and tossed by the wind" [Αἰτείτω ἐν πίστει, μηδὲν διακρινόμενος, ὁ γὰρ διακρινόμενος ἔοικε κλύδωνι θαλάσσης ἀνεμιζομένῳ καὶ ῥιπιζομένῳ].

units.la: 5. Proximi fines precum, monstrantes diversas species, peti possunt ex illo nobili dicto Pauli, 1.Tim.2.1. Adhortor igitur ante omnia, ut fiant deprecationes, preces, postulationes, gratiarum actiones pro quibusuis hominibus. Δέησις est supplicatio, petens à Deo, ut à rebus molestis liberet seruos suos. iuxta dictum: Non enim quiescet sceptrum impiorum super fortem (id est, coetum) iustorum: ne extendant iusti ad iniquitatem manus suas. Psal.125.3.
units.tr: 5. The nearer limits of prayers, showing their different kinds, can be drawn from that noble saying of Paul, 1 Tim. 2:1: "I exhort, therefore, first of all, that supplications, prayers, petitions and thanksgivings be made for all men." Deēsis [Δέησις] is a supplication, asking God to free his servants from troublesome things, according to the saying: "For the sceptre of the wicked shall not rest upon the lot (that is, the company) of the righteous, lest the righteous stretch out their hands to iniquity": Ps. 125:3.

units.la: προσευχὴ est, qua eximium aliquod bonum à Deo petimus. Psal.27.4. Unum petij à Jehouah, hoc requisiui, ut habitem in domo Jehouæ omnibus diebus vitæ meæ, ad spectandam pulcritudinem Jehouæ, & inspiciendum templum eius.
units.tr: Proseuchē [προσευχὴ] is that by which we ask God for some outstanding good. Ps. 27:4: "One thing I have asked of Jehovah, this I will seek: that I may dwell in the house of Jehovah all the days of my life, to behold the beauty of Jehovah and to inquire in his temple."

units.la: ἔντευξις [?] postulatio est, cum injurias nobis illatas, apud Deum deplorantes, eum judicem & vindicem esse volumus. Psal. 26.1. Judica me Jehouah: nam ego in integritate mea ambulaui, &c. Apoc.6.10. Mactati propter verbum Dei, clamat voce magna, dicentes: Usquequo Domine, qui sanctus es & verax, non judicas ac vindicas sanguinem nostrum de iis qui habitat in terra? Deut.15.9. Ne malignus sit oculus tuus in fratrem tuum mendicum, ita ut non des ei: clamet autem contra te ad Jehouam, & erit in te peccatum.
units.tr: Enteuxis [ἔντευξις] is a petition, when, lamenting to God the injuries done to us, we wish him to be judge and avenger. Ps. 26:1: "Judge me, O Jehovah, for I have walked in my integrity," etc. Rev. 6:10: "Those slain for the word of God cry out with a loud voice, saying: How long, Lord, holy and true, will you not judge and avenge our blood on those who dwell on the earth?" Deut. 15:9: "Let your eye not be evil toward your poor brother, so that you give him nothing; for he will cry out against you to Jehovah, and it will be sin in you."

units.la: Recte tamen Theodorus Beza(ex illis Pauli verbis: Itidem autem & Spiritus vna subleuat infirmitates nostras. quid enim precemur ut oportet, non nouimus? sed ipse Spiritus interpellat pro nobis suspiriis inenarrabilibus. Rom.8.26.) colligit, συν[illegible, ~6 letters] ad mutuas aliorum pro aliis preces referri posse. Eius exemplum habetur Matt.9.2. in baiulis paralytici.
units.tr: Yet Theodore Beza rightly concludes, from those words of Paul: "Likewise the Spirit also helps our infirmities; for we do not know what we ought to pray for, but the Spirit himself intercedes for us with groanings that cannot be uttered" (Rom. 8:26), that the prefix sun- [συν] ... can be referred to the mutual prayers of some for others. An example of this is found in Matt. 9:2, in the bearers of the paralytic.

units.la: Εὐχαριστία[?], gratiarum actio est pro omnibus beneficijs Dei, tam uniuersalibus, quàm Ecclesiae peculiaribus. Exempla plurima & pulcerrima passim in sacris Biblijs, & nominatim in Psal.102.103.104. 107. occurrunt.
units.tr: Eucharistia [Εὐχαριστία] is thanksgiving for all God's benefits, both universal and those peculiar to the Church. Very many and most beautiful examples occur throughout the Holy Bible, and by name in Psalms 102, 103, 104 and 107.

units.la: Vltimus finis inuocationis Dei, est diuini nominis sanctificatio,
units.tr: The ultimate end of invoking God is the sanctification of the divine name. ## VERSE II

units.la: VERSVS II,
Clamaui ex afflictione mea ad Ieho-uam, & exaudiuit me: de uentre inferni clamaui, & exaudisti uocem meam.
units.tr: I cried out of my affliction to Jehovah, and he heard me: out of the belly of hell I cried, and you heard my voice.

units.la: In hoc uersu occurrit illustre exemplu dulcisimae promisionis de exauditione precum, quae exstat Isa.65.24. Erit praeterea, antequam clament, ego audiam: adhuc ipsis clamantibus, ego audiam.
units.tr: In this verse there occurs a notable example of the sweetest promise concerning the hearing of prayers, which stands in Isa. 65.24: "And it shall come to pass that, before they call, I will answer; and while they are still speaking, I will hear."

units.la: Clamare ad Iehouam, nihil aliud est, quàm Spiritu & ueritate Deum adorare. Joan.4.23. Cumq; vox affectus fidelis in corde index fit, precatio eximo corde ad Deum fusa, clamor dicitur. Exodi 14.15. Quid clamas ad me? 1.Sam.7.8. Dixerunt Israelitae ad Samuelem: Ne sileas pro nobis clamando ad Jehouam Deum nostrum, ut eripiat nos de manu Peliftim.
units.tr: To cry to Jehovah is nothing other than to worship God in spirit and in truth (John 4.23). And when the voice becomes the index of a faithful affection, a prayer poured out from the heart is called a cry (Exod. 14.15): "Why do you cry to me?" (1 Sam. 7.8): "The Israelites said to Samuel: Do not cease crying out to Jehovah our God for us, that he may deliver us out of the hand of the Philistines."

units.la: Obseruetur autem αὔξησις[?] ducta a consideratione tum afflictionum, tum loci, in quo morabatur Propheta per illud tri noctium: sed hac de re paulo post dicetur.
units.tr: Note also the amplification (auxesis) drawn from the consideration both of the afflictions and of the place in which the prophet remained for those three days and nights; but this will be discussed a little later. ## THESIS

units.la: THESIS.
Ut fides non nisi ad Jehouam clamat: sic de exauditione plene persuasa est.
units.tr: Just as faith calls upon no one but Jehovah, so it is fully persuaded of being heard. ## PROOF OF THE FIRST PART

units.la: DEMONSTRATIO PRI-mæ partis.
Fides neminem alium, quàm eum in quo tanquam summo bonorum omnium auctore suauissimè acquiescit, invocat. juxta illud Pauli: Quomodo invocabunt eum, in quem non crediderint? Roman.10.14.
units.tr: Faith invokes no one other than him in whom, as in the supreme author of all good things, it rests most sweetly, according to the saying of Paul: "How shall they call on him in whom they have not believed?" (Rom. 10.14).

units.la: Credit autem Deo, & acquiescit in Jehouah solo. Nec enim fidei cultus ulli creaturae competit, sed soli Creatori: secundum illud Apostoli: Nam iccirco etiam fatigamur & probris afficimur, quòd speremus (id est, credimus & acquiesci-mus)in Deo uiuo,qui est coferuator om-nium hominum,maxime uero fidelium.
units.tr: Now faith trusts in God and rests in Jehovah alone. For the worship of faith belongs to no creature, but only to the Creator, according to the saying of the Apostle: "For this reason we also toil and suffer reproach, because we hope (that is, we believe and rest) in the living God, who is the preserver of all men, and especially of believers" (1 Tim. 4.10).

units.la: Quare etiam neminem alium inuocat, quam Iehouam conditorem & conferua torem coeli & terrae,&c.
units.tr: Wherefore faith also invokes no one else than Jehovah, the maker and preserver of heaven and earth, etc. ## Objections against the Minor Premise

units.la: Obiectiones contra Minorem.
1. Paulus ad Philemone,uersu 5.Quod, inquit, audiam tuam charitatem, ac fide quam habes erga Dominum Iesum,& er ga omnes Sanctos. Ergo,colligit Eccius, fides etiam in Sanctis inclinata recubit.
units.tr: 1. Paul, to Philemon, verse 5: "That I may hear of your love and of the faith which you have toward the Lord Jesus and toward all the saints." Therefore, Eck infers, faith also reclines inclined toward the saints.

units.la: Respondeo, esse paralogifmum figurę dictionis. Nam per μεταθεσιν nonihil tranf-positae sunt dictiones. Sed fides quidè ad Christum: charitas autem etiam ad Sanctos referri debet.
units.tr: I answer that this is a paralogism of the figure of speech. For by metathesis [μετάθεσιν] some words have been transposed. But faith is indeed directed to Christ, while love ought to be referred also to the saints.

units.la: 2. In Symbolo Niceno dicitur: εἰς μίαν ἁγίαν καθολικὴν καὶ ἀποστολικὴν ἐκκλησίαν, subaudi uerbum Credo. Ergo ut in Deum Patrem,Filium & Spiritum sanctum, sic in Ecclesiam quoqȝ nobis est crededum.
units.tr: 2. In the Nicene Creed it is said: into one holy, catholic and apostolic church [εἰς μίαν ἁγίαν καθολικὴν καὶ ἀποστολικὴν ἐκκλησίαν], the word "I believe" being understood. Therefore, just as we must believe in God the Father, the Son and the Holy Spirit, so we must also believe in the Church.

units.la: Respondeo: Non pugnat Nicenum Symbolum cum Apostolico:nec ἀπροσωπο-λυτον est, illud huic interpretando confor mare. Sic autem pronunciat Apostoli-cum cum, πιστεύω τὴν ἁγίαν ἐκκλησίαν καθολικὴν, ἀ-[?]
units.tr: I answer: the Nicene Creed does not conflict with the Apostles' Creed, nor is it an unlawful thing to interpret the one so as to agree with the other. The Apostles' Creed pronounces thus: "I believe the holy catholic Church, [the communion of saints]," etc.

units.la: γίων κοινωνίαν[?], &c. Quis etiam Ecclesiam adorandam nobis esse, unquam statuit? Nemo sanus. Atqui si in Ecclesiam credendum est, eadem quoque adoranda est.
units.tr: Who has ever laid it down that the Church is to be adored by us? No sane person. Yet if we are to believe in the Church, then it too must be adored.

units.la: Ac fieri sanè potuit, ut syncategorema Eis[?] irrepere uitio scribarum in Nicenum symbolum.
units.tr: And it could well be that the syncategorema "Eis" [εἰς] crept into the Nicene creed through a mistake of the scribes.

units.la: Obiectio contra Complexionem, pro tuenda invocatione Sanctorum.
units.tr: Objection against the complexio, in defence of the invocation of the saints.

units.la: Eccius hoc dilemma Lutheranis, quos vocat, indissolubile esse contendit: Si ergo, inquit, vivi orat pro invicem, cur etiā beati mortui hoc non facerant, qui sunt in charitate perfectiores, & apud Deum potentiores, & mente puriores?
units.tr: Eccius maintains that this dilemma cannot be resolved for the Lutherans, as he calls them: "If, then," he says, "the living pray for one another, why do the blessed dead not also do this, who are more perfect in charity, more powerful with God, and purer in mind?"

units.la: Aut ergo Sancti non orant pro nobis sicut vivi, quia est res eis indigna. Itaque nō conveniet Christo. Aut quia est res tantae excellentiae, quod soli Christo & non aliis conveniet. Ergo non convenit viatoribus. Respondeo,
units.tr: Either, then, the saints do not pray for us as the living do, because it is a thing unworthy of them; and so it would not befit Christ. Or it is because it is a matter of such excellence that it belongs to Christ alone and not to others; therefore it does not belong to wayfarers. I answer:

units.la: 1. Ad λεπτολογήματα[?], Vivos & superstites a nobis de rebus nostris doceri posse, & rogari, ut nostri in precibus memores esse velint: defunctos vero non item. Isa. 63.16. Deinde, id quod de dotibus San-ctorum {Greek text} ... ποραὰ τὸ μὴ αἴτιον ὡς αἴτιον.
units.tr: 1. As to his quibbles: the living and those who survive can be taught by us about our affairs and asked to remember us in their prayers; the dead, however, cannot likewise. (Isa. 63.16.) Then, as to what is said of the merits of the saints, he passes from what is not the cause as if it were the cause.

units.la: 2. In primo lemmate est eadem fallacia. Non enim quia res indigna Sanctis sit orare pro nobis, sed quia nescij sint rerum nostrarum, præsertim particularium, nec à nobis doceri possint, & quia cultus adorationis soli Deo competit, invocandi non sunt.
units.tr: 2. In the first premise there is the same fallacy. For it is not because it is unworthy of the saints to pray for us, but because they do not know our affairs, especially particular ones, and cannot be taught them by us, and because the worship of adoration belongs to God alone, that they are not to be invoked.

units.la: 3. In posteriore lemmate illud notandum, sanctos uiatores à nobis non adorari: sed quòd præsto nobis sint, multumq; ualeat iusti precatio, rogari, ut unà nobiscum per Christi unici Mediatoris nomẽ preces concipiant. Petit autem Ecclus principium, cum præsupponit, Eos nobis adorandos, qui pro nobis orauerũt dum essent superstites: item cum fingit, Sanctos, ubi ex hac uita discesserunt, conscios esse rerum nostrarum, quòd fictitium essentiæ diuinæ speculũ omnia quæ hæc apud nos, illis repræsentet.
units.tr: 3. On the second premise it should be noted that the saints who are still on the way are not adored by us; but since they are present with us, and the prayer of a righteous man avails much, they are asked to join with us in offering prayers through the name of Christ, the only Mediator. Yet Eck begs the question when he presupposes that those are to be adored by us who prayed for us while they were still living; and likewise when he imagines that the saints, once they have departed from this life, are aware of our affairs, because the divine essence is a kind of mirror that represents to them all the things that happen among us.

units.la: DEMONSTRATIO SECVNDAE partis Θέσεως, in qua de exauditionis fiducia agitur.
units.tr: DEMONSTRATION OF THE SECOND PART OF THE THESIS, in which confidence of being heard is treated.

units.la: Illud Dei χαρίσματα, quod Deo ueritatis, bonitatis, omnisciẽtiæ & omnipotentiæ tiæ laudem tribuit, non potest de exau‐ditione precum dubium relinquere ho‐minem.
units.tr: That attribute of God (χαρίσματα) which ascribes to God truth, goodness, omniscience and omnipotence cannot leave a man in doubt about the hearing of prayers.

units.la: Fides autem id præstat: ut ex amabili de Patre credentium exemplo liquet, de quo Paulus Rom.4.20. Aduersus promis‐sionem Dei non disceptauit infidelitate: sed robustus factus est fide, tributa gloria Deo: 21.Ac plenè persuasum habes, eum quod promiserat posse etiàm facere.
units.tr: Faith in fact secures this, as the example of our father in faith makes clear, of whom Paul says (Rom. 4.20): "He did not waver through unbelief at the promise of God, but was made strong in faith, giving glory to God; (21) and being fully persuaded that what he had promised he was able also to do."

units.la: Itaq; fide statuimus, preces nostras nō esse inane murmur, sed à Deo exaudiri.
units.tr: Therefore we hold by faith that our prayers are not an empty murmur, but are heard by God.

units.la: Ἀπορία 1. Si antequam clamemus, nos exaudit, cur sæpenumero liberationem & alia bona tamdiu differt? Quia om‐nia suo tempore agit: & quibus, quando, & quæ bona danda sint, optimè nouit.
units.tr: Objection 1. If God hears us before we cry out, why does he so often put off deliverance and other blessings for so long? Because he does all things in their time, and knows best to whom, when, and what good things are to be given.

units.la: Ἀπορία 2. Sæpe autem ea quæ petimus, se daturum negat. Vt Mosi denegauit fa‐cultatem intrandi terram Canaan: Deut. 32.50.51. Respondeo, primùm terrena & cœlestia bona nobis esse distinguèda. Vt maximè enim illa suis interdum dene‐get: hæc tamen quæ ad salutem necessa‐ria sunt, suis nunquam non largitur. De‐inde, non raro incredulitatem & peccata nostra, diuinæ erga nos beneficentiæ lar‐gitatem gitatem restringere. Postremò, non raró Deum ea propitium denegare: ne uideli- cet ijs abutamur, quæ dat iratus. Loquor de temporalium bonorum dispensatione & usu. Scitum est illud Augustini: Sæ- pe Deus multos non exaudit ad uoluntatem, ut exaudiat ad salutem. De summo Bono lib. 3.
units.tr: Objection 2. Often he refuses what we ask, as he denied Moses the right to enter the land of Canaan (Deut. 32.50, 51). I answer: first, we must distinguish earthly goods from heavenly ones. For although he sometimes withholds the former from his own people, he never fails to bestow the latter, which are necessary for salvation. Second, our unbelief and sins often restrain the generosity of God's kindness towards us. Last, God not infrequently refuses us those things in mercy, lest we abuse what he gives in anger. I am speaking of the dispensing and use of temporal goods. That saying of Augustine is well known: "God often does not hear many people according to their will, so that he may hear them for their salvation." (De summo bono, book 3.)

units.la: VERSUS III.
units.tr: VERSE III.

units.la: Nam tu proiycere fecisti me in profun-dum, & in cor marium, & flumen circum dedit me: omnes collisiones tuæ, & fluctus tui super me transierunt.
units.tr: For you cast me into the deep, into the heart of the seas, and the flood surrounded me; all your breakers and your waves passed over me.

units.la: Paraphrasis Theodori Bezæ.
units.tr: Paraphrase of Theodore Beza.

units.la: Nam tu me in profundum gurgitem, & ipsius maris intima, nautarum manibus proiciendum ipsa sortitione pronun- ciasti: ubi undiq; circumstantibus aquis, & fluctibus in se mutuo recurrentibus, obrutus iacebam.
units.tr: For you have decreed that I be cast into the deep whirlpool, into the very depths of the sea, to be thrown by the hands of the sailors by the lot itself; where, with waters surrounding me on every side and waves crashing back upon one another, I lay overwhelmed.

units.la: THESIS.
units.tr: THESIS.

units.la: Cum fides statuat, aduersa esse θεομα- χία: nequaquam proximis eorum causis irascitur.
units.tr: Since faith holds that adversities are not a fight against God, it is by no means angry with their proximate causes. [θεομαχία]

units.la: Hæc θεὸς monet, æquissimum esse, ut in Dei iudicijs acquiescamus, nec fremi-tu & indignatione ulla peccemus. iuxta illud: Obmutui, non aperiam os meum: nam tu fecisti. Psal.39.9. Non accusat Da-uid suos hostes, nec Ionas nautas à qui-bus in mare è naui deturbatus erat: sed uterq; manum Dei agnoscit, sine qua ni-hil illorum euenire potuisse, praeclarè in-telligebant. Sed ad rem.
units.tr: Faith teaches that it is most right for us to acquiesce in God's judgments and not to sin by complaining or any indignation, according to the words: "I was dumb, I did not open my mouth, because you have done it" (Ps. 39.9). David does not accuse his enemies, nor does Jonah accuse the sailors by whom he was thrown from the ship into the sea; both clearly understood that nothing of those things could have happened without the hand of God. But to the matter.

units.la: Si nec suprema afflictionum nostrarum causa accusari debet, nec est cur etiam proximis causis succensemus: tum ue-rò ut fidei est, humiliare se sub potenti manu Dei: ita incredulitatis erit, irasci seu Deo, seu eius instrumentis. Nam si qui praeter meritum male ab alio tractantur, & Dei iniussu, ij habent de quo querantur, at profecto non apud Deum.
units.tr: If the supreme cause of our afflictions ought not to be blamed, and there is no reason to be angry even at their proximate causes, then indeed it belongs to faith to humble oneself under the mighty hand of God; so it belongs to unbelief to be angry either with God or with his instruments. For if some people are treated badly by another beyond their deserts, and without God's command, they have something to complain of, but certainly not before God.

units.la: Atqui Deus, ut gratuitorum praemiorum, sic afflictionum nostrarum iustissimus dispensator, accusari sine impietate non potest. Habet enim ius ἀνυπεύθυνον in omnes creaturas, cum earum conditor sit. Deinde ipsius voluntas quid aliud est, quàm absolutissima iustitiae norma? Notum autem est illud Pauli: An non habet potestatem figulus in lutum, ut ex eadem massa fasa faciat aliud quidè uas ad decus, aliud uerò ad dedecus? Rom.9.21.
units.tr: But God, as the most just dispenser of both free rewards and our afflictions, cannot be accused without impiety. For he has a right [ἀνυπεύθυνον] over all creatures, since he is their creator. Moreover, what is his will but the most absolute standard of justice? And the saying of Paul is well known: "Has not the potter power over the clay, to make from the same lump one vessel for honour and another for dishonour?" (Rom. 9.21).

units.la: Sedenim ne quidem proximis nostra-rum afflictionum causis, quæ Dei iudi-cijs seruiût, irasci fas est. Neq; enim quia odio, liuore, aut alio cæco affectu ducun-tur, sed quia è supernis potestas illis data est, Ioan.19.11. nos affligunt. Ideo Eccle-sia primitiua in illa sua apud Deum [illegible, ~5 letters] fatetur, Pilatum, Herodem & alios [illegible, ~8 letters], ea solum facere, quæcunq; manus & consilium Dei prius definierat facien-da: Act.4.28.
units.tr: Nor is it right to be angry even with the proximate causes of our afflictions, which serve God's judgments. For they afflict us not because they are driven by hatred, envy, or some other blind passion, but because power was given them from above (John 19.11). Therefore the primitive Church, in its prayer to God, confesses that Pilate, Herod, and the others [illegible] did only those things which the hand and counsel of God had decided beforehand should be done (Acts 4.28).

units.la: Quare[?] nostrum fuerit, Dei iudiciis nō[?] obloqui: sed nos summittere potenti manui Dei. 1.Pet.5.6.
units.tr: Therefore it is our part not to object to the judgments of God, but to submit ourselves under the mighty hand of God (1 Pet. 5.6).

units.la: DE PATIENTIA CHRISTIANÆ causis.
units.tr: ON CHRISTIAN PATIENCE: the causes.

units.la: Vt autem per patientiam possideamus animas nostras, Luc.21.19. multræ & gratuissimæ caussæ iubent. Posita enim hac thesi, Etsi cum aduersis nos corripit Dominus, plerunq; utitur creaturarum quasi rundam ministerio: tamen firmiter statuendum nobis esse, illa & [illegible, ~8 letters] esse, & a Deo moderari: Fides statim colligit, illa non solum æquis animis nobis serenda,sed etiam Deo nos castiganti ex cor-de toto gratias esse agendas.
units.tr: That we may possess our souls in patience (Luke 21.19), many and very weighty reasons urge us. For this thesis being laid down, that although the Lord chastises us with adversities, he often uses the ministry of creatures as it were, we must nonetheless firmly hold that these [illegible] and are governed by God. Faith immediately infers that these are to be borne not only with calm minds, but that we should also give thanks with our whole heart to God who chastises us.

units.la: Hæc ut illustrentur, primùm quæ nos ad patientiā hortentur, cùm sublatis me-tis oculis Deum intuemur: deinde, quæ nam cum in nos ipsos descendimus: po-stremò, quę etiam ubi iuxta nos sitas creaturas Dei iudicijs famulantes adspici-mus, ἀπαλλαγῆς ἡ σωτηρίας [?] indicabimus.
units.tr: To illustrate these points, we will first set out what urges us to patience when we lift our eyes and look upon God; then what urges us when we descend into ourselves; and lastly what also urges us when we look upon the creatures of God near us, serving his judgments, [ἀπαλλαγῆς ἢ σωτηρίας] we shall point out.

units.la: Cum Deum & eius naturam perpendis, hæ patientiæ causæ, quæ sunt riuuli perennes dulcissimarum consolationum, tibi occurrunt.
units.tr: When you weigh God and his nature, these causes of patience, which are perennial streams of the sweetest consolations, present themselves to you.

units.la: 1. Deus omniscius est. Non est igitur cur afflictionum tuarum formas, causas & circumstantias eum latere putes.
units.tr: 1. God is all-knowing. It is therefore no reason to think that he is hidden from him, the forms, causes and circumstances of your afflictions.

units.la: 2. Idem omnia secundum propositum voluntatis agit. Ne igitur casu, ipsoq; co-niuete te affligi: neue nullam tuarum af-flictionum τυχόντως [?] esse opineris.
units.tr: 2. The same God does all things according to the purpose of his will. Do not therefore think that you are afflicted by chance, or that any of your afflictions happen at random [τυχόντως].

units.la: 3. Summè bonus est Deus. Ne igitur af-flictiones ab eo immissas, ἀπλῶς malas esse tibi persuadeas.
units.tr: 3. God is supremely good. Do not therefore persuade yourself that afflictions sent by him are simply evil.

units.la: 4. Summè quoq; iustus est. Ne igitur dubita, optimo iure ab eo castigari tua παραπτώματα ἡ ἁμαρτήματα [?].
units.tr: 4. He is also supremely just. Do not doubt, therefore, that you are chastised by him with the best right for your transgressions or sins.

units.la: 5. Pater tuus est per & propter Christū. Statue ergo,paterno eum erga te esse animo,& te filium γνώσιον optimo consilio castigari.
units.tr: 5. He is your Father, through and for the sake of Christ. Be assured therefore that he has a fatherly mind towards you, and that you, as his son, are chastised by the best counsel.

units.la: 6. Immensa eius sapientia est. Ergo cū te explorat & tentat, etsi finem non statim uides,tamen statue id optimum esse, quòd is Deo cognitus & probatus est.
units.tr: 6. His wisdom is immense. Therefore, when he tests and tries you, even if you do not see the end at once, hold nonetheless that it is best, since you are known and approved by God.

units.la: 7. Immensa quoq; eius potentia est.Potest igitur suos liberare ab omni malo.
units.tr: 7. His power too is immense. He is therefore able to deliver his own from every evil.

units.la: 8. Non irascitur in æternum. Psal.103.9. Non in perpetuum rixari solitus, nec in seculum iram custodire.
units.tr: 8. He is not angry forever (Ps. 103.9). He is not accustomed to quarrel perpetually, nor to keep his anger for ever.

units.la: Cum autem in temetipsum descendis,hæc consolationum capita, inter multa alia,occurrunt.
units.tr: When you descend into yourself, these heads of consolation, among many others, present themselves.

units.la: 1. Aduersa etiam summa & acerbissima,non efficiunt,ut aliquid nobis decedat. Luc.21.18. Pilus capitis uestri non peribit. Psal.34.20. Tuetur omnia ossa eius: unum ex ipsis non frangitur.
units.tr: 1. Adversities, even the greatest and most bitter, do not cause anything to be taken from us. "Not a hair of your head shall perish" (Luke 21.18). "He keeps all his bones; not one of them is broken" (Ps. 34.20).

units.la: 2. Immò ea plurimum conferunt. Psal. 119.67. Priusquam humiliarer,ego uagabar: sed nunc sermonem tuum custodio.
units.tr: 2. Rather, they contribute very much. "Before I was afflicted I went astray, but now I keep your word" (Ps. 119.67).

units.la: 71. Bonum est mihi quòd afflictus sum, ut discam edicta tua.
units.tr: 71. "It is good for me that I was afflicted, that I might learn your statutes."

units.la: 3. Deus multò mitius tecū agit,quàm peccatis tuis sis promeritus. Psal.103.10. Non secundum peccata nostra fecit nobis: neque secundum iniquitates nostras rependit super nos.
units.tr: 3. God deals with you far more gently than your sins have deserved. "He has not dealt with us according to our sins, nor repaid us according to our iniquities" (Ps. 103.10).

units.la: Cum denique iuxta te sitas creaturas, quarum ministerio ad te castigandum Deus utitur, adspicis, haec tibi in mentem venire possunt.
units.tr: Finally, when you look upon the creatures placed near you, whose ministry God uses to chastise you, these things may come into your mind.

units.la: 1, Iudiciorum Dei instrumenta duū esse genera, ἄλογα & λογικά.
units.tr: 1. The instruments of God's judgments are of two kinds: irrational [ἄλογα] and rational [λογικά].

units.la: 2, ἀλόγοις non esse cur ob id irascaris, quòd iudicij divini executioni seruiunt, cum illa nec laudem, nec uituperium merentur. Uti Deus pruina, grandine, peste, siccitate, securi è manubrio excidete, incēdio utatur: non est cur his irascamur.
units.tr: 2. There is no reason to be angry with the irrational ones because they serve the execution of divine judgment, since they deserve neither praise nor blame. As God uses frost, hail, pestilence, drought, an axe flying from its handle, or fire, there is no reason for us to be angry at these.

units.la: 3, λογικά instrumenta, ut maximè reprehensionem incurrant, cum improbo ducuntur affectu: tamen, quatenus seruiunt Dei manui & consilio, non est cur eis irascamur. Non enim nisi ea facere possunt, quæ Deus fieri vult. Ac ne quidem Satan pluribus, quàm velit & concedat Dominus, malis & incommodis quequam potest afficere: ut historia Iobi testatur. Sed haec, ita ut dixi, non nisi summa rerum stigia[?] attingendo, hoc temporis articulo percensere licet.
units.tr: 3. Rational instruments, although they most of all incur reproof when they are driven by a wicked affection, nevertheless, insofar as they serve God's hand and counsel, there is no reason for us to be angry with them. For they can do only what God wills to be done. Nor can even Satan afflict anyone with more evils and troubles than the Lord wills and permits, as the story of Job testifies. But these things, as I have said, can be reviewed at this point only by touching on the outlines of the matter.

units.la: Tunc ego dixi: Expulsus sum è conspe-ctu oculorum tuorum: verum pergam aspi-cere ad templum sanctitatis tuae.
units.tr: "Then I said: I am cast out from before your eyes; yet I will still look toward your holy temple." ## Paraphrase.

units.la: Παράφρασις.

At ego nihilominus fidei viribus elu-ctans, sic te compellare: Sum quidem ego, fateor, procul optimo iure à tuo conspectu summotus: sed tamen pergam ad templum illud tuum sanctum, utpote certum tuae in miseros tuam opem implorantes clementiae pignus, animo respicere.
units.tr: "Yet I, struggling against the strength of faith, address you thus: I am indeed, I confess, removed far from your sight by a most just right. Nevertheless I will still look with my mind toward that holy temple of yours, as a sure pledge of your clemency toward those who implore your help in their misery."

units.la: In ὑποθέσει duo occurrunt, παραμολογία & ἀντιφώνησις[?].
units.tr: Two things occur in the hypothesis: paramologia [παραμολογία] and antiphonesis [ἀντιφώνησις].

units.la: παραμολογία[?] de praesenti calamitate: Sũ, fateor, iusto tuo iudicio è conspectu tuo summotus, sic ut nihil sit quod nō videatur testari te mihi implacabiliter irasci. Ac id me nō parum afficit & terret, quod de reprobis dixit Psaltes: Vultus Iehouae super facientes malum, ut exscindat è terra memoriam eorum: Psal.34.16. Nota est Caini desperatis oratio: Ecce eiecisti me hodie à facie terrae, & à facie tua abscondar: eroq[?] vagus & profugus in terra, &c. Et illud de eodem: Egressus est Cain à facie Iehouae: v.16. Ex hac concessione[?] liquet, qualem Deum homo consternatus sibi fingat, uidelicet, alienū prorsus à miseris, implacabilem, ignem consumentem. Heb.12.29.Deut.4.24. Ne-que uero raro fit, ut etiam electi, serenae faciei Dei conspectu ad tepus orbati, re-probis se haud dissimiles esse opinentur.
units.tr: The paramologia concerns the present calamity: "I am, I admit, removed from your sight by your just judgment, so that nothing seems to testify more than that you are implacably angry with me. This affects and terrifies me no little, because the Psalmist said of the reprobate: The face of the LORD is against those who do evil, to cut off the memory of them from the earth" (Ps. 34:16). The lament of the despairing Cain is well known: "Behold, you have driven me out this day from the face of the earth, and I shall be hidden from your face; I shall be a fugitive and a wanderer on the earth," etc. And of the same man: "Cain went out from the presence of the LORD" (Gen. 4:16). From this admission it is clear what kind of God a terrified man imagines for himself: one utterly alien to the miserable, implacable, a consuming fire (Heb. 12:29; Deut. 4:24). Nor is it rare that even the elect, when for a time deprived of the sight of God's serene face, think themselves not unlike the reprobate.

units.la: Ἀντιπαγωγὴ[?] autem eluctantis & emerge-tis ex istis fluctibus fidei, haec est: Fretus tamen immensa tua potentia & misericordia, spero me in templo tuo εὐχαριστικὰ[?] sacrificia tibi oblaturum esse, summo cum meo gaudio. Scio enim te uiam inuenire posse, & apud te non esse illum uerbū impossibile. Luc.1.37.
units.tr: The antiplegia [Ἀντιπαγωγὴ] of one who struggles and emerges from these waves of faith is this: "Yet, relying on your immense power and mercy, I hope that in your temple I shall offer to you sacrifices of thanksgiving [εὐχαριστικὰ], with the greatest joy. For I know that you can find a way, and that with you that word is not impossible" (Luke 1:37).

units.la: Παραλλήλον.[?]
units.tr: Parallelon.

units.la: Et ego dicebam dum festinare: Excisus sum ab oculis tuis: uerum audisti uocem deprecationum mearum, cum clamare ad te. Psal.31,23.[?]
units.tr: "And I said in my haste: I am cut off from your eyes; but you heard the voice of my supplications when I cried to you" (Ps. 31:23).

units.la: THESIS.
units.tr: THESIS.

units.la: Vt cum desperationis tentatione ue-hementer luctatur fides: sic eam tandem fortiter insurgens uincit.
units.tr: As faith struggles vehemently with the temptation of despair, so, rising up bravely, it at length overcomes it.

units.la: Sic argumentatur Caro: Quis dubitet ei desperandum, quem à sua facie reiecit Deus? Te verò reiecit: ut res ipsa docet. Itaq; stolidum fuerit, spem inanem de li-beratione è tanta morte fovere.
units.tr: Thus the flesh reasons: who could doubt that he should despair, whom God has cast from his face? And indeed God has cast you away, as the thing itself shows. Therefore it would be foolish to cherish empty hope of deliverance from so great a death.

units.la: Respondet Fides, primùm ad Maio-rem, aliam esse electorum, aliam repro-borum sorte. Illos ut maximè duriter tra-ctari patiatur Deus, revera tamen[?] nō abij-cit eos à cōspectu suo. Ideo cum Davide precantur: Ne proijcias nos à facie tua, & Spiritum sanctum tuum ne auferas à nobis: Psal.51.11. Hos autem sereni fui vultus amabili aspectu nunquam dignatur Do-minus, quia non novit eos, id est, non agnoscit eos tanquam suos: Matth.7.23.
units.tr: Faith replies, first to the major premise, that the lot of the elect is one thing and that of the reprobate another. Although God allows the former to be treated most harshly, he nevertheless does not cast them from his sight. Hence they pray with David: "Do not cast us away from your face, and do not take your Holy Spirit from us" (Ps. 51:11). But the Lord never deigns to look upon the reprobate with the kindly gaze of his serene countenance, because he does not know them, that is, does not acknowledge them as his own (Matt. 7:23).

units.la: Deinde & ad Minorem per inficiationē[?] eadem respondet. Nam in ea occultè latet paralogismus secūdum non causam ut causam. Ex calamitatibus enim, quae communes fidelibus & infidelibus esse possunt, non rectè colligitur omnimoda reiectio. Atqui si omnibus tā bonis quàm malis communes casus spectes, ex ijs certò colligi non possunt hæc duo, videlicet, electio & reiectio. juxta illud: Etiam amorem, etiam odium nescit homo omnium quæ ante eos sunt. Omnia eveniunt consimiliter omnibus: euentus unus est iusto & impio,&c.Eccles.9.1.&2.
units.tr: Then, by denying the minor, faith answers in the same way. For in it there lurks a hidden paralogism, a fallacy of non-cause as cause. From calamities which can be common to the faithful and the unfaithful, it is not rightly concluded that there is total rejection. Indeed, if you consider calamities common to all, both good and evil, these two things cannot be surely inferred from them, namely election and rejection, according to that saying: "Man knows neither love nor hatred from all that is before him. All things happen alike to all: one event befalls the righteous and the wicked, etc." (Eccles. 9:1-2).

units.la: 1. Nihil dubium est, eo Dei dono tentationem desperationis superari, quo impetrantur spiritualia & corporalia beneficia. Inter hæc enim beneficia nō postremū locum obtinet liberatio à tētatione illa, solicitate ad desperatione. Atqui nō nisi fide illa beneficia impetramus.Matt. 21.22. Quæcunque precando petieritis, si credideritis, accipietis. Fide igitur superamus illam tentationem.
units.tr: 1. There is no doubt that temptation to despair is overcome by that gift of God by which spiritual and bodily benefits are obtained. For among these benefits, deliverance from that temptation which urges toward despair holds no small place. But we obtain these benefits only by faith. "Whatever you ask in prayer, if you believe, you will receive" (Matt. 21:22). Therefore we overcome that temptation by faith.

units.la: 2. Christus Dominus noster inquit: τὰ δυνατὰ τῷ πιστεύοντι[?] Marc.9.23. Ergo etiam ὑπομονὴν[?] illius tentationis uincere, ἀνδρεῖον[?] est fideli homini. Neque uerò aliud eo dicto Saluator noster sibi voluit, quàm nihil esse quod fidelium rectè precantium causa, Deus præstare non possit, aut non uelit. Recte autem orant: Ne nos inducas in tentationem: sed libera nos à malo: Matth.6.13. Itaq; cum tentationis ἐμβασίν[?] precatione fidei obtineant, fide quoque superasse tentationem, recte dicitur. Maior huius syllogismi probatur illo Christi dicto: πιστεύετε ὅτι δύναμαι τοῦτο ποιῆσαι[?]; Creditis me hoc posse facere?
units.tr: 2. Our Lord Christ says: "All things are possible to him who believes" [τὰ δυνατὰ τῷ πιστεύοντι] (Mark 9:23). Therefore to conquer the endurance [ὑπομονὴν] of that temptation is a manly [ἀνδρεῖον] thing for a believer. Nor did our Saviour mean anything else by that saying than that there is nothing which God cannot or will not grant to the faithful who pray rightly. And they pray rightly: "Lead us not into temptation, but deliver us from evil" (Matt. 6:13). Therefore, since they obtain by prayer that the entrance [ἐμβασίν] of temptation be averted, it is rightly said that they have also overcome the temptation by faith. The major premise of this syllogism is proved by that saying of Christ: "Do you believe that I am able to do this?" [πιστεύετε ὅτι δύναμαι τοῦτο ποιῆσαι] (Matt. 9:28).

units.la: Matth.9.28. Instrumento autem,id est fidei,in hoc & similibus dictis id tribuitur, quod proprium est causae efficientis principis,id est,Dei ipsius.
units.tr: Now in this and similar sayings, what is proper to the principal efficient cause, that is, God himself, is ascribed to the instrument, that is, to faith.

units.la: 3. Quis autem dubitet, eo τῷ χαρίσματι [?] uinci desperationis paroxysmum, quod facit ut exstent quae sperantur, & quod demonstrat quae non uidentur:Fidei autem hoc proprium est.Heb.11.1.
units.tr: 3. Who would doubt that the paroxysm of despair is overcome by that gift [τῷ χαρίσματι], which causes things hoped for to be present, and which demonstrates things not seen? And this is proper to faith (Heb. 11:1).

units.la: 4. Id quod mundum uincit,etiam tentationum,quae in mundo nos adoriuntur, παροξυσμοῖς [?] uincit.Sed,ut ait Ioanes:Quicquid natu est ex Deo,uincit mundū: & hęc est uictoria quae uicit mundum, nempe fides nostra. Quis est q uincit mundum,nisi qui credit Iesum esse Christum? 1.Ioan.5.4.5.
units.tr: 4. That which overcomes the world, it also overcomes the paroxysms [παροξυσμοῖς] of temptations which assail us in the world. But, as John says: "Whatever is born of God overcomes the world; and this is the victory which overcomes the world, namely our faith. Who is he who overcomes the world, but he who believes that Jesus is the Christ?" (1 John 5:4-5).

units.la: Det nobis Dominus noster Iesus Christus, ut cum in tentationes inciderimus varias, pro summo id ducamus gaudio; Iac.1.2, & ut sub pedibus nostris Satan cito conteratur: Rom.16.20. nobis videlicet omnibus plene de eo persuasis, quod Dominus noster dixit:Confidite,ego vici mundum.Ioan.16.33.
units.tr: May our Lord Jesus Christ grant us that when we fall into various temptations, we count it the highest joy (James 1:2), and that Satan be quickly crushed under our feet (Rom. 16:20); with all of us fully persuaded of what our Lord said: "Take courage; I have overcome the world" (John 16:33).

units.la: VERSVS V.
units.tr: VERSE 5.

units.la: Obsederant me aquae usq; ad animam: abyssus abyssus undiq; circumdederat me: alligata fuit capiti meo.
units.tr: The waters had surrounded me up to my soul; the deep, the deep, had encompassed me on every side; it was bound about my head.

units.la: Παραφρασις Th.Bezæ.
units.tr: Paraphrase of Theodore Beza.

units.la: Ecce igitur miserum me circumstant a-quæ, ipsam mihi animam præcludentes: hinc & inde me obsidet immensa profundissimi maris uorago: alga ceti aluo innatans,caput circumquaq; constringit.
units.tr: Behold, the waters stand round about me, wretched as I am, shutting up my very life; on this side and that the immense whirlpool of the deepest sea besieges me; seaweed floating in the belly of the whale wraps itself round my head on every side.

units.la: Cùm Deo summè tum iusto, tum bono,impios quidem punienti & malè perdenti, pios autem castiganti & in uiam reuocanti,omnes creaturæ militent: magnum fuerit operæpretium,utrorumque ἀθῷ καὶ πάθῳ [?], dicta & facta, multum sanè dissimilia, obseruare & perpedere. Nam ut illi incredulitate suam & eius effecta, impatientiam, fremitum aduersus Dei iudicium, desperatione, nunquam non pro-dunt: ita hi in silentio & spe fortitudinem suam collocantes, dant Deo gloriam.
units.tr: Since all creatures serve God, who is supremely just, good, and kind, punishing the wicked and destroying them, but chastising the godly and calling them back to the right way, it will be well worth our effort to observe and weigh carefully the words and deeds of each, which are very unlike one another, in both cases, [ἀθῷ καὶ πάθῳ]. For the wicked, through unbelief, always reveal their own nature and its effects: impatience, muttering against God's judgment, and despair. The godly, on the other hand, placing their strength in silence and hope, give glory to God.

units.la: Hoc loco habetur elegantissima ὑποτυ-πωσις periculorum, in quæ seruus Iehouæ, ob detrectatam uocationem diuinam,in cidit. Videbantur totius pelagi fluctus uentiq; coniurati quodammodo aduer-sus eum insurgere, & totidem esse irati & vindicis Dei testimonia. Est aut tacita comparatio fragilitatis humanæ, & tempestatis violentissimæ. Cùm vita nostra sit ἀτμὶς πρὸς ὀλίγον φαινομένη, ἔπειτα δὲ ἀφανιζομένη: Iac.4.14. quàm facile est eam exstinguì, cum homo barbari illius elementi aquæ undis obsessus tenetur, & alga non iam pedes, sed caput inuolutum detinet? Fit autē propitio Dei consilio, ut in inextricabiles malorum labyrinthos pii nonnunquam incidant, & apud seipsos mortis decretum habeant, ne unquam in seipsis confidant, sed in Deo qui mortuos excitat, quique ex tanta morte liberat. 2.Cor.1.9.10. Commemorabile est illud Davidis: Quæ utilitas in sanguine meo, cum descendero in foveam? nūquid confitebitur tibi pulvis? nunquid annuncia-bit veritatem tuam ? Psal.30.10. Et illud prophetæ Ethan Ezaitæ: Usquequò Ie-hovah abscōdes te in seculū, exardescet sicut ignis ira tua?Memeto ego quid sini, quod tempus, propter quid creaveris omnes filios hominum:Psal.89.47.48. Tales sunt etiam sanctissimorum hominum voces, cùm adversorum pondere sunt oppressi, nec respirandi locum esse putant.
units.tr: Here we have a most elegant hypotyposis [ὑποτύπωσις] of the dangers into which the servant of Jehovah fell because he had refused God's call. The waves of the whole sea and the winds seemed in some way to have conspired to rise against him, and each was a witness of God's wrath and vengeance. There is also an implied comparison between human frailty and the most violent storm. Our life is "a vapour that appears for a little time and then vanishes away" [ἀτμὶς πρὸς ὀλίγον φαινομένη, ἔπειτα δὲ ἀφανιζομένη], James 4.14. How easily is it snuffed out when a man is seized and held fast by the waves of that savage element, water, and the seaweed wraps not his feet but his head! God in his good counsel allows the godly sometimes to fall into inextricable labyrinths of evils, and to hold within themselves the sentence of death, so that they may never trust in themselves but in God, who raises the dead and delivers from such great death. 2 Cor. 1.9, 10. Memorable is that saying of David: "What profit is there in my blood, when I go down into the pit? Will the dust confess to you? Will it declare your truth?" Ps. 30.10. And that of the prophet Ethan the Ezrahite: "How long, O Jehovah, will you hide yourself for ever? Will your wrath burn like fire? Remember what I am, and for what time, and why you created all the sons of men," Ps. 89.47, 48. Such are also the cries of the holiest men when they are weighed down by the burden of adversity and think there is no place to breathe.

units.la: Necsanè fides ita leuiter afficitur afflictionum magnitudine, multitudine, & acerbissimo earum sensu, quin infirma caro querulas homini voces exprimat.
units.tr: Nor indeed is faith so lightly affected by the greatness, the multitude, and the most bitter feeling of afflictions that the weak flesh does not force complaining voices from a man.

units.la: Vt haec thesis illustretur, carnis [illegible, ~8 letters] quaedam subiungam.
units.tr: To illustrate this thesis, I will add some words of the flesh [illegible].

units.la: I. Vt terq; quaterq; beati sunt, quibus militat aether, & coiurati veniunt ad classica venti: sic modis omnibus infelices sunt, quibus omnia elementa, omnes creaturae aduersantur. Tibi vero, suggerebat caro Ionae, pelagi vis prope immensa imminet. Itaq; de te actum iam esse, quinā te quaesso, dubitare potes?
units.tr: I. Just as those are doubly and trebly blessed to whom the sky fights on their side and the winds come running at the sound of the trumpet, so those are unhappy in every way against whom all the elements and all creatures are opposed. The flesh of Jonah was suggesting to you: the force of the sea hangs over you, almost immeasurable. So it is already all over with you. Who, I beg you, could doubt it?

units.la: 2. Viden' ut abyssus abyssum invocet ad vocem canalium Dei, & omnes inundationes eius & fluctus super te transeant? Psal. 42.7. Repete igitur & illud Psal. 40.12. ut discas te tuo scelere haec ingentia mala tibi accersiuisse: Circumdederunt me mala, ita ut non sit eorum numerus: comprehenderunt me iniquitates meae.
units.tr: 2. Do you see how deep calls to deep at the voice of God's waterspouts, and all his floods and waves pass over you? Ps. 42.7. Repeat then also Ps. 40.12, so that you may learn that you have brought these huge evils upon yourself by your own wickedness: "Evils have surrounded me without number; my iniquities have overtaken me."

units.la: Quam multis studiosis iuvenibus hoc tempore[?], ob φιλαλήθειαν[?] stipendijs suis privatis, ab ijs qui clero Domini nunc imperare & iugum imponere conatur, caro has cogitationes suggerit: Quousq; conflictaberis[?] cum exilij & cum paupertatis incommodis? Quamdiu tandem contumeliofq; uoces de inobedientia & contumacia erga praeceptores, ut aiunt, bene meritos & alios, tibi ferendae erunt? Cur non mittis ad iniquitatem manus tuas, Psal.125.3. ut aliqua saltem malorum relaxatione, & uitae huius adminiculorum parte, tandem aliquando potiaris?
units.tr: How many eager young men at this time, for love of truth [φιλαλήθειαν], are deprived of their private stipends by those who now try to rule the clergy of the Lord and to impose a yoke on them! The flesh suggests these thoughts: "How long will you struggle with the hardships of exile and poverty? How long will you have to bear the insulting words about disobedience and contumacy towards your teachers, who, as they say, have deserved well, and towards others? Why do you not stretch out your hands to iniquity, Ps. 125.3, so that at least by some relief from these evils and by some part of the supports of this life you may at last obtain something?"

units.la: 3. Porro, si per patientia possidere nos decet animas nostras, cur acerbissimum istum multiplicium, quibus laboras, malorum sensum tibi Deus ille tuus, in quo speras, non mitigat, ut tolerabilior sit, cum eum auferre nolit? Itane delectatur tuis miseriis & angoribus?
units.tr: 3. Furthermore, if we ought to possess our souls in patience, why does that God of yours, in whom you hope, not lessen for you the very bitter sense of the many evils with which you labour, so that it may be more bearable, since he is unwilling to remove it? Does he take pleasure in your miseries and anguish?

units.la: Exempla.
units.tr: Examples.

units.la: Iobus:Pereat, dicebat ille, dies in qua natus sum, & nox quae dixit: Conceptus est nir[?]. Dies illa sit tenebrae: non requirat illam Deus desuper, nec splendeat super illam lux, & c. Iob.3.3. & sequentibus. Ieremias:Vae mihi mater mea, quod genuisti me, virum rixae & virum discordię toti terrę:non foeneravi eis, nec foenerati sunt mihi: omnes maledicunt mihi. Ier.15.10.
units.tr: Job said: "Let the day perish in which I was born, and the night which said: a man is conceived. Let that day be darkness; let God above not seek it, nor light shine upon it," etc., Job 3.3 and following. Jeremiah: "Woe is me, my mother, that you bore me, a man of strife and a man of discord to all the land. I have not lent to them, nor have they lent to me; yet all of them curse me," Jer. 15.10.

units.la: Vt autè afflictionum, undarum in mo-rem sibi invicem succedetium, ἐπιούσαις[?]: ita quoq; acerrima carnis adversus Spiritum lusta, patheticas uoces Sanctis di-stat[?]. Talis est & illa Pauli Apostoli: De-lector lege Dei, quod ad interiorem hominem: sed video aliam legem in membris meis, rebellantem legi mentis meæ, & captiuum reddentem me legi peccati, quæ est in membris meis. Miser ego homo, quis me eripiet ex isto corpore mortis? Rom.7.22.23.24.
units.tr: But just as afflictions succeed one another like waves, so the most bitter struggle of the flesh against the Spirit also produces passionate cries in the saints. Such is that of the apostle Paul: "I delight in the law of God according to the inner man, but I see another law in my members, fighting against the law of my mind and making me captive to the law of sin which is in my members. Wretched man that I am, who will deliver me from this body of death?" Rom. 7.22, 23, 24.

units.la: VERSVS VI.
units.tr: VERSE 6.

units.la: Ad radices montium descenderam: ter-ra cum vectibus suis erat circa me in secu-lum: sed ascendere fecisti vitam meam è sepulcro, Iehouah Deus mi.
units.tr: I went down to the roots of the mountains; the earth with its bars was around me for ever: but you brought up my life from the grave, O Jehovah my God.

units.la: Παράφρασις.
units.tr: Paraphrase.

units.la: Ad infimos usque intra mare latantes montium anfractus deveni; nulla vi alterius quàm tua frangendis terra repagulis conclusus. Et tamen Iehouah mi Deus, tu me ex isto intimo specu salvum & incolumem eruisti.
units.tr: I went down to the lowest depths of the mountains' winding valleys, which lie under the sea, and was shut in by the earth's bars, which no power but yours could break. Yet you, Jehovah my God, rescued me safe and sound from that innermost pit.

units.la: EXPLICATIO.
units.tr: EXPLANATION.

units.la: Propheta noster suo ipsius exemplo in medium adducto, duo praeclara Dei μεγα λέα[?], quae ordine sibi succedunt, uidelicet Mortificationem & Viuificationem, celebrat. Vtrumq; sane Deo tribuitur 1.Sam. 2.6. Iehouah occidit & uiuificat: descendere facit ad sepulcrum, & ascendere facit e sepulcro.
units.tr: Our prophet, bringing forward his own experience as an example, celebrates two notable works of God that follow one another in order, namely mortification and vivification. Both are certainly ascribed to God in 1 Sam. 2.6: "The LORD kills and makes alive; he brings down to the grave and brings up again."

units.la: Quomodo autem suos mortificat Dominus?
units.tr: But how does the Lord mortify his people?

units.la: Cum sensum praesentiae gratiae suae aliquandiu subducit, ut homo suae uanitatis & fragilitatis coarguatur. Id fit, cum eo res illius redeunt, ut cum Dauide pre-cetur[?]. Quousque Iehouah oblitus fceris mei penitus? Quousque abscondes faciem tuam a me? Quamdiu disponam consilia in anima mea? anxietatem in corde meo quotidie? Vsquequo exaltabitur inimicus meus supra me? Psal. 13.1.2.
units.tr: By withdrawing for a time the sense of his grace's presence, so that a man is shown up as vain and frail. This happens when his affairs go badly, so that he prays with David: "How long, LORD, will you forget me utterly? How long will you hide your face from me? How long shall I take counsel in my soul, having anxiety in my heart daily? How long shall my enemy be exalted over me?" Ps. 13.1.2.

units.la: Quomodo autem eosdem uiuificat?
units.tr: But how does he make the same people alive?

units.la: Cum paterno uultu eos respiciens, mala uel mitigat, uel tollit, uel bonorum spiritualium communionem longe ea exuberare facit. Atq; haec & alia petens Dauid: Respice, ait, & exaudi me Iehouah Deus meus: illumina oculos meos, ne ob dormiam in morte. Psal. eode, v.3. Item: Beatus est qui prudenter iudicat de afflicto sto:nam in die calamitatis liberabit eum Iehouah.Iehouah custodiet eum, & uitæ restituet eum: beatus erit in terra, & non tradet eum libidini inimicorum eius. Psal. 41.1.2.&c.
units.tr: By looking on them with a fatherly countenance, he either eases or removes their troubles, or makes their share in spiritual goods far outweigh them. Seeking these things and others, David says: "Look upon me, and hear me, Jehovah my God; enlighten my eyes, lest I sleep the sleep of death." Ps. 13, same, v. 3. Likewise: "Blessed is the one who judges wisely concerning the afflicted; for in the day of calamity Jehovah will deliver him. Jehovah will keep him and restore him to life; he will be blessed upon the earth, and he will not give him over to the desire of his enemies." Ps. 41.1.2, etc.

units.la: Sed cur prius hominem mortificat Deus, quàm eundem uiuificet?
units.tr: But why does God mortify a man before he makes him alive?

units.la: Primùm ut eiûs erroribus, qui ante-quâ ille mortificetur, eidè Sophisticè imponunt, medeatur. Psal. 119.67. Priusquâ humiliarer, ego uagabar: sed nunc sermonem tuum custodio. Animi nostri φιλαυ-τία fascinati luxuriant, ignari uidelicet suorum malorum. At ubi Dei ferulam sen-serunt, ignorantiam, iniusticiam, infirmi-tatem suam magno suo bono agnoscunt & deplorant. Deinde, ut nostræ mise-riæ sensus, diuinorum beneficiorum magnitudinem & dulcedinem nobis com-mendet. Nemo lucis & sanitatis commoda recte æstimat, nisi qui caliginis & morborum incommoda sensit. Ita etiam nemo uiuificationis bonum rite perpendit, nisi qui iam antea sese mortificatum fuisse probè commeminit.
units.tr: First, so that he may heal the errors of those who, before the man is mortified, deceive him with their sophistry. Ps. 119.67: "Before I was humbled I went astray, but now I keep your word." Our minds, bewitched by self-love, grow rank, ignorant, of course, of their own evils. But when they feel God's rod, they recognise and lament their ignorance, injustice and weakness, to their great good. Second, so that the sense of our misery may commend to us the greatness and sweetness of God's blessings. No one rightly values the benefits of light and health unless he has felt the disadvantages of darkness and sickness. So too no one weighs the good of making alive properly unless he remembers well that he was first mortified.

units.la: THESIS.
units.tr: THESIS.

units.la: Desperationis tentationem ideo supe-rat sat[?] fides,quia omnipotentiæ Dei nec ho-minum fragilitatem & mala ipsis ineui-tabilia,nec vires omniu creaturarum re-sistere posse,intelligit.
units.tr: Faith overcomes the temptation of despair because it understands that neither the frailty of men, nor the evils that are unavoidable for them, nor the powers of all creatures, can resist the omnipotence of God.

units.la: Rationes eius hæ sunt, quibus confirmatur.
units.tr: These are the reasons by which this is confirmed.

units.la: 1. Dei potentia per infirmitatem humanam perficitur.2.Cor.12.9.
units.tr: 1. God's power is made perfect in human weakness. 2 Cor. 12.9.

units.la: 2. Deus infirmitati nostræ medetur. Dat lasso fortitudinem: & cui non sunt vires,robur multiplicat.Ifa.40.29.
units.tr: 2. God heals our weakness. He gives strength to the weary, and multiplies power to the one who has none. Isa. 40.29.

units.la: 3. Omnes creaturas, ut iudiciorum Dei executioni: sic eiusdem benedictioni ser-vire oportet, cum vel nutu eas evocat.
units.tr: 3. All creatures ought to serve the execution of God's judgements, and likewise his blessing, since he calls them forth even by a nod.

units.la: 4. Deus redemptor & vivificator est. Idem omnipotens & verax est. Is vivifi-cat mortuos, & vocat quæ non sunt, tanquam sint: potest facere quod promisit. Rom.4.17.21.
units.tr: 4. God is redeemer and vivifier. The same God is omnipotent and true. He makes the dead alive, and calls those things that are not as though they were. He is able to do what he has promised. Rom. 4.17.21.

units.la: VERSVS VII.
units.tr: VERSE 7.

units.la: Quum deficeret in me anima mea, Iehova recordatus sum: & venit oratio mea ad templum sanctitatis tuæ.
units.tr: When my soul was fainting within me, I remembered Jehovah; and my prayer came to your holy temple.

units.la: Παραφραστής.
units.tr: Paraphrast.

units.la: Quamuis enim ipsa me vita destitue-ret, tamen sum recordatus, Iehova: & ad sanctu[?] templum tuum, in quo nimirum[?] te mente contemplabar, preces meæ peruenerunt.
units.tr: For although life itself was forsaking me, yet I remembered you, Jehovah; and my prayers reached your holy temple, where, of course, I contemplated you in my mind.

units.la: Ex hoc versu colligere licet, quid causæ sit, quòd Sancti, dum in omnibus premuntur, non tamé coarctantur: hæsitant, at non prorsus hæret. 2.Cor.4.8. Recordantur enim Iehouæ, quem misericordé & propensum esse ad gratiam, tardum ad iram, multum clementia & veritate, expe-rientia docti, statuunt. Psal.86.15. Ac in silentio & spe præstolantur tempus illud gratuitæ Dei beneuolentiæ, in quo Deus pro magnitudine clemetiæ suę respodet in veritate salutis servis suis. Psal.69.13.
units.tr: From this verse we may gather the reason why the saints, though pressed on every side, are nevertheless not hemmed in: they waver, but are not utterly stuck fast. 2 Cor. 4.8. For they remember Jehovah, whom, taught by experience, they hold to be merciful and inclined to grace, slow to anger, and abounding in clemency and truth. Ps. 86.15. And in silence and hope they await that time of God's free goodwill, in which God, according to the greatness of his mercy, will answer his servants with the truth of salvation. Ps. 69.13.

units.la: THESIS.
units.tr: THESIS.

units.la: Monet quinetiam fides, ut non tam in nostra mala, quæ inevitabile exitium allatura videntur: quàm in Iehouam omni potetem & beneficum respiciamus, plenè de precum nostrarum exauditione persuasi.
units.tr: Faith also advises us to look not so much at our evils, which seem to bring inevitable ruin, as at Jehovah, almighty and beneficent, being fully persuaded that our prayers will be heard.

units.la: Tria in hac thesi docendi causa per-stringemus. Primum est, de mortis decreto, quod apud se Sancti nonnúquam habent. Secundum, de recordatione Ie-houæ. Tertium, de fiducia exauditionis precum. Faciunt haec omnia mirifice ad institutionem & consolationem nostram.
units.tr: For the sake of teaching, we will touch on three points in this thesis. The first concerns the decree of death, which the saints sometimes hold within themselves. The second concerns the remembrance of Jehovah. The third concerns confidence that prayers are heard. All these things contribute wonderfully to our instruction and consolation.

units.la: 1. Περὶ τῆς ἀπονεκρώσεως τῆς θνητότητος [?]
units.tr: 1. On the putting to death of mortality [Περὶ τῆς ἀπονεκρώσεως τῆς θνητότητος]

units.la: Paulus 2. Cor. 1. 9. decretum mortis uo cat, cum homini omnia praesentem mortem intentare, nec ulla uitae huius spes reliqua esse uidetur: nisi Deus ὥσπερ ἀπὸ μι- χνῶς [?] interueniens, homine e morte tanta eripiat.
units.tr: Paul (2 Cor. 1.9) calls it a sentence of death when every circumstance threatens a man with present death and no hope of this life seems left, unless God intervenes, as if from a machine [ὥσπερ ἀπὸ μηχανῆς], and snatches the man from so great a death.

units.la: Optimo autem Dei consilio eo res nostrae interdum adducuntur, ut necin nobis ipsis, necin ullis rebus humanis, uel tantillum praesidij sit reliquum: ne confidamus in nobis ipsis, sed in Deo, qui mortuos excitat. 2. Cor. 1. 9. & neiam reti nostro sacrificare, sed liberatione nostram in solidum Deo soli acceptam ferre discamus.
units.tr: By God's best counsel, however, our affairs are sometimes brought to the point where there is not even the slightest help left in ourselves or in any human things, so that we may not trust in ourselves but in God, who raises the dead (2 Cor. 1.9); and so that we may learn not to sacrifice to our own net, but to ascribe our deliverance wholly to God alone.

units.la: Sic enim nobis secundae caussae blandiuntur, ut cum ἐξω βελῶν nobis constituti uidemur, de diuino praesidio non admodum laboremus: et cum aduersa ingruunt, ad proxima praesidia properè confugiamus, hisq; ἀντιτύπ[?] & respirationem à malis (si quae detur) non sine nefaria idololatria acceptam libenter feramus: at si illa nos fallant, aegrè tandem ad primae & omnipotentis caussae (utloquuntur) patrocinium & opem confugia-mus. mus. Actum demum praeclarè nobiscū agitur, cum de humanis praesidiis desperantes, ad Deum confugimus, cum Dauid de orantes: Serua nos Deus, quia penetrârunt aquæ usque ad animam. Jam demersi sumus in lutum profundum, & ubi consistere non possumus. Psal.69.1.2.
units.tr: For secondary causes flatter us in such a way that, when we seem to be placed beyond the reach of missiles, we do not greatly trouble ourselves about divine protection; and when adversity attacks, we hastily flee to nearby aids, and gladly accept from them relief from evils (if any is given), not without wicked idolatry. But if those aids deceive us, we reluctantly at last take refuge in the protection and help of the first and almighty cause, as they say. Indeed, our affairs are then at last handled splendidly for us, when, despairing of human aids, we flee to God, praying with David: "Save us, God, for the waters have come up to the soul. Now we have sunk into deep mire, where we cannot stand." Ps. 69.1.2.

units.la: 2. De recordatione Iehouæ.
units.tr: 2. Of the remembrance of Jehovah.

units.la: Quomodo tota Ecclesia Domini Dei sui recordetur, ex hoc illius hymno discimus. Isa.63.7. Miserationes Iehouæ memoria repetam, & laudes Iehouæ pro omnibus quæ contulit nobis Iehouah, & multiplex bonum domui Israel, quod contulit eis secundum misericordiam suam, & secundum multitudinem miserationum suarum. Et Dauid: Ingrediar, ait, potentias Iehouæ, memor ero iustitiæ tuæ soli-us. Psal.71.16.
units.tr: How the whole Church of the Lord her God remembers him, we learn from this hymn. Isa. 63.7. "I will recount the mercies of Jehovah and the praises of Jehovah, for all that Jehovah has bestowed on us, and the great goodness toward the house of Israel, which he has bestowed on them according to his mercy and according to the abundance of his mercies." And David says: "I will come in the strength of Jehovah; I will remember your righteousness alone." Ps. 71.16.

units.la: Per fidem autem Domini Dei sui recordantur fideles, cum sibi persuadent Custodem Israelis non dormitare neque dormire: esse custodē suum, & umbram dexterae: custodire quinetiam egressum & introitum nostrum. Psal.121.4.5.&8.
units.tr: By faith, however, the faithful remember the Lord their God, when they persuade themselves that the Keeper of Israel neither slumbers nor sleeps, that he is their keeper and the shade at their right hand, and that he also guards their going out and their coming in. Ps. 121.4, 5, 8.

units.la: Vt autem Solis lumen clarisimum nubes oppositae non raro obscurant, quæ tamen[?] radijs solis paulo post discutiuntur ita carnis intelligentia nonnunquam caliginem infert menti, quae tamen fidei lu-cem Sole iusticiae Christo Domino no-stro mentibus piis inferente, discutitur.
units.tr: As clouds placed before the sun's brightest light often obscure it, yet are soon dispersed by its rays, so human understanding sometimes casts a darkness over the mind; yet this darkness is dispelled when Christ our Lord, the Sun of Righteousness, brings the light of faith into pious minds.

units.la: ȝ[?]. De fiducia exauditionis precum.
units.tr: 3. On confidence that prayers are heard.

units.la: Cum fides sit πληροφορία[?] de veracitate, omnipotentia, omniscientia & misericordia Dei, non relinquit fidelem, in Spiritu & veritate orante, animi dubium de exauditione.Repetit enim dulcissimas pro missiones de exauditione precum, e quarum numero hae sunt.
units.tr: Since faith is a full assurance [πληροφορία] concerning the truthfulness, omnipotence, omniscience and mercy of God, it does not leave the faithful man, praying in spirit and in truth, in doubt about being heard. For it repeats the sweetest promises of being heard in prayer, of which these are among the number:

units.la: Psal.50.15. Invoca me in die tribulationis, & eruam te, & glorificabis me.
units.tr: Ps. 50.15. "Call upon me in the day of trouble, and I will deliver you, and you shall glorify me."

units.la: Psal.91.15. Invocat me, itaq; respondebo ei: cum ipso sum in tribulatione.
units.tr: Ps. 91.15. "He calls upon me, and I will answer him; I am with him in trouble."

units.la: Matt.7.11. Si vos igitur, cum sitis mali, noftis dona bona dare liberis vestris, quanto magis Pater vester qui est in coe-lis, dabit bona iis qui ab ipso petent?
units.tr: Matt. 7.11. "If you then, being evil, know how to give good gifts to your children, how much more will your Father who is in heaven give good things to those who ask him?"
