units.la: Matt.21.22. Et quaecunq; precando petieritis, si credideritis, accipietis.
units.tr: Matt. 21.22. "And whatever you ask in prayer, if you believe, you will receive."

units.la: Iac.5.16. Multum valet deprecatio iusti efficax.
units.tr: Jas. 5.16. "The effective prayer of a righteous man avails much."

units.la: VERSVS VIII.
units.tr: VERSE 8.

units.la: Qui obseruant uanitates mendaces, mi-sericordiam eius (id est, Dei) derelinquāt, Παράφρασις.
units.tr: Those who observe lying vanities forsake their mercy (that is, God's), Paraphrase [Παράφρασις].

units.la: Colant itaq;, quicunq; uolet, uanissima sua commenta, & ultrò sese priuent clemen-tia tua beneficio.
units.tr: Let them therefore worship, whoever wishes, their most empty inventions, and of their own accord deprive themselves of the benefit of your mercy.

units.la: Παραφράστης [?] dictum. Psal.31.6.
units.tr: Called Paraphrastes [Παραφράστης]. Ps. 31.6.

units.la: Odio habui obseruantes uanitates fallaces: ego autem in Iehouah confido.
units.tr: I hate those who observe deceptive vanities; but I trust in Jehovah.

units.la: EXPOSITIO.
units.tr: EXPOSITION.

units.la: Nemo potest duobus dominis seruire. aut enim unum habebit odio, & alterum diliget: aut uni adhærebit, & alterum contemnet: Matt.6.24. Itaq; qui adido-la sua conuertuntur, & spem in creaturis ponentes, illa colunt, misericordiæ diuinæ beneficijs seipsos spoliant. Qui uerò spem ponunt in Deo uiuo, nunquam pudefient: Psal.31.1. Rom.5.5. acuere [?] beati in eo erunt: Psal.2.12.
units.tr: No one can serve two masters: for either he will hate the one and love the other, or he will cling to the one and despise the other. Matt. 6.24. So those who turn to their idols, placing their hope in creatures and worshipping them, strip themselves of the benefits of divine mercy. But those who place their hope in the living God will never be put to shame (Ps. 31.1; Rom. 5.5), and blessed are all who trust in him (Ps. 2.12).

units.la: Ex his liquet, diuersa esse hominū studia. Nam alij quidem præterito Creatore, seruiunt rebus creatis: Rom.1.25. alij uerò spem fixam habet in Deo uiuo, qui est cōseruator omnium hominum, maximè verò fidelium; 1.Tim.4.10. Illi obseruant vanitates mendaces, dum & idola, quæ nihil in mundo sunt (1.Cor.8.4.) superstitiosè colunt, & brachij carnis, verè σύνεσιν[?] τῇ ἐπινοίᾳ[?] nituntur: & derelinquunt misericordiam Dei. Hi autem verum Deū in spiritu & veritate adorant: Ioan.4.24. & lętantur roboratam esse Dei misericordiam super timentes eum, secundum altitudinem cœli super terram. Psal.103.11.
units.tr: From these things it is clear that men's pursuits are different. For some, having left the Creator behind, serve created things (Rom. 1.25); but others have their hope fixed on the living God, who is the preserver of all men, and especially of the faithful (1 Tim. 4.10). The former observe lying vanities, while they superstitiously worship idols, which are nothing in the world (1 Cor. 8.4), and truly rely on the understanding of their own invention [σύνεσις, ἐπίνοια] and the arm of flesh, and so forsake the mercy of God. The latter, however, worship the true God in spirit and in truth (John 4.24), and rejoice that God's mercy is strengthened toward those who fear him, as high as the heavens are above the earth (Ps. 103.11).

units.la: THESIS.
units.tr: THESIS.

units.la: Quicunq; in creaturis potius quàm in Creatore confidunt, sibi ipsis & aliis, maximo utrorumq; malo, imponunt.
units.tr: Whoever trusts in creatures rather than in the Creator imposes a great evil on both himself and others.

units.la: Plusquam sacrilega audacia est, si quis prudens & sciens: flagitiosa autem igno-rantia, si quis nescius, terminos divinæ τῆς συντάξίας[?] moveat, & ἀταξίαν[?], creaturis quæ soli Creatori competunt deferenté, introducat. Dementiæ etiam est, idolis vanissimis ea tribuere, quæ viuentis & omnipotentis Dei propria sunt: & lignū appellare Patrem; ac gloriam incorruptibilis Dei commutare formata imagine mortalis hominis, & volucrum, & quadrupedum, & reptili-um.Rom.1.23.
units.tr: It is more than sacrilegious audacity if anyone, knowingly and wittingly, moves the bounds of the divine order [σύνταξις] and introduces disorder [ἀταξία], attributing to creatures what belongs only to the Creator; and it is the folly of ignorance if someone does so unknowingly. It is also madness to ascribe to most empty idols what belongs to the living and omnipotent God: to call a piece of wood "Father," and to exchange the glory of the incorruptible God for the form of a mortal man, or of birds, four-footed beasts and reptiles. Rom. 1.23.

units.la: MULTIS MODIS HOMINES ψυχικὸς[?] observare vanitates mendaces, hæc inductio perspicuè ostendit.
units.tr: IN MANY WAYS MEN [ψυχικοί] OBSERVE LYING VANITIES; this induction clearly shows.

units.la: 1. Amor mundi tantus in illis est, ut sint κοσμοι[?] in mundo. Iac.4.4. Adulteri & adulteræ, nescitis amicitiam mundi, inimiciti-am esse cum Deo? Quicunque ergo vo-luerit amicus esse mundi, inimicus Dei constituitur.
units.tr: 1. Their love of the world is so great that they are worldly [κοσμικοί] in the world. Jas. 4.4. "Adulterers and adulteresses, do you not know that friendship with the world is enmity with God? Whoever therefore wishes to be a friend of the world is constituted an enemy of God."

units.la: 2. Idolomania in illis tanta est, ut quidam illorum dicant ligno, Pater meus es tu: & lapidi, Tu me genuisti. nam obvertunt Jehouæ cervicem, & nō faciem. Jer. 2.27.
units.tr: 2. Their idolatry is so great that some of them say to a tree, "You are my father," and to a stone, "You have begotten me." For they turn the back of the neck to Jehovah and not the face. Jer. 2.27.

units.la: Cæteri paulò prudentiores, veritatem in iniustitia detinent, Deiq; veritatem mutant in mendaciu, & colunt seruiuntq; rebus creatis, &c. Rom.1.18.&25.
units.tr: Others, rather more prudent, hold the truth in unrighteousness, and exchange the truth of God for a lie, and worship and serve created things, etc. Rom. 1.18, 25.

units.la: 3. Terrenas quinetiam opes cœlestibus anteponunt, contra expressum Domini præceptum: Ne thesauros congerite in terra, ubi tinea & erosio corrumpit, & ubi fures perfodiunt & furantur. Sed congerite vobis thesauros in cœlo, &c. Matthæi 6.19.20.
units.tr: 3. Moreover, they place earthly riches above heavenly ones, against the express command of the Lord: "Do not lay up for yourselves treasures on earth, where moth and rust corrupt, and where thieves break in and steal. But lay up for yourselves treasures in heaven," etc. Matt. 6.19, 20.

units.la: 4. Valetudinem prosperam, si Deus nō statim concedat, vel à Satana sibi petendam ducunt. Exemplo est Ahasias Rex Iudæ, 2.Reg.1.
units.tr: 4. If God does not at once grant them good health, they think it must be sought from Satan. An example is Ahaziah, king of Judah. 2 Kings 1.

units.la: 5. Victoriam & successus uel à præsidijs humanis, uel à Sacramētis & alijs rebus, quorum longè alij fines sunt, pefendos putant, Vt Israelitæ cladis à Philistæis sibi illatæ caussam esse putarunt, quòd Arca fœderis non præsto esset in castris, 1.Sam.4.3.
units.tr: 5. They think that victory and success are to be sought either from human defences, or from the sacraments and other things, whose ends are quite different. So the Israelites thought the cause of their defeat by the Philistines was that the ark of the covenant was not present in the camp. 1 Sam. 4.3.

units.la: 6. In Repub. & alijs formis diuinæ τῆς σὺταξίας[?], nō huc omnia referunt, ut exemplo Dauidis, Regis optimi, Dei consilio seruiant: Act.13.36. sed ut dignitati, quæ-stui, œconomiæ, liberis, clientibus[?] suis consulant.
units.tr: 6. In the commonwealth and in other forms of the divine order, they do not refer everything to this end: that, as in the example of David, the best of kings, they serve God's counsel (Acts 13.36), but rather that they look after their own dignity, gain, household, children and clients.

units.la: 7. Salutem, cum de ea cogitare lubet, si non ex asse suis meritis, tamen partim si-bi ipsis[?], partim Christo acceptam ferunt.
units.tr: 7. When they are minded to think of salvation, they ascribe it, if not wholly to their own merits, then partly to themselves and partly to Christ.

units.la: 8. Ut cætera præteream, ex Sacramentis & operibus manuum suarum, ἀλλὰ[?] sibi fabricant: & corde recedentes, ore Deo appropinquant, frustra Deum colentes, cum doceant doctrinas quæ sunt præ-cepta hominum. Matth.15.9. Atqui, ut ait diuinus ille noster Apostolus, corpora his exercitatio paululum habet utilitatis; pietas autem ad omnia utilis est, ut quæ promissionem habeat uitæ præsentis & futuræ. 1.Tim.4.8.
units.tr: 8. To pass over the rest, they fashion for themselves, out of sacraments and the works of their hands, [something else]; and withdrawing in heart, they draw near to God with their mouths, worshipping God in vain, since they teach doctrines which are human precepts (Matt. 15.9). Yet, as that divine Apostle of ours says, bodily exercise is of little use, but godliness is profitable for all things, since it has the promise of the present life and of the life to come (1 Tim. 4.8).

units.la: Atq; non dissimile est de cæteris omnibus hominum occupationibus iudicium. Quare mirū uideri non debet,quòd misericordia Dei, quem auersantur, seipsos priuare, seu eam derelinquere dicā-tur, quemadmodum Dominus apud Ieremiam de idololatris ait: Duo mala fecit populus meus: me dereliquerunt venam aquæ viuæ, ut effoderent sibi cisternas, cisternas confractas, quæ non continent aquas. Ierem.2.13.
units.tr: And the judgment on all the other occupations of men is no different. Therefore it ought not to seem strange that men who turn away from the mercy of God are said to deprive themselves of it, or to forsake it, just as the Lord says through Jeremiah concerning idolaters: "My people have committed two evils: they have forsaken me, the fountain of living water, to dig for themselves cisterns, broken cisterns, which hold no water." Jer. 2.13.

units.la: Sedenim quid vetat, quo minus hominum vanitates mendaces obseruatium, eoq; misericordiam Domini deserentiū descriptiones è Paulinis Epistolis adducamus?
units.tr: But why should anything prevent us from adducing, from the Pauline Epistles, descriptions of those who observe men's lying vanities and so forsake the mercy of the Lord?

units.la: 1.Cor.12,2.Scitis uos Gentes fuisse,qui ad idola illa mota,prout rapi contigisset, abripiebamini.
units.tr: 1 Cor. 12.2. "You know that you were Gentiles, carried away to those dumb idols, however you happened to be led."

units.la: Eph.2.12. Vos, inquam, illo tepore fuistis absq; Christo, alieni à Repub.Israelis, extranei à pactis promissionis, spem non habentes, & Dei expertes in mundo.
units.tr: Eph. 2.12. "You, I say, were at that time without Christ, aliens from the commonwealth of Israel, strangers to the covenants of promise, having no hope and without God in the world."

units.la: Alia tamé est eorum sors, qui initiò μυ[?]- ἀγωγῆς[?] vocantur ad participandam sortem tem Sanctorum in lumine, & quibus in tenebris & umbra mortis sedentib. Christus illucescit: alia eorum qui in tenebris & peccatis suis male pereunt, nunquam eos respiciente Christo, in quo electi non erant antequam iacta essent mundi fundamenta.
units.tr: Yet the lot of those is different who are at first called to share the inheritance of the saints in light, and upon whom Christ dawns while they sit in darkness and the shadow of death; and different is the lot of those who perish miserably in their darkness and sins, Christ never looking upon them, since they were not chosen in him before the foundation of the world was laid.

units.la: VERSVS IX.
units.tr: VERSE 9.

units.la: Ego vero cum voce laudis sacrificabo tibi, & quae vovi reddam. Salus est Iehovae.
units.tr: But I will sacrifice to you with a voice of praise, and I will pay what I have vowed. Salvation belongs to Jehovah.

units.la: Παραφρασις.
units.tr: Paraphrase [Παράφρασις].

units.la: At ego palam, editaque voce, potetiam & bonitatem tuam singularem depraedicans, sacrificia tibi voti reus persoluam. Tu siquidem unus, ut ex meo unius exemplo satis superque constat, servare quoscunque libuit potes.
units.tr: But I, openly and with a raised voice, proclaiming your power and your singular goodness, will pay to you the sacrifices of my vow, as one bound by it. For you alone, as my own single example sufficiently and more than sufficiently shows, can save whomever you please.

units.la: SYLLOGISMVS
units.tr: SYLLOGISM

units.la: τῆς λέξεως.
units.tr: Of the wording [τῆς λέξεως].

units.la: Seruatori offerenda sunt σωτήρια, summa cum gratitudine, & quidem publice priuatimque. Atqui Iehouah Deus noster Seruator est: & eius solius proprium est, seruare fideles suos ipsius opem implorantes. Quare ei σωτήρια offerenda sunt.
units.tr: Thanksgiving offerings [σωτήρια] are to be offered to the Saviour, with the greatest gratitude, and indeed both publicly and privately. But Jehovah our God is our Saviour, and it is his alone to save his faithful who implore his aid. Therefore thanksgiving offerings are to be offered to him.

units.la: SYLLO-
units.tr: SYLLO-

units.la: Seruatori debetur gratiarum actio & sacrificium εὐχαριστήριον[?]. Me, inquit Ionas, mirando modo seruauit, & e media morte Deus eripuit. Quare eidem gratias summas me habere æquum est.
units.tr: Thanksgiving and the sacrifice of thanksgiving [εὐχαριστήριον] are owed to the Saviour. "He," says Jonah, "saved me in a wonderful way, and God snatched me from the very midst of death. Therefore it is right that I should give him the greatest thanks."

units.la: THESIS I.
units.tr: THESIS I.

units.la: Per fidè & voto gratitudinis erga Ser-vatorem Deum nos obstringimus, & il-lud exsolvimus. juxta hæc dicta:
units.tr: By faith and by a vow of gratitude toward God our Saviour we bind ourselves, and we discharge that vow, according to these sayings:

units.la: Psal.50.14. Sacrifica Deo laudes, & red de excelso vota tua.
units.tr: Psalm 50:14. Offer to God praises, and pay your vows to the Most High.

units.la: Et versu 23. Qui sacrificat laude, is de-mum glorificat me: qui viam disponit, o-stendam ei salutem Dei.
units.tr: And verse 23: He who offers praise honours me indeed; and to him who orders his way I will show the salvation of God.

units.la: Philipp.4.6. De nulla re soliciti estote: sed omni in re precibus & supplicatione cum gratiarum actione petitiones vestrae innotescant apud Deum.
units.tr: Philippians 4:6. Be anxious about nothing; but in everything, by prayer and supplication with thanksgiving, let your requests be made known to God.

units.la: Hæc dicta monent, non tantum cordis affectu & linguæ sermone, sed etiam factis seu fidei obedietia, nobis testandam esse gratitudinem.
units.tr: These sayings admonish us that our gratitude must be attested not only by the disposition of the heart and the speech of the tongue, but also by deeds, that is, by obedience of faith.

units.la: Pie autem docuit Melanchthon, Gratitudinem complecti veritatem & iusti-ciam[?]. Veritas agnoscit & fatetur, libera-tionem tionem & alia beneficia à Deo profecta esse. Iustitia autem obligat non tantum ad amorem,sed etiam ad officia Deo grata.
units.tr: Melanchthon rightly taught that gratitude embraces truth and justice. Truth acknowledges and confesses that deliverance and other benefits have come from God. Justice, however, obliges us not only to love but also to duties pleasing to God.

units.la: THESIS II.
units.tr: THESIS II.

units.la: Per fidem nō solùm uoce celebramus Deum liberatorem,sed etiam sacra liturgia & operibus charitatis gratitudinem testamur.
units.tr: By faith we celebrate God the deliverer not only with the voice, but also attest our gratitude by the sacred liturgy and by works of charity.

units.la: Olim populus Israeliticus [illegible, ~9 letters] addebat sacrificia Eucharistica [illegible, ~5 letters] καὶ σωτηρίας[?], ut se liberatione à malis, & omnis generis priuatias & positiuas gratias, Deo soli tribuere testarentur. Exempla exstat Exod.15.&17. 1.Sam.11.&15. & alibi.
units.tr: Formerly the Israelite people added eucharistic sacrifices [...] and thank-offerings [καὶ σωτηρίας], so that by them they might testify that deliverance from evils, and every kind of privative and positive blessing, was to be ascribed to God alone. Examples are found in Exodus 15 and 17, 1 Samuel 11 and 15, and elsewhere.

units.la: Nos, abolitis illis sacrificijs, uitulos labiorum confitentium nomini Iehouae, offeramus Deo, Eucharistia religiosè utamur & fruamur, ac beneficentiae ac communicationis ne unquam obliuiscamur: cùm talibus uictimis delectetur Deus: Heb.13.16. Pauperes enim semper nobiscum habituri sumus: & quandocunque uoluerimus, poterimus eis benefacere: Marc.13.7. Cum his autē coniungamus ardens & constans studium obediendi Deo, etiam in difficili & aerumnosa uocatione, ad quam ille nos uocauit. Ita enim constabit nostra gratitudo primum invocatione Dei & gratiarum actione: deinde, beneficentia erga pauperes: postremo, obedientia fidei erga Deum.
units.tr: We, with those sacrifices abolished, offer to God the calves of our lips confessing the name of Jehovah (Hebrews 13:16). Let us use the Eucharist religiously and enjoy it, and never forget beneficence and fellowship, since God delights in such victims. "For the poor you will always have with you, and whenever you wish you will be able to do them good" (Mark 14:7). With these let us join an ardent and steadfast zeal for obeying God, even in a difficult and burdensome calling, to which he has called us. For thus our gratitude will consist first in the invocation of God and thanksgiving, then in beneficence toward the poor, and lastly in obedience of faith toward God.

units.la: THESIS III.
units.tr: THESIS III.

units.la: Iehouae est salus. Id est, Solus verus Deus est Saluator.
units.tr: Salvation belongs to Jehovah. That is, the only true God is the Saviour.

units.la: Demonstratio i. Idem est conditor & conseruator noster[?]. Sed Iehouah ipse est Deus: ipse fecit nos, & non ipsi nos: populus eius, & pecus pascuae eius: Psal.100.3. Quare idem conseruator noster est.
units.tr: Demonstration 1. He who is our creator is also our preserver. But Jehovah himself is God: he made us, and not we ourselves; we are his people and the sheep of his pasture (Psalm 100:3). Therefore he is also our preserver.

units.la: Maior ex eo colligi potest, quia cum non minus arduum sit restitutionis & redemtionis nostrae opus, quam creationis e nihilo, non potest nisi summe iusto, summe bono, omnipotenti & veraci Deo tribui.
units.tr: The major premise can be drawn from this: since the work of our restoration and redemption is no less arduous than the creation out of nothing, it can be ascribed only to the supremely just, supremely good, almighty and true God.

units.la: Demonstratio 2. Non nisi in conditorem conseruatoremque nostrum credendum nobis est. Credimus autem in Iehouam Patrem, Filium & Spiritum sanctum. Ergo Iehouah Seruator ille noster est.
units.tr: Demonstration 2. We must believe only in our creator and preserver. But we believe in Jehovah the Father, the Son and the Holy Spirit. Therefore Jehovah is that Saviour of ours.

units.la: Maior ex eo certa est, quod non fas est, fidei cultum, soli Deo debitum & conuenientem[?], ad creaturas transferre. Utinam hoc perpendant, qui Sanctos hac uita functos cōferuatores,opitulatores & patronos suos esse fingunt, quasi hi dimidiá cum Deo feruandi potestatem obtineat, eoq; nomine inuocandi sint.
units.tr: The major premise is certain because it is not lawful to transfer the worship owed and fitting to God alone to creatures. Would that those would weigh this who pretend that the saints who have departed this life are their preservers, helpers and patrons, as if these had half the power of saving with God, and were therefore to be invoked under that title.

units.la: VERSVS VLTIMVS.
units.tr: LAST VERSE.

units.la: Praecepit Iehouah pisci, & euomuit Ionam ad aridā. καὶ προσέταξεν τῷ κήτει, καὶ ἐξέβαλεν τὸν Ἰωνᾶν εἰς τὴν ξηρά[?].
units.tr: Jehovah commanded the fish, and it vomited Jonah onto the dry land. [καὶ προσέταξεν τῷ κήτει, καὶ ἐξέβαλεν τὸν Ἰωνᾶν εἰς τὴν ξηράν.]

units.la: Duo hoc loco perpendemus, Historiam & Mysterium.
units.tr: In this passage we weigh two things: the history and the mystery.

units.la: Historiae duo membra sunt: alterū de Iehouae mandato, alterum de eiusdé exe-cutione.
units.tr: The history has two parts: one concerning the command of Jehovah, the other concerning its execution.

units.la: Mandatum erat, ut piscis Ionam illæ-sum euomeret in aridam. Dicitur autem ἀνθρωποπαθῶς, quòd Iehouah mandauerit ceto: ut intelligamus nutu & potétia Dei factum, ut immanis illa bellua Ionam in-columem in littore exponeret: ne quis hæc in scyrpo nodum quærens, belluæ ra-tionis aliquam uim tribuat.
units.tr: The command was that the fish should vomit Jonah unharmed onto the dry land. It is said anthropopathōs [ἀνθρωποπαθῶς], that Jehovah commanded the whale, so that we may understand that it was done by the nod and power of God, that that monstrous beast set Jonah down unharmed on the shore. Let no one, seeking a knot in this straw, attribute some degree of reason to the beast.

units.la: Occurrunt autem in multis Scripturæ diuinæ locis exempla istius φρονήσεως & si-milium,quæ à creaturis rationalibus du-cuntur. Psal.78.23. Nam mandauerat nu-bibus cœli desuper,& ianuas cœli aperue-rat: rat:& pluerat super eos Man ad comedē dum,&c. Psal.50.1. Deus Deorum Iehovah loquutus est, & advocavit terrā, (συν-[illegible, ~8 letters]) incolas terrae homines sic vocat) ab ortu Solis usq; ad occasum eius. Isa.1.2. Audite cœli,&c auribus percipe terra,quoniam Dominus loquutus est. Mira est αὐξήσεις[?], quæ monet etiam ἄλογα elementa promtius audire Deum & ei obedire, quàm hypocritas, ψυχικὰς[?] homines, quorum videlicet aures non perforavit nec aperuit Deus. Sed illa loquendi formula maximè huc quadrat, quæ exstat Matth.8.26. Tunc experrectus Iesus, obiurgavit mare & ventos: & facta est tranquillitas magna.
units.tr: Examples of this phronēsis [φρονήσεως] and the like, which are drawn from rational creatures, occur in many places of divine Scripture. Psalm 78:23: "For he had commanded the clouds of heaven from above, and had opened the doors of heaven, and had rained down manna upon them to eat," etc. Psalm 50:1: "God, the God of gods, Jehovah, has spoken, and has summoned the earth" (so he calls the inhabitants of the earth men) "from the rising of the sun to its setting." Isaiah 1:2: "Hear, heavens, etc., give ear, earth, for the Lord has spoken." Wonderful is the auxēsis [αὐξήσεις], which warns that even irrational elements hear God more readily and obey him, than hypocrites, men of the soul [ψυχικοί], whose ears God has not pierced nor opened. But that form of speech suits this place most closely which is found in Matthew 8:26: "Then Jesus, awakened, rebuked the sea and the winds, and there was a great calm."

units.la: Hæ autem & similes loquendi formulæ monent, in manu & potestate Opificis Dei sic esse universas creaturas, ut promtisimè ei pareant vel nutu agenti.
units.tr: These and similar forms of speech teach that all creatures are so in the hand and power of the divine Maker that they most readily obey him, even at a mere nod.

units.la: Executio mandati divini erat, Ionæin littore expositio: quæ sanè admirandum Dei opus fuit. Meminerimus autem, & hanc historiā, & alteram illam de Danie-le inter medios leones sedete, nos monere de omnipotetia & bonitate Dei, cuius gloriæ si interfit, nullo negocio è mediis flammis,è faucibus leonum, à morsu viperarum & draconum, è media denique morte nos liberare potest.
units.tr: The execution of the divine command was the setting down of Jonah on the shore, which was indeed a wonderful work of God. Let us remember, moreover, that this story, and that other one about Daniel sitting among the lions, remind us of the almighty power and goodness of God, who, if it serves his glory, can without any trouble free us from the midst of flames, from the jaws of lions, from the bite of vipers and dragons, and finally from the midst of death.

units.la: Nota sunt pijs omnibus dicta plena cōsolationis. Psal.22.20. Eripe ex gladio animam meam, & è manu canis solitariā meam. 21. Serua me ab ore leonis: & à cornibus unicornium exaudi me. Psal.23.4. Etiamsi ambulavero in valle umbrae mortis, non timebo malum: quia tu mecum es, virga tua & pedum tuum me consolantur. Psal.91.13. Super leones & aspides ambulabis: conculcabis leuncu-los & dracones. Marc.16.17. Signa autem eos qui crediderint, hæc subsequentur: Per nomen meum dæmonia eijcient: & linguis loquentur novis. 18. Serpentes tollent: & si quid lethale biberint, nequaquam nocebit eis: ægrotis manus impo-nent, & bene habebunt. Paulus Apostolus, de Nerone & se loquens: καὶ ἐῤῥύσθη[?], ἐκ στόματος λέοντος, inquit. 2.Tim.4.17. Se-quente versu addit: Et eripiet me Dominus ab omni opere malo, seruabitq; re-gno suo cœlesti.
units.tr: Sayings full of consolation are well known to all the godly. Psalm 22:20: "Deliver my soul from the sword, and my solitary life from the hand of the dog." 21: "Save me from the mouth of the lion, and hear me from the horns of the unicorns." Psalm 23:4: "Even if I walk in the valley of the shadow of death, I will fear no evil, for you are with me; your rod and your staff comfort me." Psalm 91:13: "You will walk upon lions and asps; you will trample the young lions and the dragons." Mark 16:17: "And these signs will follow those who believe: in my name they will cast out demons, and they will speak with new tongues. 18: They will take up serpents; and if they drink anything deadly, it will by no means harm them; they will lay hands on the sick, and they will be well." The Apostle Paul, speaking of Nero and himself: "and I was rescued from the mouth of the lion" [καὶ ἐῤῥύσθην ἐκ στόματος λέοντος], he says (2 Timothy 4:17). In the following verse he adds: "And the Lord will deliver me from every evil work, and will preserve me for his heavenly kingdom."

units.la: Hæc omnia faciūt ad illustrandam & confirmandam primariam huius ultimi uersus historicam thesim, quam uerbis Apostoli efferre libet: Fidelis est Deus, qui non sinet uos tentari supra id quod potestis:sed praestabit unà cum tentatione etiam euasionem, ut possitis sufferre. 1. Cor.10.13.
units.tr: All these things serve to illustrate and confirm the principal historical thesis of this last verse, which I am pleased to state in the words of the Apostle: "God is faithful, who will not suffer you to be tempted beyond what you are able, but with the temptation will also make the way of escape, that you may be able to bear it" (1 Corinthians 10:13).

units.la: De huius loci Mysterio.
units.tr: On the Mystery of This Passage.

units.la: Si uelo reducto propheticum sensum spectes, occurret oraculum de Resurrectione Christi Iesu Domini nostri.
units.tr: If you set aside the veil and look at the prophetic sense, there meets you the oracle concerning the Resurrection of Christ Jesus our Lord.

units.la: Quemadmodum Ionas, cum trinoctium in uentre ceti peregisset, incolumis emersit, quòd cetus eum diutius retinere non posset: ita Christus, cum tres dies & tres noctes in corde terrae fuisset, Matt. 12.40. resurrexit, Matt.28. Deo eum excitante, solutis doloribus mortis, eo quòd impossibile erat ipsum ab ea retineri, Actor.2.24. mors enim ei dominari non potuit, Rom.6.9.
units.tr: Just as Jonah, after he had spent three nights in the belly of the whale, came forth safe, because the whale could not hold him any longer, so Christ, after he had been in the heart of the earth for three days and three nights (Matt. 12.40), rose again (Matt. 28), God raising him up, the pains of death having been loosed, since it was impossible for him to be held by it (Acts 2.24); for death could not have dominion over him (Rom. 6.9).

units.la: Fructus autem qui ex Christi resurrectione ad nos redit, geminus est.
units.tr: The fruit, moreover, which comes to us from Christ's resurrection is twofold.

units.la: 1. Resurrectio spiritualis in hac uita, de qua Paulus: Sicut, ait, excitatus est Christus ex mortuis in gloriam Patris, ita & nos noua uita ambulemus. Rom.6.4.
units.tr: 1. A spiritual resurrection in this life, of which Paul speaks: "As Christ was raised from the dead by the glory of the Father, so we also should walk in newness of life" (Rom. 6.4).

units.la: 2. Resurrectio carnis nostrae ad aeternam vitam. Christus, inquit idem Apostolus, excitatus est ex mortuis: & primitiæ eorum qui obdormierunt, factus est. 1.Corinth.15.20.
units.tr: 2. The resurrection of our flesh unto eternal life. "Christ," says the same Apostle, "has been raised from the dead, and has become the firstfruits of those who have fallen asleep" (1 Cor. 15.20).

units.la: Augustinus in Psalm.29.expos.2. Quia resurrexit caput vestrum, hoc sperate membra cætera, quod videtis in capite. Hoc sperate membra, quod credidistis in capite. Proverbium est antiquum & verū: Ubi caput, & cætera membra. Christus in cœlum ascendit, quò nos sequuturi sumus. Non remansit apud inferos: resurrexit, iam non moritur. Cum resurrexerimus & nos, iam non moriemur.
units.tr: Augustine on Psalm 29, exposition 2: "Because your Head has risen, hope for this, the other members, which you see in the Head. Hope for this, the members, which you have believed in the Head. It is an old and true proverb: where the head is, there the other members are. Christ ascended into heaven, whither we are to follow. He did not remain among the dead; he rose, and now he does not die. When we too have risen, we shall no longer die."

units.la: PROLEGOMENA in Caput tertium.
units.tr: PROLEGOMENA on Chapter 3.

units.la: I. GENUS CAUSSAE.
units.tr: I. THE KIND OF CASE.

units.la: AD demonstratiuum caussæ genus hoc totum caput referendum esse, vel ex eo colligi potest, quòd in eo non solùm Ionæ obedientia probata in legatione obeunda, & conversio Niniuitarum, sed etiam Dei erga eosdem immensa misericordia celebratur.
units.tr: That this whole chapter belongs to the demonstrative kind of case can be gathered from this: it celebrates not only Jonah's obedience in carrying out his commission and the conversion of the Ninevites, but also God's immense mercy toward the same people.

units.la: 2. PROPOSITIO ET USUS.
units.tr: 2. PROPOSITION AND USE.

units.la: Niniuitę, inquit Christus Dominus noster, resurget in iudicio cum natione hac, & condemnabūt eam: quòd ipsi resipuerint ad prędicationem Ionæ: & ecce plus quàm Ionas est in hoc loco. Matth.12.41. Luc.11.32. Usus in eo positus est, ut statuamus, nobis quoque voce servorum Dei, & publicis privatisq; calamitatibus, excitatis & admonitis, esse resipiscendū, & quidem ita, ut cordis secūdum Deum tristitiam, odio mali, studioq; boni, testatam faciamus.
units.tr: "The men of Nineveh," says our Lord Christ, "shall rise in judgment with this generation and condemn it, because they repented at the preaching of Jonah; and behold, a greater than Jonah is here." Matt. 12:41; Luke 11:32. The use of this passage lies in our learning that we too, when stirred and admonished by the voice of God's servants and by public and private calamities, must repent. And we must do so in such a way that we show by our conduct a godly sorrow of heart, hatred of evil, and zeal for good.

units.la: 3. PARTES CAPITIS.
units.tr: 3. PARTS OF THE CHAPTER.

units.la: Treis sunt capitis parteis. 1.De Ionæ legatione. 2. De Niniuitarum conversione. 3.De eventu, qui fuit illustris declaratio immensæ bonitatis & clementiæ Dei erga resipiscentes.
units.tr: The chapter has three parts: (1) Jonah's commission; (2) the conversion of the Ninevites; (3) the outcome, which was a remarkable display of God's immense goodness and mercy toward those who repent.

units.la: 4. HYPOTHESEON, QVAE IN decem huius capitis versibus occurrunt, reductio ad suas Thesis.
units.tr: 4. THE THESES CONTAINED IN THE TEN VERSES OF THIS CHAPTER, REDUCED TO THEIR PROPOSITIONS.

units.la: 1. Id quod hominum causa, ut eis consulat, Deo semel placuit, ἀμεταμέλητον haberi debet: eoq; nō est mirum, si idem bis praecipiat.
units.tr: 1. What God has once decided for the sake of men, to provide for their good, must be regarded as [ἀμεταμέλητον] irrevocable; and so it is no wonder if he commands the same thing twice.

units.la: 2. Dei solius est, locum, tempus, doctri-nam, nam,docendi & agendi rationem,feruis suis praescribere & praestituere.
units.tr: 2. It belongs to God alone to prescribe and appoint for his servants the place, the time, the doctrine, and the manner of teaching and acting.

units.la: 3. Seruorum autem eius est,Domini mandato obedire,quomodocunque tandem rei arduae, quam aggrediuntur, circumstantiae oculos carnis perstringant.
units.tr: 3. It is the duty of his servants to obey the Lord's command, however the circumstances of the difficult task they undertake may dazzle their carnal eyes.

units.la: 4. Nec labori, nec tempori ijsdem par-cendum'est, cùm denunciata seu in genere,seu in specie Dei ira & horribilibus poenis,ad resipiscentiam summo studio uocandi sunt homines.
units.tr: 4. Neither toil nor time must be spared when men are to be called to repentance with the greatest zeal, whether God's wrath and dreadful punishments have been announced in general or in particular.

units.la: 5. Ex fidei fonte conversio vera procreat, cuius mortificatio jeiunio,summissi-one sub potenti manu Dei, & alijs documentis constat.
units.tr: 5. True conversion springs from the fountain of faith. Its mortification is shown by fasting, by humbling oneself under the mighty hand of God, and by other tokens.

units.la: 6. Exemplo poenitentiae summos homines mediocribus & infimis praeluce-re,aequum & salutare est.
units.tr: 6. It is fair and salutary that eminent men shine as an example of repentance to people of middle and lower rank.

units.la: 7. Decreta magistratuum exercitijs poenitentiae seruire debent.
units.tr: 7. The decrees of magistrates ought to serve the exercises of repentance.

units.la: 8. Conuersio ad Deum, ardentissimis precibus,odio iniusticiae & impietatis,& alijs προσκαμμάτοις[?] seu adiunctis constat.
units.tr: 8. Conversion to God is shown by most fervent prayers, by hatred of injustice and impiety, and by other [προσκαμμάτα?] attendant circumstances.

units.la: 9. Spes veniae & salutis à conuersione non potest nec debet separari.
units.tr: 9. The hope of pardon and salvation cannot and must not be separated from conversion.

units.la: 10. Nam Deus pro immensa sua cleme-tia,non modò resipiscentibus seriò ignoscit,sed etiam pœnas,cum exceptione de resipiscentia denunciatas,ad se conversis relaxat & condonat. Ipsi gloria in æter-num. Amen.
units.tr: 10. For God, in his immense mercy, not only sincerely pardons those who repent, but also remits and forgives, for those who turn to him, the punishments that were announced with the condition of repentance. To him be glory forever. Amen.

units.la: VERSUS I.
units.tr: VERSE 1.

units.la: Et fuit verbum Jehova ad Jonam secundo, dicendo, &c.
units.tr: And the word of Jehovah came to Jonah a second time, saying, etc.

units.la: Quod iam antea semel Jonæ prophe-tæ Deus imperauerat, ut videlicet Nine-vitis resipiscentiam prædicaret, id secun-do eidem injuxit. Oportebat enim id fie-ri, quod manus & consilium Dei definie-rat.Act.4.28. Et declaranda erat Dei cle-mentia, non remoto a munere propheti-co Jona, qui inobedientia sua eo se indi-gnum reddiderat.
units.tr: God had earlier commanded the prophet Jonah once, namely to preach repentance to the Ninevites; now he enjoins it on him a second time. For what the hand and counsel of God had determined had to come to pass (Acts 4:28), and God's mercy had to be made known, since Jonah, who had made himself unworthy of his prophetic office by his disobedience, had not been removed from that office.

units.la: THESIS.
units.tr: THESIS.

units.la: Id quod hominum causa, ut videlicet saluti eorum consulat, Deo semel placu-it,ἀμεταμέλητον[?] haberi debet: eoq; mirum videri non debet, si bis idem praecipiat. Consilium Jehovae in æternū perstat: cogitationes cordis eius in seculum,&c.
units.tr: What God has once decided for the sake of men, that is, to provide for their salvation, must be regarded as [ἀμεταμέλητον] irrevocable; and so it should not seem strange if he commands the same thing twice. "The counsel of Jehovah stands forever; the thoughts of his heart endure to all generations," etc.

units.la: Alia est Dei summè sapientis & omniscij & omnipotentis, alia hominum, qui utinfirmi, ita propter ignorantiam mul-tis erroribus obnoxii sunt, ratio. Non est homo Deus, ut mentiatur: & filius hominis, ut poeniteat eum. ipse dixit, & non fa-ciet? locutus est, & non praestabit illud? Num.23.19. Item: Et etiam Fortitudo (id est, fortis seu omnipotens Deus) Israelis nō mentietur, nec poenitudine ducetur: non enim homo est, ut poeniteat illum. 1.Sam.15.29. Itaq; consilium eius stabit, & omnem voluntatem suam faciet. Isa.46.10. Sed hominis quidem sunt praeparationes cordis: a Iehouah tamen est respōsio linguae. Pro.16.1. Multa quidem nobis in mentem veniunt, sed ne quidem oratio qua respondemus, in nostra potestate est, nedum facta & consiliorum executiones & euentus. In manu Dei, cuncta pro suo arbitrio moderantis, rerum omnium momenta posita sunt. Nobis sane posteriores curae, meliores esse: & caussam mutandi propositum non sa-lutare nobis, subministrare possunt: Dei autem dona & vocatio eiusmodi sunt, ut illorum Deum nunquam poeni-teat.Rom.11.29.
units.tr: The reasoning of God, who is supremely wise, all-knowing, and almighty, is one thing; the reasoning of men, who are weak and, because of their ignorance, liable to many errors, is another. "God is not a man, that he should lie; nor the son of man, that he should repent. Has he said, and will he not do it? Or has he spoken, and will he not fulfil it?" Num. 23:19. Likewise: "The Strength of Israel (that is, the strong or almighty God) will not lie nor repent; for he is not a man, that he should repent." 1 Sam. 15:29. Therefore his counsel will stand, and he will do all his pleasure. Isa. 46:10. "The preparations of the heart belong to man, but the answer of the tongue is from Jehovah." Prov. 16:1. Many things indeed come into our minds, but not even the answer we give lies in our power, much less the execution of our deeds and plans and their outcomes. All things are in the hand of God, who governs everything at his own pleasure, and the turning points of all affairs are placed there. For us, later concerns may indeed seem better, and they may supply a reason for changing a purpose that is not beneficial to us; but the gifts and calling of God are of such a kind that he never repents of them. Rom. 11:29.

units.la: QVI TANDEM FRVCTVS EX huius doctrinae meditatione ad pios redeunt?
units.tr: WHAT FRUIT, FINALLY, DO THE PIOUS DRAW FROM MEDITATING ON THIS DOCTRINE?

units.la: 1. Primus hic est, ut de voluntate Dei plene persuasi, promte & constanter mandatis eius obsequantur, quae nihil omnino temere & obiter praecipere intelligunt.
units.tr: 1. The first is this: fully persuaded of God's will, they obey his commands promptly and steadfastly, understanding that he never commands anything rashly or casually.

units.la: 2. Secundus est, ut decretum eiusdem Dei Patris de nostra salute ἀμεταμέλητον[?] καὶ μὴ παλινάγρετον esse statuamus, contra eos qui ex vasis misericordiae vasa irae aeternae fieri posse fingentes, quantum quidè in ipsis est, salutis nostrae fundamenta subuertunt. 1. Sicut enim se habuerunt causae nostrae salutis & redemtionis, ita etiā effectus. Sed oportuit pati Christum, & intrare in gloriam suam: Luc.24.26. Oportet igitur & eos salvos fieri, quorum causa Christus mortuus est. 2. Iam vero, cum nihil sit quod nos separare possit à charitate Christi, Roman.8.35. ac nemo Christi oves è manibus eius eripere possit, Ioan.10.28. quis non inde colligat, ἐφ' ᾧ βελῶν[?] salutem nostram positam esse? Neque enim absolute nostri iuris sumus, sed eius membra qui nos redemit, & suos συμφύτες[?] esse voluit.
units.tr: 2. The second is this: we should hold that the decree of the same God the Father concerning our salvation is [ἀμεταμέλητον] irrevocable and [καὶ μὴ παλινάγρετον] not to be recalled. This answers those who imagine that vessels of mercy can become vessels of eternal wrath, and who, so far as they are able, undermine the foundations of our salvation. (1) As were the causes of our salvation and redemption, so are the effects. But Christ had to suffer and enter into his glory (Luke 24:26); therefore those also must be saved for whose sake Christ died. (2) Now, since nothing can separate us from the love of Christ (Rom. 8:35), and no one can snatch Christ's sheep out of his hands (John 10:28), who would not conclude from this that our salvation rests [ἐφ' ᾧ βελῶν?] securely upon this foundation? For we are not absolutely our own, but members of him who redeemed us and willed that we be [σύμφυτοι] grafted together with him.

units.la: VERSVS II.
units.tr: VERSE II.

units.la: Surge,& uade in Niniueh ciuitatem il-
units.tr: Arise, and go to Nineveh, that great city,

units.la: lam magnam,& prædica in ea prædicationem quam loquor ad te.
units.tr: and preach in it the preaching that I speak to you.

units.la: Hic uersus præceptum Domini Dei, de Niniuitis ad resipiscentiam exhortan-dis,compleCtitur. Vt autem alibi in gene-re,de obseruatione legis suæ Deus loquens,ait: Quicquid ego præcipio uobis, custodietis ut facietis: nō addes ad illud, nec diminues ex eo: Deut:12.32. ita hæc in specie de concione pœnitentiæ præci-piens: Prædica, inquit, in ea prædicatio-nem quam loquor ad te. Vult enim De-us præscriptum suum religiosè obseruari à seruis, legatione ipsius nomine de-fungentibus.
units.tr: This verse contains the Lord God's command to exhort the Ninevites to repentance. Just as God speaks elsewhere in general about the keeping of his law, saying: "Whatever I command you, you shall take care to do; you shall not add to it, nor diminish from it" (Deut. 12.32), so here, instructing specifically about the preaching of repentance, he says: "Preach in it the preaching that I speak to you." For God wills that his prescript be observed faithfully by the servants who discharge their embassy in his name.

units.la: THESIS.
units.tr: THESIS.

units.la: Dei solius est, locum, tempus, doctrinæ genus, docendi & agendi modum & rationem seruis suis præscribere.
units.tr: It belongs to God alone to prescribe to his servants the place, the time, the kind of teaching, and the manner and method of teaching and acting.

units.la: Vt enim Principis est, Legato manda- ta certa & definita suis quibusdam circum-stantijs, præscribere: nec licet Legato ὑπὲρ τὰ ἰονα μικὰ πνλ[?] ac plura quàm in mandatis accepit, tum dictis tum factis exequi: ne[illegible, ~6 letters] παραβασίας[?] subire co gatur: ita Dei seruis ex Domini praescripto docendum, agedum & uiuendū est, & eadem incedendum regula. Phil.3.16.
units.tr: For just as it is the prerogative of a prince to prescribe to an envoy the commission, certain and defined with particular circumstances, so the envoy may not carry out, in word or deed, more or other things than he has received in his instructions, lest he be forced to undergo a transgression. In the same way, the servants of God must teach, act and live according to the Lord's prescript, and must walk by the same rule (Phil. 3.16).

units.la: Exemplum huius rei pulcerrimum habetur Matt.10. in prima Apostolorum ad oues perditas domus Israelis legatione: & Matt.28.19.20. in legatione ad omnes Gentes. Non enim λόγια[?] mandata Apostolis suis Christus dedit: sed, Profecti, ait, docete omnes gentes, baptizantes eos in nomine Patris, Filij & Spiritus sancti: docentes eos seruare omnia quae mandaui uobis.
units.tr: The most beautiful example of this matter is found in Matthew 10, in the first embassy of the Apostles to the lost sheep of the house of Israel, and in Matthew 28.19-20, in the embassy to all nations. For Christ did not give his Apostles mere opinions, but said: "Go, teach all nations, baptizing them in the name of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Spirit, teaching them to observe all things that I have commanded you."

units.la: 1. Domini uniuersorū, & inexhausti uerae sapientiae fontis est, seruis suis & doctrinam salutarem, & eius tradendae uiam aperire & praescribere. Sed Deus noster uniuersorum Dominus est, & ipsa sapientia. Eius itaq; fuerit, doctrinam salutarem patefacere, & eius docendae μισθοδοσίαν[?] indicare.
units.tr: 1. It belongs to the Lord of all things, and to the inexhaustible fountain of true wisdom, to open and prescribe to his servants both the saving doctrine and the way of delivering it. But our God is the Lord of all things and wisdom itself. It is therefore his to disclose the saving doctrine and to indicate the rule by which it is to be taught.

units.la: 2. In cuius etiam auctoritate posite; sunt opportunitates, eius est dicedi & agendi circūstantias praescribere. Sed Pater ille aeternus solus nouit tempora siue opportunitates, easq; in sua ipsius auctoritate posuit:Act.1.7. Itaq; eius solius est, agendi dicendiq; rationem commonstrare.
units.tr: 2. Opportunities also lie within his authority, and so it is his to prescribe the circumstances of speaking and acting. But that eternal Father alone knows the times or opportunities, and he has placed them in his own authority (Acts 1.7). Therefore it is his alone to show the manner of acting and speaking.

units.la: 1. Si vocationem spectes, ea vero instar cynosurae est. Hebr.5.4. Neque sibi ipsi quisquam sumit hunc honorem: sed qui vocatur à Deo, sicut Aaron.
units.tr: 1. If you look at the calling, this is indeed like a guiding star: "Nor does anyone take this honour upon himself, but he who is called by God, as Aaron was" (Heb. 5.4).

units.la: 2. Si vero doctrinam, notum est illud Pauli tonitru: Sed etiamsi nos, aut angelus è coelo evangelizet vobis, praeter id quod vobis evangelizauimus, anathema esto. Ut ante diximus, etiam nunc iterū dico: Si quis vobis evangelizauerit, praeter id quod accepistis, anathema sit. Gal-lat.1.8.9.
units.tr: 2. If you look at the doctrine, the thunderclap of Paul is well known: "But even if we, or an angel from heaven, preach to you a gospel other than what we have preached to you, let him be accursed. As we said before, so now I say again: if anyone preaches to you a gospel other than what you have received, let him be accursed" (Gal. 1.8-9).

units.la: 3. Si denique consideres Sacramenta, quod in specie de Coena Domini dixit Paulus: Ego accepi à Domino, quod & tradidi vobis: 1.Cor.11.23. id in genere de Sacramentis quoq; recte dicemus. Cum enim Domini Dei nostri solius sit Sacramenta instituere, quis dubitet eius solius esse earum λατρείαν[?] praescribere?
units.tr: 3. Finally, if you consider the sacraments, what Paul said specifically about the Lord's Supper, "I received from the Lord what I also delivered to you" (1 Cor. 11.23), we may rightly say in general also of the sacraments. Since it belongs to the Lord our God alone to institute the sacraments, who would doubt that it is his alone to prescribe the worship [λατρεία] of them?

units.la: Atq; idem est de omnibus aliis, quae in Ecclesia Dei decenter & ordine fieri de-bent, bent,iudicium. Quare non dubium est, ex praescripto Dei omnia nobis esse agenda. Vnde liquet,no solum infelicem,sed etiam plufquam sacrilegam esse audaciam eorum,qui exemplo tyrannorum leges pretio figentium & refigentium, doctrinę genus & ceremoniarum diuinitus fancitam ἀντάξιαν uiolant:& ἑτεροδιδασκαλίαν ac ceremonias partim inutiles, partim superstitiosas, partim impias in Ecclesiam inuehere non uerentur.
units.tr: And the same holds for all the other things that ought to be done in the Church of God decently and in order. Therefore there is no doubt that all things must be done by us according to God's prescript. From this it is clear that the audacity of those is not only unhappy but even more than sacrilegious, who, after the example of tyrants who fix and refix laws for a price, violate the kind of teaching and the divinely sanctioned ceremonies, and who do not hesitate to introduce into the Church a different teaching [ἑτεροδιδασκαλίαν] and ceremonies that are partly useless, partly superstitious, and partly impious.

units.la: SED CVR POENITENTIAM Dominus Deus noster Niuiuitus & nobis omnibus praedicari uoluit?
units.tr: BUT WHY DID OUR LORD GOD WISH REPENTANCE TO BE PREACHED TO THE NINEVITES AND TO ALL OF US?

units.la: Quia ut gloriae Dei agnitio nos ad nostrae ignominię, quę peccati poena est,sensum reuocat:sic nostri agnitio ad Dei misericordiam, qua nobis omnibus opus est,implorandam adducit. Concio uerò de poenitentia iubet nos in nofmetipfos descendere: peccatum, cuius nobis omnes conscij fumus,confiteri:Deo gloriam dare,&c.
units.tr: Because, just as the knowledge of God's glory calls us back to a sense of our own shame, which is the punishment of sin, so the knowledge of ourselves leads us to implore the mercy of God, which all of us need. The sermon on repentance, moreover, bids us descend into ourselves, to confess the sin of which we are all conscious, to give glory to God, and so on.

units.la: Quemadmodum autē Deus prius nos mortificat, quàm uiuificet: ita eius feruis initiò poenitentia prędicanda est, deinde uerò Euangeliū, quod annunciat remissionem fionem peccatorum. Huius ordinis exempla occurrunt in concionibus Prophetarum,Ioannis Baptistae & Apostolorum, quorū uestigijs nos insistere par est.
units.tr: Just as God mortifies us before he makes us alive, so his servants must first preach repentance, and then the gospel, which announces the remission of sins. Examples of this order occur in the sermons of the Prophets, of John the Baptist and of the Apostles, whose footsteps we ought to follow.

units.la: VERSUS III.
units.tr: VERSE III.

units.la: Surrexit itaque Ionah, & abijt in Nini-ue iuxta verbum Iehova. Porrò Niniueh erat ciuitas magna Dei, itinere triū dierū.
units.tr: So Jonah arose and went to Nineveh, according to the word of the LORD. Now Nineveh was an exceedingly great city of God, a three days' journey across.

units.la: Ionas,ita ut in mandatis à Deo acceperat,Niniuen ꝑfectus est, urbe amplisimā & populosissimā,tridui itinere patetem.
units.tr: Jonah, just as he had received in his commission from God, went to Nineveh, a very large and very populous city, a city that took three days to cross.

units.la: Duo hoc loco ἐν τῇ ὑποθέσει notāda sunt, quorum tamen utrumq; ἐγκωμιαστικόν est.
units.tr: Two things in this passage [ἐν τῇ ὑποθέσει] are to be noted, both of which, however, are [ἐγκωμιαστικόν] worthy of praise.

units.la: Alterum est de obedientia, quam Ionas suscepta ad Niniuitas legatione praestitit: alterum uero est descriptio ciuitatis Niniueh. Nos ubi de utroque egerimus, ad Thesin accedemus.
units.tr: The one concerns the obedience that Jonah showed in undertaking the embassy to the Ninevites; the other is the description of the city of Nineveh. When we have treated each of these, we shall come to the Thesis.

units.la: DE OBEDIENTIA IONAE, in munere sibi delegato capessen-do declarata.
units.tr: THE OBEDIENCE OF JONAH, shown in his undertaking of the task entrusted to him.

units.la: Eximia laude dignam fuisse hanc obedientiam, causae quas subiungam, perspicuè ostendunt.
units.tr: That this obedience deserves exceptional praise, the reasons I shall add make clear.

units.la: 1. Quia per fidem, Dei mandato moré gerens, iter ingressus est Ionas.
units.tr: 1. Because Jonah set out on the journey by faith, obeying God's command.

units.la: 2. Quia uicit tentatione,natam ex perfuasione populi Ifraelitici, de religione uera inter gentes non annuncianda,cùm ea propria esset eius populi, quem Deus sanctificauerat sibi in peculium.
units.tr: 2. Because he overcame a temptation that arose from the conviction of the Israelite people that the true religion was not to be proclaimed among the nations, since it belonged to that people whom God had sanctified as his own possession.

units.la: 3. Quia Dei uoluntate suo honori praetulit. Sciebat Deum pro sua clementia Niniuitis,si resipuissent,parsurum esse: eoq; uereri poterat,ne uanus uates,excidium denunciando,uideretur.
units.tr: 3. Because he preferred God's will to his own honour. He knew that God, in his mercy, would spare the Ninevites if they repented, and so he could fear that he would appear to be a false prophet in announcing destruction.

units.la: 4. Quia inobedietiae turpe maculam, honestissimo obedientiæ documento contexit: suo exemplo monens,in malo proposito non esse nobis perstandum, & cauendum ne bis ad eundem lapidem impingamus: sed errata καὶ παραπτώματα compensanda nobis esse fructibus Spiritus, & donorum Dei τοῖς κατορθώμασιν.
units.tr: 4. Because he covered the shameful stain of disobedience with the most honourable proof of obedience. By his example he warns us not to persist in an evil purpose, and to take care that we do not stumble twice over the same stone, but that our errors and transgressions [καὶ παραπτώματα] be made good by the fruits of the Spirit and by the gifts of God [τοῖς κατορθώμασιν].

units.la: 5. Quia fuit insignis typus legationis Apostolorum ad omnes gentes: quem si Pseudoiudæi ætate Apostolorum recte perpendissent, nequaquam illis præconium Euangelij inter Gentes uitio dedissent.
units.tr: 5. Because his mission was a remarkable type of the mission of the Apostles to all nations. Had the false Jews of the Apostles' time weighed this rightly, they would never have held the proclamation of the Gospel among the Gentiles against them.

units.la: 6. Quia etsi gentis suæ amantissimus Propheta sciret, Israelitis ἀμεταμελήτοις opprobrio & præiudicio fore, si resipiscerét Niniuitæ:ac hos surrecturos[?] in iudicio,& iudicatuiudicaturos Israelem contumacem: tamen Deo parendum esse, statuit.
units.tr: 6. Because, although the prophet, being most loving toward his own people, knew that repentance by the Ninevites would bring shame and condemnation upon the Israelites, who are unrepentant [ἀμεταμελήτοις], and that these Ninevites would rise up in judgement and would condemn stubborn Israel, he nevertheless resolved that God must be obeyed.

units.la: DESCRIPTIO CIVI-tatis Ninivch.
units.tr: DESCRIPTION OF THE CITY OF NINEVEH.

units.la: Quanta fuerit amplitudo ciuitatis Ni-niueh, docet αὐξήσεως[?] Hebraeis familiaris, qua diuina quaedam eius magnitudo celebratur. Erat, inquit Propheta noster, Ni-niueh ciuitas magna Elohim, Deo. Ita in Psal. 104.16. Saturantur arbores Iehouae: cedri Libani quas plantauit. Additur per ἐπιξηγήσεως[?] itinere trium dierum: id quod nonnulli de uicinis pagis, ius comune ciuitatis obtinentibus, alij de ambitu urbis, alij deniq; de urbis regionibus praecipuis interpretantur.
units.tr: The great size of the city of Nineveh is shown by an amplification [αὐξήσεως], a figure familiar to the Hebrews, by which a certain divine greatness of the city is celebrated. Our prophet says, "Nineveh was a great city of God [Elohim]." So in Psalm 104:16: "The trees of the LORD are satisfied, the cedars of Lebanon which he planted." There is added, by way of explanation [ἐπιξηγήσεως], "a journey of three days." Some interpret this as the neighbouring villages that share the common rights of the city, others as the circuit of the city walls, and others finally as the principal districts of the city.

units.la: Fuerunt sane quarundam urbium ambitus prodigiosae propemodum magnitudinis: ut exempla[?], quae subijcia[?], monent.
units.tr: Indeed, the circuits of some cities were of almost prodigious size, as the examples I shall add show.

units.la: Carthaginis, cū eā deleret Scipio Iunior, ambitus fuit sex miliariū Germanicorum: diameter circiter duorū miliarium.
units.tr: When Scipio the Younger destroyed Carthage, its circuit was six German miles, and its diameter about two miles.

units.la: Constantinopoleos, cum eam Turcae, Anno Christi 1453, expugnarent, ambitus erat cētum & undecim stadiorum, id est, miliariū Germanicorū trium & dimidij.
units.tr: When the Turks took Constantinople in the year of Christ 1453, its circuit was one hundred and eleven stadia, that is, three and a half German miles.

units.la: Celebratur magnitudo Ecbatanę, quę fuit Medorum μητρόπολις: Iudithæ 1.capite: & Tigranocertæ, à Plutarcho in vita Luculli.
units.tr: The greatness of Ecbatana, which was the metropolis of the Medes, is celebrated in Judith, chapter 1, and that of Tigranocerta by Plutarch in the Life of Lucullus.

units.la: Plinius lib.6. Naturalis Historiæ, cap. 26. Babylon, inquit, Chaldaicarum gentium caput, diu summam claritatem obtinuit in toto orbe, propter quam reliqua pars Mesopotamiæ Assyriæque Babylonia appellata est, sexaginta milia passu-um amplexa muris, ducenos pedes altis, quinquagenos latis, in singulos pedes ternis digitis mensura ampliore quam nostra, interfluo Euphrate, mirabili ope-re utroq;. Durat adhuc ibi Iouis Beli templum. Inuentor hic fuit fideralis scientiæ.
units.tr: Pliny, Natural History, book 6, chapter 26: "Babylon," he says, "the head of the Chaldean peoples, for a long time held the highest renown in the whole world. Because of it the rest of Mesopotamia and Assyria was called Babylonia. It was enclosed by walls sixty thousand paces long, two hundred feet high and fifty feet wide, the measure of a foot there being longer than ours by three fingers. The Euphrates flows through it, and both banks are of wonderful workmanship. The temple of Jupiter Belus still stands there. Here was the inventor of astral science."

units.la: Vadianus in Epitome sua de tribus partibus terræ, in Chaldęae descriptione, hęc memoriæ prodidit: Porrò veteres trium clarissimarum urbium hoc tractu meminerunt, videlicet Babylonis infra Euphratis in Tigrin perducti[?] fossam sitæ, & Seleuciæ, quæ interamnis fuit, & Nini, quæ in ora Assyriæ Tigridis ripæ imposita fuit Plinio, ita tamé, ut Seleucia inter hanc & illam medio propemodum situ fuerit.
units.tr: Vadianus, in his Epitome on the three parts of the earth, in his description of Chaldea, has handed down this memory: "Furthermore, the ancients mention three very famous cities in this region, namely Babylon, situated below the Euphrates where it is drawn into the ditch of the Tigris; Seleucia, which lay between the rivers; and Ninus, which, according to Pliny, was placed on the bank of the Tigris at the edge of Assyria. Yet Seleucia lay almost midway between the one and the other."

units.la: Memoratur & Ctesiphon recentior quidem, sed par & magnitudine & munitio [?]ibus Seleuciæ. Ninus sanè uetustisima Regum Assyriorum regia fuit, quam Scriptura Niniuen nominat, Ionæ Prophetæ claram uaticinio, unde Niniuitæ dicti, dé quibus Matt.11. Condiderat eam primus Assur, à quo Assuria, uel quod idem est, Assyria circumiacèns regio uocata est. De-inde Beli filius Ninus, maritus Semiramidis, ampliauit, clarissimis ædificijs auctâ. Munsterus ait, Niniuen habuisse in area sua 400. stadia, quę faciunt ferè 12. milia-ria Germanica.
units.tr: Ctesiphon is also mentioned, a more recent city, but equal to Seleucia in size and fortification. Ninus, however, was the most ancient royal seat of the Assyrian kings, which Scripture calls Nineveh, made famous by the prophecy of Jonah, whence its people are called Ninevites, as in Matthew 11. Assur, from whom Assyria, or what is the same, the surrounding region of Assyria, was named, had first founded it. Afterwards Ninus, son of Belus and husband of Semiramis, enlarged it, adorning it with most splendid buildings. Münster says that Nineveh had within its area 400 stadia, which make nearly 12 German miles.

units.la: Enimuerò cum ferè magnatum urbiū magnæ sint corruptelæ, iuxta proverbiū, [?]ἀρχὴ μεγάλη, [?]ἡ μεγάλη πόλις, uiolationem multiplicem iuris, æqui, amicitiæ, comitantur multæ pœnæ & calamitates, quæ efficiunt, ut sit quemadmodum distum Amphidis monet, [?]ἀγὴν δὲ θέατρον ἀντύχας σὺ φῶς γέμον. Atq; eo sanè nomine modis omnibus laboriosum & ærumnosum est ministerium Ecclesiasticū in eiusmodi ciuitatibus, ijs Dei servis qui Deo, non hominibus placere studet: ut Gregorij Nazianzeni curatoris, & Ioannis Chrysostomi episcopi Ecclesiæ Constantinopolitanæ, item Athanasij & aliorum exempla ostedunt.
units.tr: Indeed, since great cities are almost always great corruptions, according to the proverb, "a great city is a great evil" [ἀρχὴ μεγάλη, ἡ μεγάλη πόλις], they are accompanied by manifold violations of law, justice and friendship, and by many punishments and calamities. These make it as Amphis warns: "the contest is a theatre full of misfortunes and light" [ἀγὼν δὲ θέατρον ἀντύχας σὺ φῶς γέμον]. For this reason the ecclesiastical ministry in such cities is in every way laborious and burdensome for those servants of God who seek to please God, not men; as the examples of Gregory Nazianzen, the guardian, of John Chrysostom, bishop of the Church of Constantinople, likewise of Athanasius and others show.

units.la: Seruorum autem Dei opt.maximi est, Domini mandato obedite, quomodocū-que tandem rei arduæ quam aggrediū-tur, circumstantiæ oculos & intelligentiam carnis perstringant.
units.tr: It is, however, the duty of the servants of God most high to obey the Lord's command, however difficult the task they undertake, even if its surrounding circumstances dazzle the eyes and the understanding of the flesh.

units.la: Sic argumentatur τὸ τῆς σαρκὸς φρόνημα cum hominem ad difficile aliquam functionem uocari audit: Homini cordato nūquam excidere debet illud uetus pro-uerbium: ἀρχὴν δὲ ἔργων ἡ προθυμία ἀμήχανα[?] Quæ efficere nequeas, nec uel ordiri decet. Tu uero τ᾽ ἀμήχανα aggrederis, norn memor tuę infirmitatis, & magnitudinis eius rei quam suscipis. Cur igitur ἀδύνατα τὰ ὑπὲρ ἡμᾶς.
units.tr: So argues the mind of the flesh [τὸ τῆς σαρκὸς φρόνημα] when it hears that a man is called to some difficult function. The old proverb should never slip from the mind of a sensible man: the beginning of impossible deeds is eagerness [ἀρχὴν δὲ ἔργων ἡ προθυμία ἀμήχανα]. What you cannot accomplish, you should not even begin. But you undertake the impossible things [τ᾽ ἀμήχανα], not mindful of your weakness and of the greatness of the thing you take up. Why then, things beyond us are impossible [ἀδύνατα τὰ ὑπὲρ ἡμᾶς]?

units.la: Respondet intelligentia Spiritus: Ne-mo cordatus est, nisi qui est uere fidelis. Atqui hic nequaquam Stoicorum more in fecundas caussas respicit, & earum me-sura uiribusq; Dei potentiam metitur & æstimat: sed statuit, Deum uocare ea quę non sunt, tanquam sint: Rom.4.17. Deum idoneos facere Testameti fui ministros: 2.Cor.3.6. &, ut plurima uno dicto συλ-λήβδην[?] complectar, Dei potentiam perinfirmitatem nostram perfici: 2.Cor.12.9. Fatendum autē est,etiam eximios Dei seruos non raro ad tempus vehementer fidei & vocationis impedimentis cōtur-bari & præpediri.Verùm ubi fide corda à terra ad cœlum,& à creaturis ad omnipo tentem Creatorem sustulerunt, freti Dei potentia & præsentia,bene sperare inci-piunt.
units.tr: The understanding of the Spirit replies: no one is sensible unless he is truly faithful. And yet this reasoning does not, in the manner of the Stoics, look to secondary causes and measure God's power and estimate it by their strength. Rather it holds that God calls those things which are not as though they were (Rom. 4:17), that God makes us fit ministers of his covenant (2 Cor. 3:6), and, to sum up many things in one saying, that God's power is made perfect in our weakness (2 Cor. 12:9). It must be admitted that even eminent servants of God are not seldom for a time greatly disturbed and hindered by the obstacles of faith and of their calling. But when they have lifted their hearts by faith from earth to heaven, and from creatures to the almighty Creator, relying on God's power and presence, they begin to hope well.

units.la: Moses vocatus ad gubernationem po-puli Israelitici, qui iam educędus erat ex Ægypto,cum Israelitas sibi fidem non ef-se habituros,& se non esse disertum,cau-satus esset,tandem dicebat:Obsecro Domine,mitte quæso per manum illius quē missurus es:Exod.4.13. Sed cum à Domino obiurgato prodigijs fides facta esset, vocantem Deum secutus, fidelis fuit in tota domo illius,ut famulus,ad testificanda quæ post dicenda erant.Hebr.3.5.
units.tr: Moses, called to govern the Israelite people, who were now to be led out of Egypt, when he pleaded that the Israelites would not have faith in him and that he was not eloquent, at last said: "Pardon, Lord, I beg you, send, I pray, by the hand of him whom you will send" (Exod. 4:13). But when the Lord rebuked him and faith was established by signs, he followed the God who called him, and was faithful in all his house, as a servant, to bear witness to those things that were to be spoken afterwards (Heb. 3:5).

units.la: Est & Abrahæ maximè commemora-bile exemplum, quod Apostolus Paulus his verbis celebravit: Abraham contra spem sub spe credidit, ut fieret pater mul-tarum gentium,secundum id quod ei di-ctum fuerat: Ita erit semen tuum. Ac mi-nimè imbecillis fide,non considerauit su-um ipsius corpus iam emortuum,cū cen-tum tum circiter natus esset annos, nec emortuam vuluam Sarae. Adversus autē promissiones Dei non disceptauit infidelitate[?] sed robustus factus est fide, tributa gloria Deo:ac plenè persuasum habens, eum quod promiserat, posse etiam facere. Ro-man.4.18.19.20.21.
units.tr: There is also the example of Abraham, most worthy of remembrance, which the Apostle Paul celebrated in these words: "Abraham against hope believed in hope, that he might become the father of many nations, according to what had been said to him: So shall your seed be. And not weak in faith, he did not consider his own body, now dead, since he was about a hundred years old, nor the dead womb of Sarah. Yet he did not waver through unbelief at the promises of God, but was strengthened in faith, giving glory to God, and being fully persuaded that what he had promised he was also able to do" (Rom. 4:18–21).

units.la: Huius Patris nostri vestigijs ipsi quoq; insistentes, faciamus officium, & fide vincamus omnia impedimenta & scandala, quæ nobis Satan & mundus obijciunt.
units.tr: Let us also, following the footsteps of this father of ours, do our duty, and by faith overcome all the hindrances and stumbling-blocks which Satan and the world put before us.

units.la: Repetamus etiam sępenumero piam sententiam elegantissimorum versuum Stigelij, nobilis poetæ:
units.tr: Let us also often repeat the pious sentiment of the most elegant verses of Stigel, a noble poet:

units.la: Non ego dura pati discrimina mille recuso, Dum tua constanti tueor mandata labore: Sed ne deficiam, ne sævo vincar ab hoste, Tu mihi præsto veni, tu suffice robora fessos.
units.tr: I do not refuse to bear a thousand hard trials, while with steadfast labour I keep your commands; but lest I fail, lest I be conquered by the cruel enemy, be present to me, and give strength to the weary.

units.la: VERSVS IIII,
units.tr: VERSE 4,

units.la: Et cœpit Ionah intrare civitatem itinere diei unius, & clamavit, dixitq; Adhuc quadraginta dies sunt, & Ninive subvertetur.
units.tr: And Jonah began to enter the city a day's journey, and he cried and said, Yet forty days, and Nineveh shall be overthrown.

units.la: Cum primum Propheta urbem diei unius itinere ingressus esset, voce clarissi-ma ad resipiscentiam Ninivitas hortatus est:addita comminatione,futurum,ut,ni si pœnitentiam agerent,post quadragesimum diem Niniueh cū suis incolis sub-uerteretur,uel eluuione,uel igne cœlitùs in eam, ut olim in Sodomam, depluen-te,uel terræmotu aut hiatu, uel deniq; a-lio aliquo modo.
units.tr: As soon as the prophet had entered the city, a day's journey in, he urged the Ninevites to repentance with a very clear voice, adding a threat: unless they repented, Nineveh with its inhabitants would be overthrown after the fortieth day, either by a flood, or by fire rained down from heaven upon it as once upon Sodom, or by an earthquake or a chasm, or finally by some other means.

units.la: Diligenter autem obseruanda nobis est συνᾳδολογ[?], ut ex cōminatione uelut parte,totum,uidelicet concionem de pœnitentia,recte colligamus. Qui enim non re[?] sipiscentibus exitium comminatur,idem ad Deum conuersis ueniam & malorum mitigationem pollicetur. Neq; consentaneum est, Ionam minis tantum egisse ad terrendos Niniuitas, cum pœnitentiæ præco esset. Sed præstat in iuniorum gratiam syllogismo rem compleĉti[?] in hunc modum.
units.tr: We must carefully observe the agreement [συνῳδία] of the parts, so that from the threat, as from one part, we rightly infer the whole, namely the sermon on repentance. For whoever threatens destruction to those who do not repent also promises pardon and the softening of evils to those who turn to God. Nor is it consistent to suppose that Jonah acted only by threats to terrify the Ninevites, since he was a herald of repentance. But it is better, for the sake of the younger readers, to set out the matter in syllogistic form in this way.

units.la: Pœnitentiæ concio quatuor partibus constat. Primò, τῷ ἐλέγχῳ[?], quo peccato-rum rei conuincuntur, & peccata eis an-nunciantur: Isa.58. ac illustre eius exem-plum habetur Rom.1.2. & 3.cap. in quibus Iudæi & Gentes rei peraguntur iniustitiæ & impietatis. Secundò, τῇ παρανομί[?]-ea, quæ & agenda & omittenda præscribit, & addit exhortationes efficaces ad studium boni & odiū mali. Isa.1.16. Lauate uos, mūdi estote, remouete malum operum uestrorum a conspectu oculorū meorum: definite malefacere, 17.discite benefacere, quærite iudicium, dirigite oppressum, iudicate pupillo, iudicate viduæ. Tertiò, promissione veniæ & mitigationis malorum. Isa.59.1. Ecce nō est abbreuiata manus Iehouæ, ut saluare nō possit: nec aggrauata est auris eius, ut nō exaudiat. Ier.4.1, Si reuersus fueris Israel, dixit Iehouah, ad me, & si abstuleris abominationes tuas a facie mea, non demigrabis. Postremò, feria comminatione. Luc.13,3.& 5. Nisi resipiscatis, omnes itidem peribitis.
units.tr: A sermon on repentance consists of four parts. First, by refutation [ἐλέγχῳ], by which men are convicted of the guilt of their sins and their sins are declared to them: Isaiah 58, and a notable example of this is in Romans 1, 2 and 3, where Jews and Gentiles are proved guilty of unrighteousness and impiety. Second, by exhortation [παραινέσει], which prescribes both what is to be done and what is to be left undone, and adds effective exhortations to the pursuit of good and the hatred of evil: Isaiah 1:16–17, Wash yourselves, make yourselves clean, put away the evil of your doings from before my eyes; cease to do evil, learn to do well, seek judgment, relieve the oppressed, judge the fatherless, plead for the widow. Third, by the promise of pardon and the softening of evils: Isaiah 59:1, Behold, the hand of the LORD is not shortened, that it cannot save; neither is his ear heavy, that it cannot hear. Jeremiah 4:1, If you return, Israel, says the LORD, to me, and if you take away your abominations out of my sight, you shall not wander. Last, by threat, which is a terror: Luke 13:3 and 5, Unless you repent, you will all likewise perish.

units.la: Fuit autem Ionas poenitentiæ totius præco fidelis, ut ex historia de prædicatione & eius fructu liquet. Resipuerunt enim Niniuitæ ad præconium Ionæ.Lu-cæ 11.32.
units.tr: Jonah was, moreover, a faithful herald of the whole of repentance, as is clear from the history, from his preaching and its fruit. For the Ninevites repented at the proclamation of Jonah: Luke 11:32.

units.la: Itaq; non est existimandum, minis solummodò egisse, & mutilo poenitentiæ præconio contentum fuisse: sed potius summa fide illa quatuor ἀφορμὰς[?] seu capita tradidisse & ursisse.
units.tr: Therefore it is not to be thought that he acted only by threats, and was content with a truncated proclamation of repentance; rather, with the greatest faithfulness, he delivered and set forth those four heads or chapters.

units.la: Sed unde colligis exceptionem de conuersione?
units.tr: But from where do you infer an exception concerning conversion?

units.la: 1. Ex euentu. Resipiscentibus enim Ni-niuitis ignouit & pepercit Deus.
units.tr: 1. From the outcome. For God spared and pardoned the Ninevites because they repented.

units.la: 2. Ex doctrinae de resipiscentia partibus, de quibus iam dictum est.
units.tr: 2. From the nature of the doctrine of repentance, the parts of which have already been mentioned.

units.la: 3. Ex Prophetae τῇ συμπαθείᾳ[?] erga eos, quos summe periclitari uidebat, nisi refi-piscerent. Etsi autem postea doluit Ionae, cum Deum parcere Niniuitis animaduerteret: non tamen ut ἐπιχαιρέκακος[?] & ambitiosus, sed ut in tetationis[?] (in qua Dei ve-ritas non minus, quam prophetae auĉo-ritas[?], periclitari uidebatur) paroxysmo aestuans introducitur & reprehenditur.
units.tr: 3. From the sympathy of the prophet towards those whom he saw to be in the greatest danger unless they repented. Although afterwards Jonah grieved, when he perceived that God was sparing the Ninevites, yet he is not presented and rebuked as a man of malicious joy and ambition, but as one seething in the paroxysm of temptation, in which the truth of God seemed to be endangered no less than the authority of the prophet.

units.la: 4. Ex Dei ingenio. Non tam enim denunciatione iræ suae erga hominum ge-nus, quā gratiae suae praeconio[?] delectatur.
units.tr: 4. From the character of God. For he delights less in the proclamation of his anger against the human race than in the proclamation of his grace.

units.la: 5. Ex absurdis quae alioqui sequuntur. 1. Pereundum uidelicet Niniuitis fuisse, siue resipiscerent, siue non resipiscerent. 2. Frustra quibusdā[?] refipiscentiae donū a Deo dari, 3. Deū quod ἁπλῶς[?] denun-ciauerat et comminatus fuerat Niniuitis, nō exequendo, uanitatis labem sibi aspersisse[?]. 4. Nihil interesse inter minas sine conditione denunciatas, & inter eas quae cum hypothesi quadam denunciatae sunt.
units.tr: 5. From the absurdities which otherwise follow. (1) That the Ninevites must have perished, whether they repented or not. (2) That the gift of repentance is given by God to no purpose. (3) That God, having unconditionally declared and threatened the Ninevites, by not carrying it out, stained himself with a blemish of vanity. (4) That there is no difference between threats declared without condition and those declared with some stipulation.

units.la: Etsi autem de numeris non soleo philosophari, nisi cum res postulat: tamen ea quae adnotauit diuus Hieronymus ad hūc lo-cum, ipsius uerbis exponam. Porro, inquit ille, numerus quadragenarius conuenit peccatoribus, & ieiunio, & orationi, & sacco, & lacrymis, & perseuerantiae deprecandi: ob quod & Moyses ieiunauit quadraginta diebus in monte Sina: & Helias fugiens Iezabel, & Dei desuper ira pendente, quadraginta dies ieiunasse describitur. Ipse quoque Dominus uerus Iona, missus ad praedicationem mūdi, ieiunauit quadraginta dies: & haereditate nobis ieiunij derelinquens, ad eum[?] corporis sui sub hoc numero nostras animas praeparat.
units.tr: Although I am not accustomed to philosophise about numbers unless the matter requires it, I will nevertheless set out, in his own words, what the blessed Jerome noted on this passage. Further, he says, the number forty belongs to sinners, to fasting, to prayer, to sackcloth, to tears, and to perseverance in entreaty; for which reason Moses fasted forty days on Mount Sinai, and Elijah, fleeing from Jezebel while God's anger hung over him from above, is described as having fasted forty days. The Lord himself, the true Jonah, sent to preach to the world, also fasted forty days, and in leaving us the inheritance of fasting, he prepares our souls under this number for his own body.

units.la: THESIS,
units.tr: THESIS,

units.la: Nec labori, nec tempori seruis Dei parcendum est, cum denunciata seu in genere, seu in specie Dei ira, & horribilibus poenis, ad resipiscentiam uocādi sunt ho-mines.
units.tr: The servants of God must spare neither labour nor time when, whether in general or in particular, God's anger and horrible punishments have been declared and men are to be called to repentance.

units.la: Testimonia duo.
units.tr: Two testimonies.

units.la: Ezech.33.7. Fili hominis, speculatorem dedi te domui Israel, & audies de ore meo uerbū, & p̄monebis eos ex me, &c,
units.tr: Ezekiel 33:7, Son of man, I have made you a watchman to the house of Israel; and you shall hear the word from my mouth, and warn them from me, etc.

units.la: 2.Tim.4.2.Prædica sermone, insta tempestiuè, intempestiuè: argue, obiurga, exhortare cum omni lenitate & doctrina.
units.tr: 2 Timothy 4:2, Preach the word; be urgent in season and out of season; reprove, rebuke, exhort with all patience and teaching.

units.la: Exemplum Pauli Apostoli.
units.tr: Example of the Apostle Paul.

units.la: Act.20.18. Vos Presbyteri Ecclesiæ Ephesinæ scitis, à primo die quo ingressus sum Asiam, quomodo uobiscum per omne tempus fuerim: 19.Seruiens Domino cum omnia modestia, & multis lacrymis ac tentationibus, quæ mihi euenerunt in Iudæorum insidijs: 20.Vt nihil subterfugerim eorum quæ uobis conduceret, quo minus ea uobis annunciarem, & docerem uos publicè & per singulas domos: 21.Testificans Iudæis simul & Grȩcis conuersionem ad Deum, & fidem in Dominum nostrum Iesum.
units.tr: Acts 20:18-21: "You yourselves know, elders of the church of Ephesus, from the first day that I came into Asia, how I have been with you at all times, serving the Lord with all humility and with many tears and trials, which befell me through the plots of the Jews; how I kept back nothing that was profitable for you, but declared it to you and taught you publicly and from house to house, testifying both to Jews and to Greeks repentance toward God and faith in our Lord Jesus."

units.la: Idem, quomodo munere Apostolico apud Corinthios sit perfunctus, his uerbis ostendit, dicens: Ego cum ad uos uenirem, fratres, non ueni cum eminentia facundiæ aut sapientiæ, annuncians uobis testimonium Dei. Non enim decreueram quicquam scire inter uos, nisi Iesum Christum, eumq; crucifixum. Et fui ego cum infirmitate & timore ac tremore multo apud uos,&c. 1.Cor.2.1.23.
units.tr: The same apostle shows how he discharged his apostolic office among the Corinthians, in these words: "When I came to you, brothers, I did not come with excellence of speech or of wisdom, proclaiming to you the testimony of God. For I had resolved to know nothing among you except Jesus Christ, and him crucified. And I was with you in weakness, and in fear and much trembling," and so on. 1 Cor. 2:1-3.

units.la: VERSVS V.
units.tr: Verse 5

units.la: Crediderunt autem uiri Ninive Deo, & praedicauerunt ieiunium, induerunt sefaccis, a maiore ipsorum usq; ad minore.
units.tr: And the men of Nineveh believed God, and proclaimed a fast, and put on sackcloth, from the greatest of them even to the least.

units.la: Summam hypothesis Christus Dominus noster sic est complexus: Νινευῖται μετενόησαν εἰς τὸ κήρυγμα Ἰωνᾶ: Nineuitae resipuerunt ad praedicationem Ionae. Matt.12.41.
units.tr: Christ our Lord summed up the whole matter in this way: The Ninevites repented at the preaching of Jonah [Νινευῖται μετενόησαν εἰς τὸ κήρυγμα Ἰωνᾶ]. Matt. 12:41.

units.la: Duo autem Niniuitis tribuuntur. Alterum est, quòd crediderint Deo: alterum, quòd praedicauerint ieiunium publicu.
units.tr: Two things are attributed to the Ninevites: first, that they believed God; second, that they proclaimed a public fast.
